docs.title: MineFunkin Docs
docs.text:
MineFunkin is a Friday Night Funkin' engine for Minecraft. At a Speaker you fight another player or the Dummy, right in the world, with everybody around watching. At the Retro TV you practise songs and make your own charts.

This wiki is about everything around the notes: the camera swinging round on the drop, the lanes going upside down, your opponent turning into a giant, the whole game window shaking on a miss. You can build all of that yourself with small text files next to your song. You don't need to know Java or any other programming language for it.

Pick where you want to go:

  • Event scripts

    Learn to script your songs: flashes, zooms, modcharts, the fight camera, both fighters, stages, effects and shaders - even the game window. Small text files, no Java needed.

    Start here · Your first event

  • Event API

    Look things up: every callback, action, shortcut and function, and one page per property group - each with its kind, default, range and an example.

    The API · Frequently used

  • Songs

    What's in a song folder, where it goes, how to import one, and the .mfknsong and .mfkn files.

    Songs

  • Addon API

    For other mods (Java): song results, fights, practice and every note of the local player's runs. Opt-in, on the server and the client.

    Addon API 1.1 · Set up your mod

docs.text: You want to ... Go here make your very first event Your first event - ten minutes, step by step find out what some name does the Event API, or just type it into the search up top make the lanes and notes dance Modcharts put a stage behind the fighters Stages and sprites bring over a song from Psych or Kade Coming from Psych · Coming from Kade get your song files in order Songs understand an error message Errors and fixes hook your own Java mod into MineFunkin the Addon API know what you may share and how the License

docs.title: A little taste
docs.text:
Here's a whole event. Drop it into a song's folder as pop_flash.event, and the chart editor gets a new event called Pop Flash - with a slider and a colour picker, built from the two lines under params:

format 1.1

event {
    name = "Pop Flash",
    color = #FF6EC7,
    category = "Party",
}

params {
    strength = number { from = "value1", default = 0.05, min = 0, max = 0.3, label = "Zoom pop" },
    tint     = color  { from = "value2", default = #FFFFFF, label = "Flash colour" },
}

function onEvent(p)
    camera.bump += p.strength      -- the camera pops
    flash(p.tint, beats(0.5))      -- a flash in your colour, gone after half a beat
end

Place it on a big drum hit and press Space. That's really all it takes.

docs.title: Addon API 1.1
docs.text:
Making a mod and want it to know when someone just cleared a song? The Addon API lets other mods react to what happens in MineFunkin: a song was played to the end, a fight between two players is over, a player hit a note. A progression mod could hand out XP for a cleared song, a server mod could forbid fights in the Nether, a HUD mod could show your combo, a stats mod could count your "Sick!"s.

This part is for mod developers (Java). If you want to change what happens inside a song - flashes, lanes, the camera - you're looking for event scripts, no Java needed.

docs.title: What you can build
docs.text:
Idea Side With XP, money or items for a cleared song server onSongCompleted An achievement for the first "Perfect" on a song server onRankImproved No fights in the Nether, at spawn, during a minigame server allowFight A prize for the winner of a fight server onFightEnded A chat message when two players start a fight server onFightStarted A list of the best players on a song server songs().leaderboard A sound or a particle on every "Sick!" client onNoteJudged Your own combo or accuracy display client currentRun() "Playing Bopeebo (Hard)" in a status or presence mod client onSongStarted

Complete code for these is on Recipes.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. Your mod asks for the API. One line in your mod's metadata file and one small class (see Set up your mod).
  2. MineFunkin hands your class a handle while the game starts: an object called api that belongs to your mod.
  3. You tell the handle what you want to hear about: api.events().onSongCompleted(...). From then on MineFunkin calls your code every time that happens.

The API is opt-in: if no installed mod asks for it, it stays completely off - no events fire, nothing is recorded for it, it costs the game nothing. And your mod doesn't need MineFunkin either: without it, your addon class is simply never loaded, and the rest of your mod works as usual.

It's the same API on both builds of MineFunkin - Fabric 1.21.11 and NeoForge 1.21.1: the same types, the same events, the same queries. Only the way your mod asks for it differs.

docs.title: Server side or client side?
docs.text:
Server side Client side Runs on the server (in singleplayer: the built-in one) each player's own game Knows about results that count, fights between players, who practices, the leaderboard the local player's own runs, live and note by note - practice included Can it be trusted? yes - results say whether the server checked them no - it's the player's own game Use it for rewards, rules, ranks, announcements HUDs, sounds, statistics, presence

A mod can use both: one class for each side.

docs.title: Words used here
docs.text: Word Meaning handle The api object your class gets. Everything goes through it. listener A piece of your code that MineFunkin calls when something happens (a Java lambda). event The something: a song completed, a note judged, a fight ended. run One play of a song, from the end of the countdown to its end. A restart is a new run. chart, song key One song + character + difficulty, played on one side. SongRef.key() is the text MineFunkin stores scores, leaderboards and replays under (each side its own) - use it for your own per-chart data too. practice, dummy fight, player fight The three ways to play: at the Retro TV (counts for nothing), at a Speaker against the dummy, at a Speaker against another player. verified The server checked the numbers itself (see Can I trust a result?). server thread, render thread Where your listener runs: the game's main threads. Keep listeners quick.

docs.text: Set up your mod step by step: compile against MineFunkin, ask for the API, see it work Recipes complete, small addons to copy Server side, Client side every event and query Types every record and enum, field by field Versions and loaders detecting the version, what changed since 1.0, Fabric and NeoForge

docs.title: Client side
docs.text:
The client side knows the local player's own runs, live and note by note - practice at the Retro TV included, which never reaches a server. Your class implements MineFunkinClientAddon and gets a MineFunkinClientApi handle (see Set up your mod):

public final class MyMineFunkinClientAddon implements MineFunkinClientAddon {
    @Override
    public void onMineFunkinClientApi(MineFunkinClientApi api) {
        api.events().onNoteJudged((session, note) -> {
            if (note.judgment() == Judgment.SICK) {
                Minecraft.getInstance().getSoundManager().play(SimpleSoundInstance.forUI(SoundEvents.NOTE_BLOCK_BELL, 2.0f));
            }
        });

        api.events().onSongEnded((session, end) -> {
            // session.mode(): PRACTICE, DUMMY_FIGHT or PLAYER_FIGHT
            // end.outcome(): COMPLETED, FAILED or ABORTED
        });
    }
}

Everything runs on the render thread. The client is the player's own game: fine for HUDs, sounds and statistics, not for rewards - for those, use the server side, which can check results.

docs.title: A run
docs.text:
A run is one play of a song: it starts when the countdown ends (onSongStarted) and ends exactly once (onSongEnded). Every event in between carries the same SongSession:

SongSession runId() counts up per run in this game session - tells two runs of the same song apart mode() PRACTICE (at a Retro TV), DUMMY_FIGHT or PLAYER_FIGHT song() the chart: song, character, difficulty, and its key() chart() the played side of the chart: notes, holds, length, tempo opponent() the other player in a player fight, null otherwise

A restart is a new run (the old one ends as ABORTED). Replays are never reported - watching a run isn't playing one.

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
Event When Your listener gets onSongStarted The countdown ended the session onNoteJudged Every judged note - hits and misses, including a press with nothing to hit the session, a NoteJudgment: lane, judgment, songTimeMs, offsetMs, combo, ghostTap onHoldNote A hold note was hit, held to its end, or let go too early the session, a HoldNote: lane, phase (STARTED / COMPLETED / DROPPED), lengthMs, songTimeMs onBeat Every beat of the song, from 0 the session, the beat number, the tempo there (charts can change tempo) onChartEvent The song reaches a chart event ("Hey!", "Add Camera Zoom", your own .events ...) the session, a ChartCue: name, value1, value2, timeMs onPauseChanged Paused or resumed (in a fight: once both fighters agreed) the session, boolean onSongEnded The run ended - see below the session, a SongEnd

Lanes are numbered 0 left, 1 down, 2 up, 3 right. offsetMs is negative for an early press, positive for a late one, and NaN when there was no timed press (a note that scrolled past, a dropped hold).

docs.title: How a run ends
docs.text:
SongEnd.Outcome COMPLETED Played to the end without failing. FAILED The health ran out (fights only - practice can't fail). ABORTED Left before the end: quit, restarted, gave up, or the fight ended early because the opponent gave up or left.

SongEnd also has the score, accuracyPercent, the rank (FAILED for a failed run, null for an aborted one - it isn't a result), the hits per judgment and the song file's audioLengthMs.

docs.title: Queries
Recipes
docs.text: Small, complete addons to copy - each one is a few lines and does one useful thing. Paste it into your addon class's onMineFunkinApi (server) or onMineFunkinClientApi (client); Set up your mod shows the class around it.

docs.title: XP for a cleared song
docs.text:
api.events().onSongCompleted((player, result) -> {
    if (!result.verified()) {
        return; // only results the server checked
    }
    HitStats hits = result.hits();
    player.giveExperiencePoints(hits.sick() * 2 + hits.good());
});

docs.title: A diamond for the first "Perfect" on a chart
docs.text:
api.events().onRankImproved((player, result, previousBest) -> {
    boolean perfect = result.rank() == Rank.PERFECT || result.rank() == Rank.PERFECT_GOLD;
    if (perfect && result.verified()) {
        player.addItem(new ItemStack(Items.DIAMOND));
        player.sendSystemMessage(Component.literal("Perfect on " + result.song().songId() + "!"));
    }
});

onRankImproved fires only when the rank beats every earlier one of this player on this chart, so the diamond comes once per chart.

docs.title: No fights in the Nether
docs.text:
api.events().allowFight((challenger, challenged, song) -> {
    if (challenger.level().dimension() == Level.NETHER || challenged.level().dimension() == Level.NETHER) {
        return Component.literal("No fights in the Nether.");
    }
    return null; // allowed
});

docs.title: A prize for the winner
docs.text:
api.events().onFightEnded((server, end) -> {
    if (end.reason() != FightEnd.Reason.COMPLETED || end.isDraw()) {
        return;
    }
    ServerPlayer winner = server.getPlayerList().getPlayer(end.winner().id());
    if (winner != null) { // they may have left already
        winner.addItem(new ItemStack(Items.MUSIC_DISC_CAT));
    }
    server.getPlayerList().broadcastSystemMessage(
            Component.literal(end.winner().name() + " won on " + end.fight().song().songId() + "!"), false);
});

docs.title: Announce fights in the chat
docs.text:
api.events().onFightStarted((challenger, challenged, fight) ->
        challenger.level().getServer().getPlayerList().broadcastSystemMessage(Component.literal(
                challenger.getName().getString() + " vs " + challenged.getName().getString()
                        + " on " + fight.song().songId() + " - fight!"), false));

docs.title: Log suspicious results
docs.text:
api.events().onResultRejected((server, claimed) ->
        LOGGER.warn("{} claimed {} points on {}, but the replay disagrees",
                claimed.player().name(), claimed.score(), claimed.song().key()));

docs.title: A sound on every "Sick!"
docs.text:
api.events().onNoteJudged((session, note) -> {
    if (note.judgment() == Judgment.SICK) {
        Minecraft.getInstance().getSoundManager().play(SimpleSoundInstance.forUI(SoundEvents.NOTE_BLOCK_BELL, 2.0f));
    }
});

docs.title: Practice time
docs.text:
private long startedAt;
private long practiceMs;

// in onMineFunkinClientApi:
api.events().onSongStarted(session -> startedAt = System.currentTimeMillis());
api.events().onSongEnded((session, end) -> {
    if (session.mode() == PlayMode.PRACTICE) {
        practiceMs += System.currentTimeMillis() - startedAt;
    }
});

docs.title: Accuracy per lane
docs.text:
private final int[] hits = new int[4];
private final int[] notes = new int[4];

// in onMineFunkinClientApi:
api.events().onNoteJudged((session, note) -> {
    if (note.ghostTap()) {
        return; // a press with nothing to hit isn't a note
    }
    notes[note.lane()]++;
    if (!note.isMiss()) {
        hits[note.lane()]++;
    }
});

docs.title: What's playing (for a status or presence mod)
docs.text:
api.events().onSongStarted(session -> {
    SongRef song = session.song();
    String status = "Playing " + song.songId() + " (" + song.difficultyLabel() + ")"
            + (session.mode() == PlayMode.PLAYER_FIGHT ? " vs " + session.opponent().name() : "");
    myPresence.set(status);
});
api.events().onSongEnded((session, end) -> myPresence.clear());

docs.title: Server side
docs.text:
The server side knows the results that count, the fights between players, who is practicing, and the server's songs and leaderboard. Your class implements MineFunkinAddon and gets a MineFunkinApi handle (see Set up your mod):

public final class MyMineFunkinAddon implements MineFunkinAddon {
    @Override
    public void onMineFunkinApi(MineFunkinApi api) {
        api.events().onSongCompleted((player, result) -> {
            if (!result.verified()) {
                return; // the client's own word - no rewards for that
            }
            player.giveExperiencePoints(result.hits().sick() * 2 + result.hits().good());
        });

        api.events().allowFight((challenger, challenged, song) ->
                challenger.level().dimension() == Level.NETHER ? Component.literal("No fights in the Nether.") : null);
    }
}

The handle has four parts: api.events() (listen), api.fights(), api.players() and api.songs() (ask). Everything runs on the server thread - in singleplayer that's the built-in server.

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
Event When Your listener gets onSongCompleted A song was played to its end without failing - a dummy fight (when the player's game reports it) or a player fight (once the server scored both runs, a moment after the fight ended) the ServerPlayer, the SongResult onRankImproved Right after onSongCompleted, when a CHECKED run's rank beats every earlier rank of this player on this chart the ServerPlayer, the SongResult, the previous best Rank (null the first time) onResultRejected A dummy-fight result that its own replay proved wrong. No onSongCompleted fires for it - for anti-cheat logs the MinecraftServer, the claimed SongResult allowFight A fight between two players is about to happen - see Fights challenger, challenged, the SongRef onFightStarted Both fighters stand in place. The song starts a second or two later, once both games are ready challenger, challenged, the FightInfo onFightEnded Every fight that started, exactly once, however it ended the MinecraftServer, the FightEnd onPracticeChanged A player opened (true) or left (false) practice at a Retro TV, as their game reports it. Also false when they disconnect the ServerPlayer, boolean

Events about a player who is online right now give you their ServerPlayer. Events that can come after a player left (a fight that ended by a disconnect, a result proven fake) give you the server and PlayerRefs (UUID + name) instead.

Never fired for practice runs (practice stays on the player's game by design - use the client side), for failed runs, for fights that ended early (giving up, a disconnect, a timeout), and for replays.

docs.title: What fires when
docs.text:
Dummy fightPlayer fightPractice
  1. The player plays a song at a Speaker against the dummy.
  2. Their game reports the result (and, with online play, uploads the replay).
  3. A few seconds later, once the replay is checked: onSongCompleted (+ onRankImproved on a new best rank) - or onResultRejected if the replay disproves it.
  1. A opens a Speaker for a fight against a player and waits on one pad; B steps onto the free pad: allowFight (A is the challenger, B the challenged).
  2. Both stand on their pads: onFightStarted.
  3. The song ends, someone gives up or leaves: onFightEnded (always, exactly once).
  4. If it was played to its end: the server scores both runs itself, then onSongCompleted (+ onRankImproved) for each fighter who finished without failing.

onPracticeChanged(player, true) when they open a Retro TV's menus or songs, onPracticeChanged(player, false) when they leave or disconnect. Nothing else - practice results never reach the server.

docs.title: Can I trust a result?
docs.text:
result.validation() says who vouches for the numbers. It's final when the event fires.

Validation SERVER_SCORED A player fight. The server replayed both fighters' key presses on its own copy of the chart - every number is the server's. REPLAY_VERIFIED A dummy fight whose uploaded replay replayed to exactly the reported result. UNVERIFIED The player's game's own report, unchecked: online play or replay validation is off on this server, the player's game sent no replay, or the server doesn't host the song so it can't check it.

result.verified() is true for the first two. Check it before you hand out anything valuable - an unverified result is only as honest as the player's game.

By default your mod never even sees an unverified result: onSongCompleted gets only checked ones. A server admin can let unverified results through as well (apiUnverifiedResults: true in server.json) - for mods that look at validation() themselves. onRankImproved and the stored ranks always count checked results only.

docs.title: Fights
docs.text:
allowFight is a veto. It's asked when the second player steps onto a Speaker's free pad - the challenger is the player who opened the Speaker and waited, the challenged the one who stepped on. Return null to allow the fight, or a Component with the reason to refuse it - both players see the reason (above the hotbar, while the second player stays on the pad). If several mods have rules, the first one that refuses wins.

api.events().allowFight((challenger, challenged, song) -> {
    if (challenger.isCreative() || challenged.isCreative()) {
        return Component.literal("No fights in creative mode.");
    }
    return null;
});

onFightEnded gets a FightEnd: the fight, why it ended, the winner (null for a draw) and each fighter's score so far.

FightEnd.Reason COMPLETED The song was played to its end (or ran out of time after one side finished). FORFEIT A fighter gave up or left the fight screen - the other one wins. DISCONNECT A fighter disconnected - the other one wins. NOT_STARTED The song never started: a player's game wasn't ready in time. No winner. CANCELLED A mod ended it with api.fights().cancel(...). No winner.

docs.title: Queries
docs.text:
Call Gives api.fights().isFighting(uuid) whether that player is in a fight right now api.fights().fightOf(uuid) their fight (Optional<FightInfo>) api.fights().running() every running fight api.fights().cancel(fightId) ends a fight at once: no winner, nothing recorded, both fighters go back to where they stood (CANCELLED). false if no such fight runs api.players().isPracticing(uuid) whether that player is practicing at a Retro TV api.players().isProtected(player) MineFunkin's protection: fighters and practicing players take no damage, aren't targeted by mobs and aren't pushed api.players().bestRank(uuid, songKey) the best rank that player reached on that chart (since the API went online) api.songs().serverSongIds() the server's songs (folder names) - it reads the folder, so not every tick api.songs().charts(songId) every playable chart of a song (character + difficulty), as SongRefs api.songs().chart(songId, character, difficulty) one chart's SongRef, with its key() api.songs().onlinePlay() whether the server runs its online features (leaderboard, replays) api.songs().leaderboard(songKey, limit) the top of a chart's leaderboard, best first, as LeaderboardEntrys - empty without online play

Every field of every type: Types.

docs.title: Set up your mod
docs.text: Four steps, from an empty mod to a line in your log every time someone clears a song. It takes about as long as making a coffee. The examples are for a server-side addon; a client-side one works the same way with the client interface (shown in the tabs).

docs.title: 1. Compile against MineFunkin
docs.text:
Your mod needs MineFunkin's classes to compile, but it shouldn't ship them or require them. Put MineFunkin's jar into a libs/ folder in your project and add it as a compile-only dependency:

Fabric (Loom)NeoForge (ModDevGradle) 
dependencies {
    modCompileOnly files("libs/minefunkin-0.3.0.jar")
}

dependencies {
    compileOnly files("libs/minefunkin-0.3.0.jar")   // the jar of MineFunkin's NeoForge build
}

To try your mod together with MineFunkin, drop the same jar into your development run's mods folder (run/mods).

docs.title: 2. Write the addon class
docs.text:
One class per side. MineFunkin creates it once while the game starts and hands it the handle:

Server sideClient side 
package com.example.mymod;

import com.notfoxxz.minefunkin.api.MineFunkinAddon;
import com.notfoxxz.minefunkin.api.MineFunkinApi;
import org.slf4j.Logger;
import org.slf4j.LoggerFactory;

public final class MyMineFunkinAddon implements MineFunkinAddon {
    private static final Logger LOGGER = LoggerFactory.getLogger("mymod");

    @Override
    public void onMineFunkinApi(MineFunkinApi api) {
        api.events().onSongCompleted((player, result) ->
                LOGGER.info("{} cleared {} with {} points", player.getName().getString(),
                        result.song().songId(), result.score()));
    }
}

package com.example.mymod.client;

import com.notfoxxz.minefunkin.api.client.MineFunkinClientAddon;
import com.notfoxxz.minefunkin.api.client.MineFunkinClientApi;
import org.slf4j.Logger;
import org.slf4j.LoggerFactory;

public final class MyMineFunkinClientAddon implements MineFunkinClientAddon {
    private static final Logger LOGGER = LoggerFactory.getLogger("mymod");

    @Override
    public void onMineFunkinClientApi(MineFunkinClientApi api) {
        api.events().onSongEnded((session, end) ->
                LOGGER.info("Run {} of {} ended: {}", session.runId(), session.song().songId(), end.outcome()));
    }
}

The client class only ever runs on the client - keep it with your other client-only code.

Keep MineFunkin's classes inside your addon classes

Your addon classes are only loaded when MineFunkin is installed. Use MineFunkin's types only in them (or in classes only they use) - a MineFunkin type in your main mod class would crash your mod for players without MineFunkin.

docs.title: 3. Ask for the API
4. See it work
docs.text:
Start the game and look in logs/latest.log:

[Render thread/INFO] (MineFunkin/API) MineFunkin API 1.1 (client): online for [mymod]
[Render thread/INFO] (MineFunkin/API) MineFunkin API 1.1 (server): online for [mymod]

One line per side; a mod with only a server-side class gets online on the (server) line only. A dedicated server writes the (server) line.

If it says offline - no mod asked for it, MineFunkin didn't find your request: check the entrypoint names (Fabric) or the annotation and the modproperties block (NeoForge), and the version string.

Now play a song at a Speaker against the dummy (right-click it, "Gegen den Dummy") until the end: your line shows up in the log.

docs.title: Rules for listeners
docs.text:
• Keep them quick. Server listeners run on the server thread, client listeners on the render thread
  • the game waits for them. Don't read files or wait for the network inside one; hand slow work to your own thread.
  • A listener that throws is logged under your mod id and skipped. It never breaks MineFunkin or another mod's listener.
  • Register any time. Most mods register everything in onMineFunkinApi, but you can keep the handle and register later.
  • Check result.verified() before handing out anything valuable on the server - see Can I trust a result?.

Next: Recipes for complete small addons, or Server side / Client side for everything the API offers.

docs.title: Types
docs.text: Everything the events hand you and the queries give back. They are Java records (read a field with result.score(), result.hits().sick()) and enums. Server-side types are in com.notfoxxz.minefunkin.api, client-side ones in com.notfoxxz.minefunkin.api.client; Rank and Judgment are in com.notfoxxz.minefunkin.game.

docs.title: PlayerRef
docs.text:
A player by UUID and name - in events that can come after the player left.

Field id() the player's UUID name() their name

docs.title: SongRef
docs.text:
One chart: song + character + difficulty, played on one side. Each side keeps its own bests - the player side and the opponent side have different keys.

Field key() the text MineFunkin stores everything per chart and side under (local bests, the leaderboard, replays, ranks) - use it for your own per-chart data too songId() the song's folder name characterLabel() the playable character, "" for a song without characters difficultyLabel() the difficulty, as the song list shows it

SongRef.of(songId, character, difficulty) makes the player side's, SongRef.of(songId, character, difficulty, true) the opponent side's. opponentSide() says which one you have. Results (SongResult.song(), onRankImproved) carry the side the run was played on.

docs.title: PlayMode
docs.text: Value PRACTICE at a Retro TV (or its editor): no health, no ranks, nothing saved or sent - client events only DUMMY_FIGHT at a Speaker against the dummy (or /minefunkin battle on a server without MineFunkin) PLAYER_FIGHT at a Speaker against another player (one waits on a pad, the other steps onto the free one)

docs.title: ChartInfo
docs.text:
The side of the chart that was played.

Field noteCount() notes to hit (a hold counts once; "never press" notes don't count) holdCount() how many of them are holds lengthMs() from the song's start to the end of its last note (the audio runs on a little longer) startBpm() the tempo at the start (charts can change it) scrollSpeed() the chart's own scroll speed

docs.title: HitStats
docs.text:
How a run's notes were judged.

Field sick(), good(), bad(), shit() hits per judgment miss() misses, including dropped holds and presses with nothing to hit maxCombo() the longest streak without a miss hits() every hit (all but misses) judged() hits + misses

docs.title: Rank
docs.text:
The end-of-song rank, from the run's accuracy:

Value PERFECT_GOLD every note a "Sick!" PERFECT 100 % accuracy EXCELLENT 90 % and up GREAT 80 % and up GOOD 60 % and up SHIT below 60 % FAILED the health ran out (client side only - a server result is never FAILED)

Better ranks come first: rank.ordinal() is smaller for a better rank. rank.label is the name the game shows.

docs.title: Judgment
docs.text: One note's judgment: SICK, GOOD, BAD, SHIT, MISS.

docs.title: SongResult
docs.text:
A song played to its end without failing, as the server knows it.

Field player() PlayerRef song() SongRef mode() DUMMY_FIGHT or PLAYER_FIGHT validation() who vouches for the numbers - see Can I trust a result? verified() shorthand: true unless UNVERIFIED score(), accuracyPercent() rank() Rank, never FAILED hits() HitStats (the server's own count for a player fight) chart() ChartInfo opponent() the other fighter in a player fight, null against the dummy

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: Value SERVER_SCORED a player fight - the server scored it itself REPLAY_VERIFIED a dummy fight whose replay confirmed it UNVERIFIED the player's game's own report, unchecked

docs.title: FightInfo
docs.text:
A fight between two players.

Field fightId() its number (for api.fights().cancel(...)) challenger(), challenged() PlayerRefs - who opened the Speaker and waited, who stepped onto the free pad song() SongRef challengerPlaysOpponentSide() whether the challenger plays the chart's opponent side involves(uuid) whether that player is one of the two opponentOf(uuid) the other one of the two

docs.title: FightEnd
docs.text:
How a fight ended.

Field fight() FightInfo reason() COMPLETED, FORFEIT, DISCONNECT, NOT_STARTED, CANCELLED - see Fights winner() PlayerRef, null for a draw (equal scores, both failed) isDraw() winner() == null challenger(), challenged() each side's FightEnd.Line

FightEnd.Line is one fighter's last known state - for a fight cut short, the score so far. For a COMPLETED fight the server has scored both runs itself (it replays their key presses on its own chart), and the lines and the winner come from that, not from what the games reported:

Field player() PlayerRef score(), accuracyPercent(), misses() finished() their game reported the end of their run (played to the end, or failed) failed() their health ran out

docs.title: LeaderboardEntry
docs.text:
One place on a chart's leaderboard.

Field position() 1 = best player() PlayerRef score(), accuracyPercent(), rank()

docs.title: SongSession
docs.text:
One run of a song by the local player.

Field runId() counts up per run in this game session mode() PlayMode song() SongRef chart() ChartInfo opponent() the other player in a player fight, null otherwise

docs.title: NoteJudgment
docs.text:
One judged note.

Field lane() 0 left, 1 down, 2 up, 3 right judgment() Judgment isMiss() judgment() == MISS songTimeMs() when it was judged offsetMs() how early (negative) or late (positive) the press was; NaN without a timed press combo() the combo after it (0 after a miss) ghostTap() a press with nothing to hit (always a miss)

docs.title: HoldNote
docs.text: Field lane() 0-3 phase() STARTED (its head was hit), COMPLETED (held to its end), DROPPED (let go too early - a miss) lengthMs() the hold's length songTimeMs() when this happened

docs.title: ChartCue
docs.text:
A chart event as the song reaches it.

Field name() the event's name ("Add Camera Zoom", your own .event's name, ...) value1(), value2() its two values, as written in the chart timeMs() its time in the chart

docs.title: SongEnd
docs.text:
How a run ended.

Field outcome() COMPLETED, FAILED or ABORTED - see How a run ends score(), accuracyPercent() rank() Rank: FAILED for a failed run, null for an aborted one hits() HitStats audioLengthMs() the song file's length, -1 if it never finished loading

docs.title: LiveRun
docs.text:
A run as of right now (api.currentRun()).

Field session() SongSession songTimeMs() the position in the song (negative in the short lead-in after the countdown) audioLengthMs() the song file's length, -1 while it's still loading score(), accuracyPercent(), combo() hits() HitStats so far notesLeft() notes not judged yet health() 0 to 1 (practice has health too, it just can't fail) paused()

docs.title: LocalBest
docs.text:
The local player's best on a chart, as saved on this computer (api.localBest(songKey)).

Field score(), accuracyPercent(), rank() achievedAtMillis() when (milliseconds since 1970, like System.currentTimeMillis())

docs.title: How versions work
docs.text:
The API has a version of two numbers, major.minor - now 1.1. A new minor version only adds things, so an addon written for 1.0 works with 1.1. A new major version may change or remove things.

Your mod names the version it was written against ("minefunkin:api": "1.1", see Set up your mod). MineFunkin serves it when the major number matches and the minor isn't higher than its own. Otherwise your mod gets no handle, and the log says why.

docs.title: Detecting the version
docs.text:
• Before loading any MineFunkin class: MineFunkin's own mod metadata carries the same key. It holds the string "1.1"; it's missing before 1.1.

    FabricNeoForge 
    FabricLoader.getInstance().getModContainer("minefunkin")
        .map(c -> c.getMetadata().getCustomValue("minefunkin:api"))

    ModList.get().getModContainerById("minefunkin")
        .map(c -> c.getModInfo().getModProperties().get("minefunkin:api"))

  • With the handle: api.version() returns "1.1" at runtime. Prefer it over the constant MineFunkinApi.VERSION, which the Java compiler copies into your class (it would still say what you compiled against).

  • The log states it on every start: MineFunkin API 1.1 (server): offline - no mod asked for it, or online for [yourmod] with the mods that asked.

docs.title: Changes from 1.0
docs.text:
1.0 was the static MineFunkinEvents (SONG_COMPLETED / SONG_RANK_ACHIEVED with SongCompletion). It is gone: anyone could register on it without asking, which kept the API always on. To move to 1.1:

  • declare the minefunkin entrypoint (Fabric) or @MineFunkinPlugin (NeoForge);
  • register through api.events().onSongCompleted and onRankImproved;
  • read SongResult, which carries everything SongCompletion had, plus mode, validation, hits, chart and opponent.

One behaviour change: a fight that ended early (giving up, a disconnect) no longer reports a completed song.

docs.title: Loaders
docs.text:
Build How a mod asks Where the version is Fabric 1.21.11 the minefunkin / minefunkin-client entrypoints "minefunkin:api" under custom in fabric.mod.json NeoForge 1.21.1 @MineFunkinPlugin on the class, found in NeoForge's mod scan data "minefunkin:api" under [modproperties.<modid>] in neoforge.mods.toml

Only one class inside MineFunkin (api.internal.ApiHost) knows the loader: it finds the mods that ask for the API and reads the version they want. Everything else - the types, the events, the queries - is plain Java and Minecraft and the same on every build. A port to another loader swaps that one class for its loader's way of finding addons.

docs.title: Event API
docs.text:
Every single name a .event script can use, all in one place. This is the part of the wiki you look things up in - you don't have to read it front to back. The search up top is your friend here.

The sidebar has it in three parts: the basics (the most used names, the language, the fixed words), the calls (what the game calls, and what your script can call), and one page per property group.

How many What they are 18 callbacks the functions the game calls: onBeat, onHit, onFrame, ... 20 actions statements that do something: tween, after, every, playSound, reset, ... 43 shortcuts one call for a common effect: flash, zoom, flipScroll, setPose, ease, ... 46 functions give a value back: sin, lerp, hsv, beats, sub, mod, ... 5 built-in values time, beat, step, bpm, pi 246 properties on 20 pages the values the game reads every frame: camera.zoom, strum[2].x, player.pose, ... 78 modifiers Numbers planned on the beats that bend the playfield: sway, downscroll, turnZ, cam.z, ... 9 choice lists the fixed words some of them take: easings, layers, blend modes, poses, ...

New here? This page will make more sense after Your first event - it's ten minutes, promise. After that, the names you'll use most are on Frequently used, and the language itself (variables, if, for, operators) is on Files and code.

docs.title: How to read an entry
docs.text:
Every entry looks the same, so once you can read one, you can read them all:

number camera.zoom = 1

0 – 5fights onlykept at the song's end

  • the name as you write it, as the entry's heading,
  • the signature: its kind (number, colour, switch = true / false, choice = one of a few words, text), every way to write it, and its default. For a call: its arguments, the [optional] ones in brackets,
  • tags: its range, its unit, read only, fights only, Windows only, kept at the song's end,
  • then what it does, notes, an example, and the matching name in Psych Engine / Kade Engine.

(The tags above are only a sample.)

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
One page per group. Each starts with how to use it and an example, then lists every property with its kind, default and range. The kinds and how properties combine: Properties.

Page What Count camera zoom, beat bump, shake; the fight camera 13 hud score line, title, hearts, bars, the playfield's angle and offset 19 judgments the rating popups 4 screen, flash, vignette colours over the picture, the playfield's size 8 strums the whole strumline, scroll, input 10 strum[lane] one lane 17 underlay the strum background 4 note[i] every note on its way, one by one 15 text[n] eight texts 13 image[n] 32 pictures, sprite sheets, Psych sprites, videos 22 Fighters player, opponent, boyfriend, dad, puppet[i] 32 Body parts player.head, .leftArm, ... 8 fx built-in effects 17 shader[n] the song's own shaders 8 volume the song's audio tracks 3 window the game window, desktop mode 19 popout[n] pop-out windows 15 monitor the monitor's place and size 4 song the kind of run, progress, who sings 9 player (your run) score, combo, misses, accuracy, health 6

docs.title: Actions and timers
docs.text:
Actions do things: animate a property, run code later, put things back, play a sound. They're the building blocks everything else is made of - even the shortcuts (flash(), zoom(), flipScroll(), ...) are just ready-made actions for the common cases.

Kind Actions Animate tween · approach · stopTween Later and again after · every · cancel Put things back reset / resetAll · resetCamera · resetPuppet · resetFx · resetWindow The song scrollTo / scrollBy · countdown · scatterStrums Sound playSound · loopSound Debugging log / print

Durations are milliseconds. Write them with beats(2), steps(4), seconds(0.5) or ms(300) - beats and steps use the tempo at the moment of the call, so a song's tempo changes are taken care of.

docs.title: tween
docs.text:
tween(prop, to, duration[, ease])

Animates a property from where it is now to to.

prop a number or colour property: camera.zoom, strum[2].x, flash.color, ... to where it ends up duration how long - beats(2), seconds(1); 0 = at once ease optional - how it moves, one of the easing curves (default "linear") 
tween(camera.zoom, 1.2, beats(2), "sineInOut")   -- zoom in over two beats
tween(flash.color, #FF0000, beats(1))             -- colours blend channel by channel

Setting the property directly stops a tween on it, and a new tween replaces the old one. Opacities stay inside 0-1 even when an overshooting ease (backOut, elasticOut) swings past.

Psych: doTweenX, doTweenAlpha, doTweenZoom, noteTweenX, startTween · Kade: tweenPos, tweenAngle, tweenFadeIn

docs.title: approach
docs.text:
approach(prop, to, rate)

Moves a property a share of the way toward to every 60th of a second - it follows a moving target smoothly, at the same speed whatever the frame rate. rate is that share, 0-1 (0.05 = gentle, 0.3 = snappy).

function onFrame(dt)
    approach(hud.angle, player.combo > 50 ? 2 : 0, 0.05)   -- tilts while the combo is high
end

docs.title: stopTween
docs.text:
stopTween(prop)

Stops a tween right where it is. (reset would put the property back to its default instead.)

stopTween(camera.zoom)       -- the zoom stays where the tween had got to

Psych: cancelTween(tag)

docs.title: after
docs.text:
after(duration, function() ... end[, "name"])

Runs the function that much later, in song time. It remembers every local as it was when you called after, so each round of a loop keeps its own value:

function onEvent(p)
    for lane = 0, 3 do
        after(beats(lane * 0.5), function()
            tween(strum[lane].angle, 360, beats(1), "backOut")   -- one lane after the other
        end)
    end
end

With a name, cancel can drop it before it runs.

Psych: runTimer(tag, seconds) + onTimerCompleted

docs.title: every
docs.text:
every(duration, function() ... end[, times][, "name"])

Runs the function again and again, one duration apart - times times, or until the song ends. The first run is one duration from now. Its locals stay from one run to the next, so a counter inside it counts on.

function onEvent(p)
    local ticks = 0

    every(beats(1), function()                -- 8 times, once a beat
        ticks += 1
        text[2].value = str(ticks)
    end, 8)

    every(beats(0.5), function()              -- until cancel("blink")
        strums.alpha = strums.alpha == 1 ? 0.6 : 1
    end, "blink")
end

It runs at most once a frame, however short the duration.

Psych: runTimer(tag, seconds, loops)

docs.title: cancel
docs.text:
cancel("name")

Drops this event's waiting after / every calls with that name. Other events' timers aren't touched.

after(beats(16), function()
    cancel("blink")
    strums.alpha = 1
end)

Psych: cancelTimer(tag)

docs.title: reset
docs.text:
reset(what[, duration[, ease]])resetAll([duration[, ease]])

Puts things back to their defaults - at once, or eased over a duration (the easing defaults to "sineInOut"). what is:

what Puts back one property: hud.angle, strum[2].x that property a group: hud, judgments, underlay, camera, fx, screen, flash, vignette, volume, ... every property of it (camera with the bump settings) strums the whole strumline and every lane one slot: strum[2], text[0], image[4], shader[1] everything of that slot text, image, shader every slot a fighter: player, opponent, boyfriend, dad, puppet[i] like resetPuppet a body part: player.head that part window like resetWindow popout[n] eases it home, then closes it

resetAll puts back every property the scripts can write. Numbers and colours ease; texts and switches change at once. A text, picture or shader reset over a duration fades out (alpha / amount to 0) and is cleared at the end - unless a script writes to it meanwhile. Tweens on what's reset stop.

reset(hud.angle)                         -- at once
reset(hud, beats(1), "backOut")          -- the whole HUD, overshooting a little
reset(strum[2], beats(0.5))              -- one lane
reset(text[0], beats(1))                 -- fades out, then empty
resetAll(beats(2))                       -- everything, over two beats

The song's end resets the moving parts by itself - see When the song ends.

Psych: — (set every value back by hand) · Kade: —

docs.title: resetCamera
docs.text:
resetCamera([duration[, ease]])

Puts the fight camera back: at once, or gliding home over the duration. fights

resetCamera(beats(2))

docs.title: resetPuppet
docs.text:
resetPuppet(who[, duration[, ease]])

Puts a fighter back - position, size, turn, tint, body parts: "player", "opponent", "both", or 0 / 1. fights

resetPuppet("both", beats(1))

docs.title: resetFx
docs.text:
resetFx([duration[, ease]])

Switches the effects and shaders off: at once, or fading out.

resetFx(beats(2))

docs.title: resetWindow
docs.text:
resetWindow([duration[, ease]])

Puts the game window back and closes every pop-out: at once, or gliding home first.

resetWindow(beats(1))

docs.title: scrollTo
docs.text:
scrollTo(speed[, duration])scrollBy(factor[, duration])

scrollTo sets the scroll speed (1 = the player's own); scrollBy multiplies the current one. In the "modern" scroll style notes are placed on the planned curve, so the changes are worked out when the song starts.

scrollTo(1.5, beats(2))     -- 1.5x, eased in over two beats
scrollBy(0.5)               -- half of what it is now, at once

Psych: the built-in "Change Scroll Speed" event · Kade: scrollspeed

docs.title: countdown
docs.text:
countdown()

Shows the 3-2-1-GO countdown over the running song - for a song that "starts again" after a break.

docs.title: scatterStrums
docs.text:
scatterStrums([rate])

Throws your four lanes to random spots that never overlap or leave the screen, easing there at rate (default 0.7). resetLanes brings them home. Players find it hard to read - use it sparingly, if at all.

docs.title: Sound
docs.text: Sound files are .ogg files in the song's folder or its events/ folder. More in Sounds and music.

docs.title: playSound
docs.text:
playSound(file[, volume[, "name"]])

Plays a sound once. volume 0-1 (default 1), on top of MineFunkin's own volume. With a name it can be faded and stopped later; a new sound under the same name replaces the one still playing.

playSound("cymbal.ogg", 0.7)
playSound("thunder.ogg", 1, "thunder")

Psych: playSound(file, volume, tag)

docs.title: loopSound
docs.text:
loopSound(file, volume, "name")

Plays a sound over and over until stopSound("name") or the song's end. A loop always needs a name.

loopSound("rain.ogg", 0.6, "rain")

Psych: playSound + onSoundFinished to start it again

docs.title: log
docs.text:
log(...)print(...)

Writes the values, joined with spaces, to the event log (logs/minefunkin-events.log). The quickest way to find out what a script does. At most 200 lines per event per run.

log("combo is", player.combo, "at", time)

Psych: debugPrint

docs.title: Easing curves
docs.text:
Family In Out In and out sine (gentle) sineIn sineOut sineInOut quad quadIn quadOut quadInOut cubic cubicIn cubicOut cubicInOut quart quartIn quartOut quartInOut expo (sharp) expoIn expoOut circ circIn circOut back (overshoots) backIn backOut backInOut elastic (springs) elasticOut bounce bounceOut

In starts slow and ends fast, out starts fast and settles - the usual pick for something that arrives. backOut, elasticOut and bounceOut overshoot and settle: great for pops, squashes and landings. linear keeps the same speed all the way.

docs.title: Callbacks
docs.text:
Callbacks are how your script hears about the song. They're functions the game calls when something happens: a beat, a hit, a miss, the chart reaching your event. You just write the ones you care about and leave out the rest - a file can have any mix of them.

function onBeat(b)
    camera.bump += 0.02      -- runs on every beat of the song
end
When Callbacks The song onStart · onCountdown · onSongStart · onEvent · onEnd · onFail The music's time onBeat · onStep · onSection · onFrame Notes onHit · onMiss · onOpponentHit Keys onKeyPress · onKeyRelease · onGhostTap Pause onPause · onResume

Every callback runs for every loaded event

onBeat in your file runs on every beat - whether or not the chart has used your event yet. That's why a file with only onBeat / onHit and no onEvent works as a song script, and why an event that switches a mode on checks its own active variable first.

Parameters are optional and you name them yourself: function onBeat() and function onBeat(b) both work. Just don't call them beat, step or time - those are built-in values, so the name is taken (function onBeat(b) still reads the current beat as beat).

docs.title: onStart
docs.text:
function onStart()

The song is set up, before the countdown - and again on every restart. Set up your pictures, texts and starting values here.

function onStart()
    strums.alpha = 0
    tween(strums.alpha, 1, beats(4))     -- the lanes fade in during the countdown
end

Psych: onCreate · Kade: start(song)

docs.title: onCountdown
docs.text:
function onCountdown(n)

Each step of the 3-2-1-Go countdown. Gets n: 3, 2, 1, then 0 for "go".

function onCountdown(n)
    text[3].value = n == 0 ? "GO!" : str(n)
    text[3].alpha = 1
    tween(text[3].alpha, 0, beats(0.9))
end

Psych: onCountdownTick(counter)

docs.title: onSongStart
docs.text:
function onSongStart()

The music starts, right after the countdown.

function onSongStart()
    showStrums(beats(1))     -- the lanes come in with the music
end

Psych: onSongStart

docs.title: onEvent
docs.text:
function onEvent(p)

The song reaches a chart event of this file's name (or alias). Gets p: the event's parameters by name (p.speed, p.tint, ...) plus the raw p.value1 and p.value2.

params {
    tint = color { from = "value1", default = #FFFFFF, label = "Colour" },
}

function onEvent(p)
    flash(p.tint, beats(1))
end

Psych: onEvent(name, value1, value2) in custom_events/

docs.title: onEnd
docs.text:
function onEnd()

The song was played to its end. Not when it was failed, left, or a fight was decided early.

function onEnd()
    text[0].value = "CLEAR!"
end

Psych: onEndSong

docs.title: onFail
docs.text:
function onFail()

Your health ran out - just before the song ends as failed. Only where there's health: in fights (practice has none).

function onFail()
    fadeOut(#000000, beats(1))
end

Psych: onGameOver

docs.title: The music's time
docs.text: Beats and steps ride the same beat as the camera bop, so everything on the beat lands together. A slow frame never skips one: if the game hitches over a few steps, each still gets its onStep (and onBeat, onSection) in order - you can hang a whole song's timeline on step numbers.

docs.title: onBeat
docs.text:
function onBeat(b)

A new beat starts. Gets b: the beat number (0, 1, 2, ...).

function onBeat(b)
    if b % 4 == 0 then camera.bump += 0.03 end   -- a pop on the first beat of every bar
end

Psych: onBeatHit + curBeat · Kade: beatHit(beat)

docs.title: onStep
docs.text:
function onStep(n)

A new step starts - a sixteenth note, four per beat. Gets n: the step number.

function onStep(n)
    if n == 256 then flash() end      -- an exact moment of the song, by step
end

Psych: onStepHit + curStep · Kade: stepHit(step)

docs.title: onSection
docs.text:
function onSection(n)

Every 4 beats (beats 0, 4, 8, ...), right after that beat's onBeat. Gets n: the section number (0, 1, 2, ...).

function onSection(n)
    zoom(n % 2 == 0 ? 1.05 : 1, beats(1))   -- in and out, bar by bar
end

Psych: onSectionHit + curSection

docs.title: onFrame
docs.text:
function onFrame(dt)

Every rendered frame. Gets dt: milliseconds since the last frame. Use it for anything that moves all the time - work positions out from time (or beat), so it looks the same at any frame rate.

function onFrame(dt)
    hud.angle = sin(time / 500) * 1.5      -- a slow sway
end

Psych: onUpdate(elapsed) · Kade: update(elapsed)

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
The three note callbacks get the note:

Field note.lane 0-3: left, down, up, right note.judgment "sick", "good", "bad", "shit" or "miss" note.offset how early (negative) or late it was hit, in ms; 0 for misses and the opponent note.hold whether it's a hold note

note or n?

Inside function onHit(note) the name note is that one note - the notes on their way (note[0], note[1], ...) are out of reach there. If you need both, call it n: function onHit(n).

docs.title: onHit
docs.text:
function onHit(note)

You hit a note.

function onHit(note)
    if note.hold then return end
    strum[note.lane].scale = 1.15
    tween(strum[note.lane].scale, 1, beats(0.5), "backOut")
end

docs.title: Pause
docs.text: While the game is paused or counting down, only onCountdown, onPause and onResume are called. Tweens and after / every timers run on the song's time, so they wait while it's paused.

docs.text:

The song is paused.

Psych: onPause

docs.text:
function onResume()

The song goes on after a pause.

docs.title: In what order
docs.text: Within one frame, for every loaded event - the built-ins first, then the song's own files in file-name order: the steps, beats and sections that started, then onFrame. After that come the waiting after / every functions whose time has come. Two scripts writing the same property in the same frame: the later one wins (and the event log names both).

docs.title: Your own functions
docs.text:
You can write your own functions next to the callbacks. They take parameters, return a value, and are called like any function:

local function pop(amount)
    camera.bump += amount
end

function onHit(note)
    pop(note.judgment == "sick" ? 0.03 : 0.01)
end

More on that in Functions and values.

docs.title: camera
docs.text:
Everything about how the song is framed: the zoom and the little pop on every beat - and in a fight, the camera behind your fighter itself. Where it stands, where it looks, how wide its lens is.

How to use it

camera is always there, you don't have to set anything up. Change a value, tween it, and when you're done, put it all back with reset(camera) or resetCamera([duration]).

  • In every song: zoom, bump, bumpEvery, bumpStrength, shake.
  • Only in fights: x, y, z, yaw, pitch, roll, fov and nudge move the camera that stands behind your fighter. Practice has no world, so there they simply do nothing. And only you see your camera move - your opponent has their own.

Shortcuts: zoom, shake, focus. How it all fits together: The fight camera.

Psych: camGame.zoom, cameraShake, triggerEvent('Camera Follow Pos') · Kade: cameraZoom, cameraAngle

docs.title: Example code
docs.text:
format 1.1
-- Bump on every beat, and look over at the opponent for two beats.
event { name = "Look Over" }

function onBeat(b)
    camera.bump += 0.03
end

function onEvent(p)
    tween(camera.yaw, -6, beats(1), "sineInOut")
    tween(camera.fov, -8, beats(1), "sineInOut")
    after(beats(2), function() resetCamera(beats(1)) end)
end

docs.title: Choices
docs.text:
Some properties and actions take one of a few fixed words - a layer, an easing curve, a pose. They're all on this page, one list each, so you can see what every word actually does.

Don't worry about typos: a word a property can't take is an error as soon as the file loads, with a guess at what you meant: text[0].layer = "frnot" → unknown layer "frnot" - did you mean "front"?

docs.title: Easing curves
docs.text:
How a value moves from where it is to where it's going.

How to use it

The last argument of tween, reset / resetAll, the reset actions and most shortcuts that take a duration. Left out = "linear" (tween) or "sineInOut" (the resets). Case doesn't matter.

tween(camera.zoom, 1.2, beats(2), "sineInOut")   -- smooth in and out
tween(player.squash, 0, beats(1), "elasticOut")  -- lands like jelly
reset(hud, beats(1), "backOut")                  -- overshoots a little on the way home
Family In Out In and out linear linear sine (gentle) sineIn sineOut sineInOut quad quadIn quadOut quadInOut cubic cubicIn cubicOut cubicInOut quart quartIn quartOut quartInOut quint quintIn quintOut quintInOut expo (sharp) expoIn expoOut expoInOut circ circIn circOut circInOut back (overshoots) backIn backOut backInOut elastic (springs) elasticIn elasticOut elasticInOut bounce bounceIn bounceOut bounceInOut

In starts slow and ends fast, out starts fast and settles - the usual pick for something that arrives. backOut, elasticOut and bounceOut overshoot and settle: good for pops, squashes and landings. Opacities and volumes stay inside 0-1 even while an overshooting curve swings past.

For modifiers (ease, add) the same names work, plus "instant" (there at once) and "arc" (out to the value and back).

Psych: 'sineInOut' etc. (the same names as Flixel's FlxEase) · Kade: FlxEase

docs.title: Layers
docs.text:
Where a text or picture is drawn, from the bottom up.

How to use it

text[n].layer and image[n].layer. Within a layer, order decides: higher is drawn later, so on top. Texts and pictures share it; with the same order, pictures come before texts and lower slots before higher ones.

image[1].file  = "logo.png"
image[1].layer = "lanes"    -- behind the notes, in front of the strum background
text[0].layer  = "top"      -- stays visible while the screen fades to black
text[0].order  = 2
Layer Drawn "stage" Pictures only. In a fight painted onto the world, right before the fighters - a stage's background and its sprites (use follow so they stay on the world while the camera moves). In practice it's under the puppets. "back" Behind the strum background - under everything that belongs to the playfield. "lanes" On the strum background, under the receptors and notes. "front" Over the playfield and the HUD (the default). "top" Over everything, even the flash and screen colours - a line stays readable over a cut to black.

The vignette sits between the playfield and "front", so captions stay readable while it darkens the edges. Texts and pictures stay put on the screen: the bump, shake and HUD rotation don't move them (a picture with follow moves with the fight camera instead).

Psych: addLuaSprite(tag, front), setObjectOrder, setObjectCamera

docs.title: Blend modes
docs.text:
How a picture is laid over what's under it.

How to use it

image[n].blend. The default is "normal".

image[3].file = "glow.png"
image[3].blend = "add"        -- a glow: only brightens
image[4].file = "shadow.png"
image[4].blend = "multiply"   -- a shadow or a tint: only darkens
Mode What it does "normal" Painted over, by its alpha. "add" Its colours are added - light, glows, sparks, fire. Black disappears. "multiply" Multiplied - darkens and tints. White disappears. "screen" The opposite of multiply - lightens softly. Black disappears. "erase" Wipes out what's under it where it's opaque. In desktop mode that's a hole to the desktop. "key" In desktop mode its exact #131313 pixels become holes to the desktop; the rest is drawn normally. Outside desktop mode it's a normal picture.

Psych: setBlendMode(tag, 'add')

docs.title: Fonts
docs.text:
Minecraft's own fonts for text[n].font.

How to use it

Set text[n].font. The default is "default". A resource pack that changes a font changes it here too.

text[2].value = "the end is near"
text[2].font = "alt"    -- enchanting table runes
Font "default" Minecraft's pixel font. "uniform" The smooth Unicode font. "alt" The enchanting table's runes (Standard Galactic). "illager" The illagers' runes.

Psych: setTextFont(tag, 'vcr.ttf') - MineFunkin can't load font files; use these.

docs.title: Poses
docs.text:
MineFunkin's own poses for a fighter - the ones the notes play.

How to use it

player.pose (or the shortcut pose(who, name)) plays one; setPose(who, name, ...) replaces one with a pose of your own for the rest of the song.

-- The opponent "sings" a chord with you, then drops.
opponent.pose = "left"
after(beats(1), function() opponent.pose = "right" end)
after(beats(2), function() opponent.pose = "death" end)
after(beats(6), function() opponent.pose = "none" end)
Pose "left", "down", "up", "right" The note pose of that lane: pops at the moment it's set and holds, like a held note. Changing straight to another lane pops the new one. "death" The death: the fighter jolts back and sits down, and stays down. "none" Lets go: a held pose eases out like a released note, the death ends. The notes decide again. "idle" Only for setPose: the rest pose the idle bob plays around.

"Left" and "right" keep their direction on the screen: seen from behind (your fighter) or from the front (the opponent), a "left" pose leans to the screen's left.

docs.title: Fighter names
docs.text:
How an action or shortcut is told which fighter you mean.

How to use it

The who argument of pose, setPose / clearPose, setSkin, setModel, focus, bind / unbind, resetPuppet, atPlace. As properties, the same names are the Fighters: player.x, dad.alpha, puppet[1].pose.

pose("dad", "up")              -- whoever plays the opponent part
setSkin("both", "skins/bf.png")
resetPuppet(1, beats(1))       -- puppet[1] = the opponent
Name Who "player" or 0 You. "opponent" or 1 The other fighter. "boyfriend" Whoever plays the chart's Boyfriend part (the player side) - you, unless you play the opponent side. "dad" Whoever plays the chart's opponent part. "both" Both at once - for pose, setPose, clearPose, setSkin, setModel, resetPuppet. "center" Only for focus: the camera's middle between the two.

Use boyfriend / dad when an effect belongs to a part of the chart (Boyfriend's solo), player / opponent when it belongs to you (your own camera, your fighter in front). song.side says which side you play.

docs.title: Effect targets
docs.text:
What an effect covers.

How to use it

fx.target for the built-in effects, shader[n].target for each of the song's own shaders. The default is "screen".

fx.target = "world"   -- the notes and the HUD stay sharp
fx.pixelate = 8
Target What gets the effect "screen" Everything: the world, the HUD, the strumline, your texts and pictures. "world" Only the world - the notes and the HUD stay sharp, so even a heavy effect stays playable. Fights only. "terrain" The world without the two fighters: everything around them changes, they stay as they are. Fights only.

Practice (the Retro TV) has no world, so "world" and "terrain" do nothing there; a shader's status says "fight only". They run in the order terrain, world, screen.

docs.title: Scroll directions
docs.text:
Which way the notes travel.

How to use it

strums.scroll for every lane, strum[lane].scroll for one, or the shortcuts setScroll and flipScroll.

setScroll("down")      -- every lane
strum[0].scroll = "up" -- only the left lane goes up
Direction "auto" As the player has set it (player.downscroll). For one lane: follow strums.scroll. "up" Notes rise to receptors at the top. "down" Notes fall to receptors at the bottom.

strum[lane].isDown says what a lane really does right now. For other angles (notes from the side) use strum[lane].direction.

docs.title: Pop-out parts
docs.text:
What a pop-out window can show.

How to use it

popout[n].show: one or more parts, separated by commas, spaces or +. A part that is in a pop-out leaves the game window (unless keep is on). Case doesn't matter.

popout[0].show = "player"
popout[1].show = "left, right"
popout[2].show = "score + health"
Part "player", "opponent" A fighter: in a fight the fighter from the world, in practice its puppet. "strums" All four of your lanes. "left", "down", "up", "right" One lane (also "lane0" ... "lane3"). "opponentStrums" The opponent's receptors (practice). "judgments" The rating popups. "score", "title", "health" One piece of the HUD. "hud" The whole HUD. "text0" ... "text7" A text. "image0" ... "image31" A picture.

docs.title: Fighters
docs.text:
The two fighters: player (you) and opponent. Move them, turn them, squash them, tint them, pose them, re-skin them, pin them to the screen like sprites, outline them. All of it only in your own picture, so go wild.

How to use it

Every property here has several names for the same two fighters:

Name Who player / puppet[0] you opponent / puppet[1] the other one boyfriend / dad by the chart's sides: whoever plays the Boyfriend part / the opponent part - the same as player / opponent unless you play the opponent side

Where: in a fight, the fighters in the world - seen only by you, the real players don't move. In practice, the two puppets beside the lanes follow most of it (position, size, squash, turn, tint, poses, body parts, pinning); clip*, outline*, depth and facing are fights only.

Put one back with resetPuppet(who[, duration]) or reset(player, duration). Shortcuts: pose, setPose, setSkin, setModel, swapFighters, bind, focus. Body parts: Body parts. The whole picture: The fighters.

Psych: boyfriend.x, dad.alpha, characterPlayAnim, setObjectCamera · Kade: boyfriend, dad

docs.title: Example code
docs.text:
-- The opponent slides in from the right into the middle, looks at you, then goes back.
function onEvent(p)
    opponent.pinned = true
    opponent.screenX = 1.3
    opponent.screenY = opponent.homeY
    opponent.facing = "camera"
    tween(opponent.screenX, 0.5, beats(2), "cubicInOut")
    after(beats(8), function()
        tween(opponent.screenX, opponent.homeX, beats(2), "cubicInOut")
        after(beats(2), function() resetPuppet("opponent") end)
    end)
end

docs.title: Frequently used
docs.text: The handful of names almost every event is made of. Learn these and you can build most things - each one links to its full entry.

docs.title: The skeleton of an event
docs.text:
format 1.1

event { name = "My Event" }

function onEvent(p)       -- the chart reaches the event
    flash()
end
Name onEvent(p) the chart reaches this event - p.value1, p.value2, your parameters onBeat(b) every beat onFrame(dt) every frame - for things that move all the time onHit(note) / onMiss(note) you hit / missed a note onStart() before the countdown - set things up, preload pictures

docs.title: Time
docs.text: Name beats(n), steps(n), seconds(n) durations, at the song's tempo time, beat, step where the song is right now after(duration, function() ... end) later every(duration, function() ... end) again and again

docs.title: Making things move
docs.text: Name tween(prop, to, duration[, ease]) animate any number or colour - with an easing curve reset(what[, duration[, ease]]) put it back sin(x), lerp(a, b, t), clamp for values worked out every frame

docs.title: One-line effects
docs.text: Shortcut flash([colour]) a flash zoom(z[, duration]) zoom in, and stay shake(strength) a short shake flipScroll() downscroll ↔ upscroll hideHud() / showHud() the HUD out / in focus(who) the fight camera leans toward someone pose(who, name) a fighter strikes a pose

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: Property camera.zoom, camera.bump the zoom, the beat pop hud.angle, hud.alpha the HUD turned, faded strum[lane].x, strum[lane].alpha one lane moved, faded strums.x, strums.alpha the whole strumline flash.alpha, screen.alpha colours over the picture text[n].value a text on the screen image[n].file a picture on the screen player.squash, player.pose your fighter fx.grayscale, fx.chromatic built-in effects

docs.title: Reading the game
docs.text: Name player.health, player.combo your run song.singer who sings right now song.mode practice, fight, replay or watching

docs.title: Functions and values
docs.text:
Functions work something out and hand you the answer, so you can use them anywhere a value fits: hud.angle = sin(time / 300) * 5. (The ones that do something, like tween and after, are on Actions and timers.)

Kind Built-in values time, beat, step, bpm, pi Game state score, combo, health, the song's progress, who sings - read only Durations beats, steps, seconds, ms Maths sin, lerp, clamp, snap, pingpong, ... Chance and noise random, randomInt, chance, noise Colours rgb, hsv, mix Text str, upper, sub, find, replace, ... Notes and fighters noteSlot, atPlace Your own functions local function name(...) ... end

docs.title: Built-in values
docs.text:
Name Value time the song time in milliseconds beat the current beat (whole number, counts from 0) step the current step (a sixteenth, four per beat) bpm the tempo right now pi 3.14159... 
-- Sway the playfield once every two seconds, whatever the tempo.
function onFrame(dt)
    hud.angle = sin(time / 1000 * pi) * 3
end

Psych: getSongPosition(), curBeat, curStep, bpm · Kade: songPos, curBeat, curStep, bpm

docs.title: Game state
docs.text:
Values the game keeps up to date; scripts read them like properties. Each has its entry on its property page:

Page What it answers player (your run) player.score, .combo, .misses, .accuracy, .health, .downscroll song song.mode, .fight, .practice, .replay, .length, .progress, .singer, .side, .canHeal screen screen.width, screen.height - the playfield's size strums / strum[lane] strums.spacing, scroll.speed, strum[lane].isDown, .pressed note[i] notes.count, note[i].lane, .time, .distance, ... Fighters player.homeX, .homeY, .place window / monitor the window's and the monitor's places and sizes, what works here 
-- The whole screen goes a little redder the lower your health is.
function onFrame(dt)
    screen.color = #FF0000
    screen.alpha = (1 - player.health) * 0.25
end

Psych: getProperty("health"), score, misses, rating, mustHitSection · Kade: downscroll, mustHit, screenWidth

docs.title: Durations
docs.text:
Every duration in an action is in milliseconds. These turn musical lengths into milliseconds at the tempo of the moment:

Function beats(n) n beats steps(n) n steps (a quarter beat each) seconds(n) n seconds ms(n) n milliseconds (as written - for readability) 
tween(camera.zoom, 1.1, beats(2), "sineInOut")    -- over two beats
after(steps(3), function() flash.alpha = 0.5 end)  -- three sixteenths later

docs.title: Maths
docs.text:
Function sin(x), cos(x), tan(x) x in radians (pi = half a turn) atan2(y, x) the angle of (x, y) in degrees abs(x), sqrt(x), exp(x), ln(x), pow(a, b) (a ^ b is the same as pow(a, b)) floor(x), ceil(x), round(x), int(x) int cuts toward zero: int(-1.5) = -1, floor(-1.5) = -2 sign(x) -1, 0 or 1 min(a, b), max(a, b), clamp(x, lo, hi) lerp(a, b, t) from a (t = 0) to b (t = 1) smoothstep(e0, e1, x) 0 below e0, 1 above e1, a soft S-curve between snap(x, s) x rounded to a multiple of s: snap(37, 10) = 40 pingpong(x, length) 0 → length → 0 → length ... as x grows 
function onHit(note)
    -- A value that runs 0 → 1 → 0 over every bar:
    local wave = pingpong(beat % 4, 2) / 2

    -- Closer to the beat = more glow (0 ms off = 1, 80 ms or more = 0):
    local glow = 1 - smoothstep(0, 80, abs(note.offset))
    strum[note.lane].scale = 1 + 0.2 * glow * wave
end

docs.title: Chance and noise
docs.text:
Function random() a number from 0 to 1 random(a, b) a number from a to b randomInt(a, b) a whole number from a to b, both included: randomInt(0, 3) = a random lane chance(p) true with probability p (chance(0.25) = one in four) noise(x) smooth noise from -1 to 1. The same x always gives the same value, so it wobbles instead of jittering. 
-- A camera that drifts like a handheld one:
function onFrame(dt)
    camera.yaw = noise(time / 900) * 2
    camera.pitch = noise(time / 1100 + 50) * 1.5
end

random() gives the same numbers every time the song is played - on a restart, in its replay and for someone watching from inside - so a "random" effect looks the same for everyone. Each script draws its own numbers (another event added to the song doesn't change yours). noise is for a smooth wobble, random for a fresh pick.

docs.title: Colours
docs.text:
Colours are numbers written #RRGGBB (or #AARRGGBB). These make them:

Function rgb(r, g, b[, a]) from 0-255 channels hsv(h, s, v[, a]) hue in degrees, saturation and value 0-1, alpha 0-1 mix(c1, c2, t) c1 blended toward c2 by t (0-1) 
-- A colour that walks around the wheel, one turn every 4 beats:
flash.color = hsv(beat * 90 % 360, 0.7, 1)

-- Health from green to red:
underlay.color = mix(#FF3040, #30FF80, player.health)

tween on a colour property blends channel by channel, so colours fade smoothly too.

docs.title: Text
docs.text:
Function str(x) a value as text upper(s), lower(s) len(s) how many characters sub(s, from[, to]) a piece of the text, counting from 1. Negative counts from the end. find(s, part) where part first appears in s (from 1); 0 = not in it replace(s, what, with) every what in s replaced by with trim(s) the spaces at both ends cut off startsWith(s, part), endsWith(s, part) true or false

.. joins text: "Combo " .. player.combo. + joins too when one side is text.

format 1.1

event {
    name = "Shout",
    description = "Shows value1 big; value2 = 'red' for red. Two lines with a | in between.",
}

function onEvent(p)
    local line = trim(p.value1)
    local bar = find(line, "|")

    if bar > 0 then
        text[2].value = upper(sub(line, 1, bar - 1))   -- before the |
        text[1].value = sub(line, bar + 1)              -- after it
    else
        text[2].value = upper(line)
    end

    text[2].color = startsWith(p.value2, "red") ? #FF3040 : #FFFFFF
end
sub example Gives sub("hello", 2, 4) "ell" sub("hello", 2) "ello" sub("hello", -3) "llo"

find, replace, startsWith and endsWith mind upper and lower case - "A" isn't "a" for them (while == ignores case).

docs.title: mod
docs.text:
mod(modifier[, field]) → number

A modifier's value right now, on one field (left out = yours, 1). Works for your own ones (customMod) too.

function onFrame(dt)
    -- Follow the planned sway with the HUD a little.
    hud.x = mod("sway") / 10
end

docs.title: copyField
docs.text:
copyField([source]) → number

A new playfield: 1 (the default) = another copy of your notes, 0 = the opponent's notes, played by themselves. Gives its number (2-7) - use it as the field in ease and the others. A copy shows the same notes you play: you hit once, every copy reacts. Call it in onStart. Six at most; past that it gives -1 and says so in the event log.

local mirror = 0

function onStart()
    mirror = copyField(1)
    set(0, 100, "flipSides", mirror)     -- the copy is mirrored
    set(0, 50, "fade", mirror)           -- and half see-through
end

Psych modcharting tools: addPlayfield()

docs.title: noteSlot
docs.text:
noteSlot(id)

Where the note with this id is in the note[i] list this frame, or -1 once it's gone (hit, missed, off the screen). A note's place in the list moves on as the notes before it are hit; its id stays.

local marked = -1

function onBeat(b)
    if notes.count > 0 then marked = note[notes.count - 1].id end   -- the last one on the screen
end

function onFrame(dt)
    local i = noteSlot(marked)
    if i >= 0 then note[i].scale = 1.5 end
end

docs.title: atPlace
docs.text:
atPlace(place)

Which fighter stands on a place right now: atPlace("bf") / atPlace("dad") gives 0 (you) or 1 (the other) - for puppet[atPlace("dad")]. The places follow bind: without one, you stand on "bf".

-- Whoever stands in the far spot glows red, whoever it is.
function onEvent(p)
    puppet[atPlace("dad")].color = #FF6060
end

docs.title: Your own functions
docs.text:
local function pulse(lane, amount)
    strum[lane].scale = 1 + amount
    tween(strum[lane].scale, 1, beats(0.5), "elasticOut")
end

local function strength(judgment)
    if judgment == "sick" then return 0.3 end
    if judgment == "good" then return 0.15 end
    return 0.05
end

function onHit(note)
    pulse(note.lane, strength(note.judgment))
end

Functions are defined at the top of a file (not inside another function), can take parameters and return a value. They can call each other in any order: the file is read completely before anything runs. The one function you write inside another is the one you hand to after or every.

docs.title: fx
docs.text:
Built-in effects over the picture: colour, blur, pixels, waves, glitches, bloom. No shader writing needed - set a number and it's there.

How to use it

fx is always there. Every effect is off at its default and nothing is computed while all of them are. They run while the song plays, never on the pause menu or the results. target says what they cover: everything, only the world, or the world without the fighters (the effect targets).

The player's "Fewer flashes" option (Options › MineFunkin › Accessibility) keeps invert and glitch at 0.3 and brightness at 1.3 at most.

Put them back with resetFx([duration]). Your own GLSL: shader. The whole picture: Effects.

docs.title: Example code
docs.text:
-- The drop: the world goes grey and grainy, the notes stay sharp.
function onEvent(p)
    fx.target = "world"
    tween(fx.grayscale, 1, beats(1))
    fx.grain = 0.4
    after(beats(16), function() resetFx(beats(2)) end)
end

docs.title: hud
docs.text:
Everything that isn't the notes: the score line, the song's title and time, the hearts of a fight, the cinematic bars - plus the angle and offset of the whole playfield. Fade it out for a quiet moment, tilt it for a drop, move single pieces out of the way of your stage art.

How to use it

hud is always there. The whole HUD: alpha, angle, x, y. One piece: scoreX ... healthScale, each moved and sized around its own middle.

Shortcuts: hideHud / showHud. The rating popups are judgments, the strip behind the lanes is the underlay.

docs.title: image[n]
docs.text:
Thirty-two pictures: logos, stage art, sprite sheets, Psych sprites with their animations, videos, plain coloured boxes. Everything you need to dress up a song.

How to use it

image[0] to image[31] - set file and it shows, "" hides it. Positions and sizes are shares of the screen. A picture is loaded the first time it's drawn; preload(file) in onStart loads it before, so it's there on the right frame.

  • Files: a .png in the song folder or its events/ folder (up to 8192 pixels a side, 128 pictures and 512 MB per song). "solid" = a plain white box to colour with color.
  • Animated: a grid sprite sheet (columns, rows, fps), a Psych sprite (.png + Sparrow .xml, anim), or a video as a folder of numbered frames ("videos/intro/").
  • In a fight: the "stage" layer paints it onto the world behind the fighters, follow keeps it on the world while the camera turns.

Texts and pictures share the layers. More: Stages and sprites.

Psych: makeLuaSprite, makeAnimatedLuaSprite, addAnimationByPrefix, setBlendMode, setScrollFactor · Kade: —

docs.title: Example code
docs.text:
-- The song's logo in the top left corner, a pulsing glow behind it.
function onStart()
    image[0].file = "logo.png"
    image[0].x = 0.16
    image[0].y = 0.14
    image[0].width = 0.24
    image[1].file = "glow.png"
    image[1].x = 0.16
    image[1].y = 0.14
    image[1].width = 0.3
    image[1].blend = "add"
    image[1].order = -1
end

function onBeat(b)
    image[1].alpha = 1
    tween(image[1].alpha, 0.3, beats(1))
end

docs.title: judgments
docs.text:
The "Sick!" popup, the ms label and the combo number that jump up on every hit. Move them, shrink them, or hide them for a part where you want the screen clean.

How to use it

judgments is always there. Where they pop up by default is the player's own setting (Options › MineFunkin › Display › "Judgment position"); x and y move them from there.

Shortcuts: hideJudgments / showJudgments.

-- Smaller judgments, a bit higher, for a busy part.
tween(judgments.scale, 0.7, beats(1))
tween(judgments.y, -40, beats(1))
