docs.title: Files and code
docs.text: An event file is plain text. If you've seen Lua, it'll look familiar (function ... end, local, if ... then ... end) - but it's MineFunkin's own language: smaller, with a few handy extras (c ? a : b, ??, #RRGGBB colours), and without the parts a chart never needs. Here's all of it on one page.

docs.title: The file
docs.text:
format 1.1
-- What the event does, in a comment.

event {
    name = "Name",                    -- the name charts use (case doesn't matter) - required
    alias = { "Old Name", "Other" },  -- more names that run this event (optional)
    color = #7C6BFF,                  -- the marker colour in the editor
    category = "Camera",              -- the group in the editor's type picker (default "Custom")
    description = "...",              -- shown in the editor
}

params {
    -- the event's controls in the editor - see Parameters
}

local count = 0                       -- variables (see below)

function onEvent(p)                   -- functions: the callbacks and your own helpers
    count += 1
end
  • The first line that isn't blank or a comment is the format line: format 1.1, the only version MineFunkin runs (format 1.0 files from the development builds before the first release are converted with one click
  • see versions).
  • The top of a file holds only these: event { } (required), params { }, variables, and functions. All code goes inside functions.
  • Comments: -- (or ##) to the end of the line, and --[[ ... ]] across several lines.
  • Line breaks and indentation don't matter. Blocks end with end.
  • Text goes in double or single quotes. Inside the quotes, \n is a new line, \t a tab, and \" or \' a quote.
  • Colours are written #RRGGBB, or #AARRGGBB with alpha.
  • One file defines one event and may be at most 64 KB.

docs.title: The event header
docs.text:
event { } names the event and says how the editor shows it. Every key but name can be left out.

Key name The name charts use (case doesn't matter). A song's own file with the name (or an alias) of a built-in event replaces it for that song. alias More names that run this event: alias = "Old Name" or alias = { "A", "B" }. color The marker colour in the editor, #RRGGBB. category The group in the editor's type picker (default "Custom"). description What it does - the editor shows it in the picker and the inspector. only "fight" = runs only in fights (and their replays, and watching a fight from inside); "practice" = only at the Retro TV. Left out = everywhere. The event log says when an event doesn't run here. 
event {
    name = "Camera Swing",
    category = "Camera",
    color = #6BB8FF,
    description = "Swings the fight camera from side to side.",
    only = "fight",          -- practice stays calm
}

For a check inside the code instead of the whole file: song.mode.

docs.title: Variables
docs.text:
local count = 0        -- at the top: this event's own variable, kept for the whole song
shared mood = "calm"   -- at the top: one value shared by every event that declares it

function onBeat(b)
    local half = b / 2  -- inside a function: lives until the end of its block
    count += 1
end

Top-level variables start with their value when the song starts, and again on every restart. Use a name only after declaring it with local. There are no global variables. shared variables are how two files talk to each other - see song scripts.

Some names are taken (beat, step, time, camera, flash, ...) - the error message says so, and Errors and fixes lists them all.

docs.title: Statements
docs.text:
x = value Sets a variable or property. Also +=, -=, *=, /=. += on text appends. Setting a property stops a tween on it. local x = value A new local. if cond then ... elseif cond then ... else ... end Branches. for i = 1, 10 do ... end Counts from 1 to 10, both ends included. for i = 10, 1, -1 do counts down. break leaves the loop. return value Ends the function and gives the value back. name(...) Calls one of your functions, an action or a shortcut.

There are no while or repeat loops; count with for. Semicolons between statements are optional.

docs.title: Values and operators
docs.text:
Values are numbers, text, true, false and nil. Colours are numbers written #RRGGBB. nil, false, 0 and "" count as false in conditions.

Operator c ? a : b a if c, else b a ?? b a, or b when a is nil or, and, not a or b gives a if it counts as true, else b; a and b gives b if a counts as true, else a ==, != (or ~=), <, <=, >, >= comparison; text compares ignoring case .. joins text: "Score " .. player.score (+ also joins when one side is text) +, -, *, /, %, ^ % stays non-negative for a positive divisor (-1 % 4 = 3); ^ is power

Built-in values (time, beat, step, bpm, pi) and every function (sin, lerp, hsv, beats, ...) are on Functions.

docs.title: Functions inside functions: after
docs.text:
The only function you write inside another one is the one you hand to after. It runs later and remembers every local as it was when it was made, so each round of a loop keeps its own value:

function onEvent(p)
    for lane = 0, 3 do
        after(beats(lane * 0.5), function()
            strum[lane].angle = 0
            tween(strum[lane].angle, 360, beats(1), "backOut")
        end)
    end
end

Lane 0 spins at once, lane 1 half a beat later, and so on. Your own helper functions go at the top of the file: see Functions.

docs.title: Modifiers
docs.text:
Numbers that bend how a playfield is drawn, planned on the song's beats. They never change how notes are judged: you press at the same moment whatever the field looks like.

How to use it

Plan them on the song's beats with ease, set and add, change one right now with setMod, read one with mod(). Most are percent (100 = the full effect), some pixels (measured on a 1280 x 720 screen, whatever the window) or degrees.

Fields: 1 = yours, 0 = the opponent's (not drawn - a fight shows only yours), 2-7 = ones copyField() made. Leave the field out and a change goes to all of them.

Names are looked up without case. Coming from Psych or Kade? The guide's table says which of ours is theirs.

docs.title: Example code
docs.text:
function onStart()
    ease(16, 2, "cubicOut", 100, "sway")       -- beat 16, over 2 beats
    ease(16, 2, "cubicOut", 50, "hover")
    set(24, 100, "downscroll1")                -- lane 1 scrolls the other way from beat 24
    ease(32, 4, "sineInOut", 0, "sway")
end

0 px How far past the receptor notes are still drawn.

docs.title: Field
docs.text: Where the whole field is, how big, how it's turned. Turning goes around the receptor row's middle; spin around the screen's.

Moves the whole field down (pixels).

Moves the whole field toward the camera (pixels) - it gets bigger.

docs.title: zoom

The field's size around its middle (100 = normal, 200 = twice as big).

docs.title: shrink
docs.text:
percent "shrink" = 0

Makes the field smaller: 100 = half its size, -100 = one and a half.

docs.title: turnX
docs.text:

Tips the field forward / back around its receptor row (3D).

docs.title: turnY

degrees "turnY" = 0

Turns the field left / right around its receptor row (3D).

docs.title: turnZ
docs.text:
degrees "turnZ" = 0

Turns the field clockwise around its receptor row.

docs.text: Every field is seen through its own camera (with no field given, they all move together). It looks at the screen from the front - cam.z moves it back, cam.fov makes the 3D stronger or flatter.

pixels "cam.x" = 0

Moves the field's camera right (pixels) - the field moves left.

The camera's lens (degrees, 45 = normal): wider = stronger 3D.

docs.title: Lanes
docs.text: Where each lane is. Per-lane modifiers have a form for one lane: slideX2 moves only lane 2, on top of slideX.

docs.title: slideX
docs.text:
pixels "slideX" · "slideX0" … "slideX3" = 0

Moves lanes right (pixels): slideX = all, slideX0..slideX3 = one lane.

docs.title: slideY
docs.text:
pixels "slideY" · "slideY0" … "slideY3" = 0

Moves lanes down (pixels).

docs.title: slideZ
docs.text:
pixels "slideZ" · "slideZ0" … "slideZ3" = 0

Moves lanes toward the camera (pixels).

docs.title: flipSides
docs.text:
percent "flipSides" = 0

Mirrors the lanes left-right (100 = right lane on the left, 50 = all in the middle).

docs.title: swapPairs
docs.text:
percent "swapPairs" = 0

Swaps neighbouring lanes (left with down, up with right).

docs.title: pinch
docs.text:
percent "pinch" · "pinch0" … "pinch3" = 0

Pulls the lanes together (100 = all in the middle, -100 = twice as far apart).

docs.title: pinchZ
docs.text:
percent "pinchZ" · "pinchZ0" … "pinchZ3" = 0

Bends the row into depth: the outer lanes go back (100 = as far back as they are from the middle; minus = toward the camera).

docs.title: downscroll
docs.text:
percent "downscroll" · "downscroll0" … "downscroll3" = 0

Flips the scroll direction (100 = up- becomes downscroll; 50 = receptors in the middle).

docs.title: fold
docs.text:
percent "fold" = 0

Folds the row like a book: the outer lanes turn back into depth (100 = a quarter turn).

docs.title: Travel
docs.text: How the notes come in. Only the drawing - when you have to press stays exactly the same.

docs.title: speed
docs.text:
percent "speed" = 100

The field's scroll speed (100 = the song's, 200 = notes come twice as fast). Only how they're drawn.

docs.title: freeze
docs.text:
percent "freeze" = 0

The notes stop where they were when it started (100); going back to 0 they catch up.

docs.title: slowDown

docs.title: speedWave
docs.text:
percent "speedWave" · "speedWave0" … "speedWave3" = 0

Notes speed up and slow down as they travel.

docs.title: hover.speed
docs.text:
percent "hover.speed" = 0

How fast hover bobs (0 = normal).

docs.title: bendZ

docs.text:

docs.title: note[i]
docs.text:
Every note on its way to you, one by one. Make them ride in on a wave, fade as they come closer, spin, grow - the wildest modchart effects live here.

How to use it

Every frame the game lists the notes of your lanes that are on the screen (or about to be), in the order they come: note[0] is the next, up to note[notes.count - 1] (at most 128). Read lane, time, distance, ...; write x, y, alpha, angle, scale, visible.

Your values last one frame: before every frame the game puts all notes back. Write them every frame in onFrame. A tween on a note[i] is an error when the file loads, for the same reason.

The list only exists while a script of the song uses note[...] - songs without cost nothing.

Psych: getPropertyFromGroup('notes', i, ...), notes.length · Kade: notes in update

docs.title: Example code
docs.text:
-- Swaying notes: each sways sideways by its distance, and fades in late.
function onFrame(dt)
    for i = 0, notes.count - 1 do
        note[i].x = 30 * sin(note[i].distance / 200 + note[i].lane)
        note[i].alpha = clamp(1 - (note[i].distance - 400) / 600, 0, 1)
    end
end

-- Remember the next note and keep turning it, wherever it is in the list.
local spinning = -1
function onBeat(b)
    if notes.count > 0 then spinning = note[0].id end

    local i = noteSlot(spinning)
    if i >= 0 then note[i].angle = time / 2 end
end

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
A chart event carries two text values, value1 and value2 (the Psych Engine / .mfkn way). Typing settings into raw text fields is no fun, though - so parameters describe what's in them. The editor builds proper controls from them (sliders, switches, colour pickers, dropdowns), and when you edit an event it writes your settings back into value1 and value2 for you.

params {
    speed = number { from = "value1", default = 1, min = 0.1, max = 5, step = 0.05, label = "Speed" },
    style = choice { from = "value2.1", options = { "classic", "modern" } },
    fast  = flag   { from = "value2", word = "FAST" },
}
Kind Value Editor control number a number slider (with min and max) + field switch on when the text isn't empty (the Psych convention: any value1 = on) toggle bool on/true/yes/1 or off/false/no/0 toggle text the text as it is text field color #RRGGBB, RRGGBB, 0xRRGGBB or 8 digits with alpha swatch + field lane 0-3 or L/D/U/R four arrow buttons choice one of options (a unique start like d for down is enough) segmented buttons flag whether word appears anywhere in the value toggle

Options: from, default, min, max, step, label, plus options for a choice and word / group for a flag. Flags with the same group are one pick in the editor - at most one of them is on:

params {
    classic = flag { word = "classic", group = "Style" },
    modern  = flag { word = "modern",  group = "Style" },
}

Writing just the kind (fast = switch) is fine too.

  • from = "value2" reads the whole value. from = "value2.1" reads the part before the first comma, "value2.2" the second part, and so on (up to 8). A value is used either whole or in parts, not both. Flags look at the whole value and are left out of the parts.
  • Without from, parameters take value1, then value2, in the order they are listed.
  • A blank or unreadable value gives the default. Without a default it gives nil, so a script can keep what was set before: speed = p.speed ?? speed.
  • min and max clamp numbers and give the editor's slider its ends. step is the slider's step.
  • onEvent(p) gets them as p.speed, p.style and so on, plus the raw p.value1 and p.value2.

docs.title: Body parts
docs.text:
Every limb on its own: head, body, both arms, both legs. For waves, dances and poses of your own - on top of MineFunkin's animation, or instead of it.

How to use it

Write them as player.head.pitch, opponent.leftArm.roll, puppet[i].rightLeg.scale, boyfriend.body.yaw ... - the parts are head, body, leftArm, rightArm, leftLeg, rightLeg.

"Right", "left" and "forward" are the figure's own: your fighter is seen from behind, so its right is your right; the opponent faces you, so its right is on your left. Both arms at roll = 90 is a T-pose for either; an arm straight up is roll about 165.

Everything goes on top of MineFunkin's own animation. With animate = false on the fighter the animation stops and your values are the whole pose.

Works in fights and on practice's puppets. Back home: resetPuppet(who) or reset(player.head).

docs.title: Example code
docs.text:
-- A wave: the right arm goes up and swings.
player.rightArm.roll = 150
for i = 0, 3 do
    after(beats(i * 0.5), function()
        tween(player.rightArm.roll, i % 2 == 0 ? 120 : 160, beats(0.5), "sineInOut")
    end)
end
after(beats(2), function() resetPuppet("player", beats(0.5)) end)

docs.text:
How your run is going: score, combo, misses, accuracy, health. Read only - scores stay honest - but perfect for a combo counter, or for making things wilder the better you play.

How to use it

Psych: score, combo, misses, rating, health, downscroll · Kade: —

-- The screen goes a little redder the lower your health is.

docs.title: popout[n]
docs.text:
Extra windows that show pieces of the game - your lanes, a fighter, the score - anywhere on the screen. Borderless, see-through, always on top.

How to use it

popout[0] to popout[7] - set show to a list of parts and the window opens, "" closes it. A part shown in a pop-out leaves the game window (unless keep). Pop-outs need a system that lets programs place windows (not Wayland) and the player's OK (Options › MineFunkin › Window & desktop).

The whole picture: Game window and pop-outs.

docs.title: Example code
docs.text:
-- Your fighter jumps out of the game, onto the desktop next to it.
function onEvent(p)
    popout[0].show = "player"
    tween(popout[0].x, -400, beats(2), "backOut")
    after(beats(8), function() reset(popout[0], beats(1)) end)
end

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
Almost everything you'll do in a script comes down to this: change a property. A property is a value with a name, like camera.zoom, strum[2].alpha or player.scale. The game looks at all of them every frame, so the moment you set one, the picture changes. Three things you can do with any of them:

camera.zoom = 1.2                                -- set it
tween(camera.zoom, 1, beats(2), "sineInOut")     -- animate it
reset(camera.zoom)                               -- put it back to its default

docs.title: Where to find what
docs.text:
Group Page camera.* - zoom, beat pop, shake, the fight camera camera hud.* - score line, title, hearts, bars, the playfield's angle and offset hud judgments.* - the rating popups judgments screen.*, flash.*, vignette.* - colours over the picture screen, flash, vignette strums.*, scroll.* - the whole strumline, the scroll, your keys strums strum[lane].* - one lane, its way in and speed strum[lane] underlay.* - the strum background underlay notes.count, note[i].* - every note on its way note[i] text[n].* - eight texts text[n] image[n].* - 32 pictures, sheets, Psych sprites, videos image[n] player.*, opponent.*, boyfriend.*, dad.*, puppet[i].* - the fighters Fighters player.head.*, .leftArm.*, ... - body parts Body parts fx.* - built-in effects fx shader[n].* - the song's own shaders shader[n] volume.* - the song's audio volume window.*, popout[n].*, monitor.* - windows window, popout[n], monitor song.*, player.score, ... - the game's state (read only) song, player (your run)

strum[lane] exists once per lane (0 left, 1 down, 2 up, 3 right), text[n] has 8 slots (0-7), image[n] 32 (0-31), shader[n] 4, popout[n] 8, puppet[i] 2 (0 = you, 1 = the opponent), note[i] up to 128 (as many as notes.count says).

docs.title: Kinds of properties
docs.text:
Kind Example number hud.angle = 15 Can be tweened. Opacities (*.alpha) and volumes go from 0 to 1. colour flash.color = #FF3040 Written #RRGGBB. Can be tweened: colours blend channel by channel. on / off player.visible = false true or false. choice text[0].layer = "top" One of a few words, listed with the property. text text[0].value = "GO!" read player.combo Can only be read.

A fixed value a property can't take (strums.alpha = 5, text[0].layer = "middle") is an error as soon as the file loads, so you catch it right away. A number worked out while the song runs is just kept inside the allowed range, and the event log mentions it once.

docs.title: One thing at a time
docs.text: The one rule worth remembering: a property holds just one value. Setting it stops a tween on it, and two scripts writing it every frame overwrite each other - only the last one shows (the event log names both). So give every effect that runs all the time its own property. That's exactly why lanes have two offsets (x and wobbleX) and the camera has zoom and bump.

docs.title: When the song ends
docs.text:
You don't have to clean up after yourself - the moving parts go home on their own: the HUD, the zoom and shake, the strumline and every lane, the strum background, the fight camera, the fighters (skins and the song's own poses included), the audio volumes, the effects and shaders, the game window and the pop-out windows. Texts and pictures disappear.

Some things are kept on purpose, because the results screen is drawn over them: the flash, screen and vignette colours (a song can end on a cut to black), the beat bump's settings, hud.extras, scroll.style, and the layout of texts, pictures and shaders. Every property page tags them kept at the song's end.

docs.title: Putting things back yourself
docs.text: Mid-song, you often want things back now. reset puts a property, a group (reset(hud)), a slot (reset(strum[2])) or a fighter back - at once, or eased: reset(hud, beats(1), "backOut"). resetAll does everything at once.

docs.title: screen, flash, vignette
docs.text:
Colours over the whole picture: a flash that fades by itself, a colour that stays (a cut to black, a red tint), and a dark vignette around the edges. Cheap, quick, and great for big moments.

How to use it

Always there. All three are drawn over the playfield and the world, under the texts and pictures on the "top" layer.

  • flash is meant to fade: set its alpha high, tween it to 0.
  • screen stays until you change it - fades to black, a white-out, a tint.
  • vignette darkens (or tints) the edges.

Shortcuts: flash, fadeOut / fadeIn.

Psych: cameraFlash, cameraFade · Kade: flashCamera

docs.title: Example code
docs.text:
-- A red flash on the drop, then a slow fade to black over the last bar.
flash.color = #FF3040
flash.alpha = 0.8
tween(flash.alpha, 0, beats(1))

after(beats(28), function()
    screen.color = #000000
    tween(screen.alpha, 1, beats(4))
end)

docs.title: shader[n]
docs.text:
Your song's own shaders, four slots of them. Write a .fsh, or bring a .frag from a Psych mod as it is.

How to use it

shader[0] to shader[3] - set file and it runs, "" stops it. The file is a .fsh (MineFunkin's form: vec4 effect(vec2 uv)) or a Psych / Flixel .frag (taken as it is) in the song folder, its events/ or shaders/ folder. A .frag's own uniforms are set with setShaderFloat.

Whether shaders from a song run at all is the player's choice (Options › MineFunkin › Song effects): by default a server's song must pass MineFunkin's shader check, the player's own songs run freely. status says what became of a file.

How to write one: Your own shaders.

docs.title: Example code
docs.text:
-- A shader from the song folder, faded in, its first number pulsing on the beat.
function onStart()
    shader[0].file = "shaders/ripple.fsh"
    shader[0].amount = 0
    tween(shader[0].amount, 1, beats(2))
end

function onBeat(b)
    shader[0].a = 1
    tween(shader[0].a, 0, beats(1), "quadOut")
end

docs.title: Shortcuts
docs.text:
The easy mode, and nothing to be ashamed of. One call each for the things charts do all the time: flash the screen, zoom, hide the HUD, flip the scroll, swap the fighters. You don't need to know anything about properties or tweens to use them - put them inside onEvent (or any other callback) and they just work.

format 1.1

event { name = "Chorus Hit" }

function onEvent(p)
    flash(#FF6EC7)        -- a pink flash
    shake(0.01)           -- a short shake
    zoom(1.1, beats(1))   -- zoom in over one beat, and stay
    hideHud(beats(2))     -- the score line fades out
end
Kind Shortcuts Modifiers ease · set · add · setMod · customMod Lanes and scroll flipScroll · setScroll · hideStrums / showStrums · hideLane / showLane · moveStrums · resetLanes HUD hideHud / showHud · hideJudgments / showJudgments Screen flash · fadeOut / fadeIn · zoom · shake Fighters focus · swapFighters · pose · setPose / clearPose · setSkin · setModel · bind / unbind Effects setShaderFloat Health fights setHealth / addHealth Sound stopSound · soundVolume Events together trigger · call / callIn · preload Debugging inspect

The duration is always optional. Left out, hiding, showing, moving and zooming happen at once; the flash, the fades, the shake, the camera's focus and the fighters' swap take one beat. Write durations with beats(2), steps(4), seconds(0.5) or ms(300). Everything a shortcut changes goes back by itself when the song ends.

A word a shortcut doesn't take (setScroll("sideways"), pose("plyer", "left")) or a lane that doesn't exist is an error when the file loads, with a "did you mean ...?" - not a surprise in the middle of the song.

docs.title: Modifiers
docs.text:
The modifiers: numbers that bend how a field is drawn, planned on the song's beats. Usually all of it goes into onStart: one line per change, in any order. Seeking, watching from inside, replays and the editor all land on the same picture, because a modifier's value only depends on the beat. The guide: Modifiers.

The last two values are the same everywhere: the field (1 = yours, 2-7 = ones copyField() made, a text like "1 2" or "all"; left out = every field) and, for ease, where it starts from (left out = wherever it is at that beat).

docs.title: ease
docs.text:
ease(beat, beats, easing, value, modifier[, field[, from]])

From beat on, over beats beats, the modifier eases to value. The easing is one of the usual names - "cubicOut", "sineInOut", "linear" ... - plus two of the modifiers' own: "instant" (there at once) and "arc" (out to the value and back where it was).

The latest change that started decides: an ease that starts while another one runs takes over from wherever the value is at that moment.

function onStart()
    ease(32, 2, "cubicOut", 100, "sway")         -- every field
    ease(32, 2, "cubicOut", -300, "z", 1)        -- only yours, 300 px back
    ease(40, 1, "arc", 45, "turnZ")              -- tip over and back in one beat
    ease(48, 4, "linear", 0, "sway", "all", 150)  -- from 150 down to 0
end

Psych modcharting tools: ease(32, 2, 'cubeOut', '100, drunk')

docs.title: set
docs.text:
set(beat, value, modifier[, field])

At beat, the modifier jumps to value.

function onStart()
    set(64, 100, "downscroll")   -- the scroll flips at beat 64
    set(72, 0, "downscroll")
end

docs.title: add
docs.text:
add(beat, beats, easing, amount, modifier[, field])

Like ease, but to amount more than the value is at that beat - for kicks that stack on whatever is going on.

-- Every bar the field turns a quarter further.
function onStart()
    for bar = 0, 15 do
        add(bar * 4, 1, "backOut", 90, "turnZ")
    end
end

docs.title: setMod
docs.text:
setMod(modifier, value[, field])

The modifier is value right now - for values you work out yourself every frame (in onFrame) or that answer the player (in onHit). Calling it every frame is fine: it moves one entry along instead of piling them up.

-- The field leans toward the lane you just hit.
function onHit(n)
    setMod("turnZ", (n.lane - 1.5) * 4)
end

Psych modcharting tools: setMod('drunk', 1) · Kade: receptor.angle = ...

docs.title: customMod
docs.text:
customMod(name[, default])

A modifier of your own: a number on the same timeline - eased with ease, read with mod() - that draws nothing by itself. Use it for values you turn into something else in onFrame, or to let two planned values add up. Declare it in onStart of every file that uses it (declaring it twice is fine).

function onStart()
    customMod("glitch")
    ease(64, 4, "sineOut", 1, "glitch")
    ease(72, 1, "sineIn", 0, "glitch")
end

function onFrame(dt)
    fx.glitch = mod("glitch")             -- a planned value driving a screen effect
end

docs.title: Lanes and scroll
docs.text: Lanes are numbered 0 (left), 1 (down), 2 (up), 3 (right).

docs.title: flipScroll
docs.text:
flipScroll([lane])

Downscroll becomes upscroll and the other way round - every lane, or just one.

flipScroll()      -- the whole strumline
flipScroll(2)     -- only the up lane

Psych: setPropertyFromClass("ClientPrefs", "downScroll", ...) · Changes strums.scroll / strum[lane].scroll

docs.title: setScroll
docs.text:
setScroll(direction[, lane])

Sets the scroll direction: "up", "down", or "auto" (back to the player's own setting) - for every lane or one.

setScroll("down")        -- everybody scrolls down
setScroll("up", 0)       -- except the left lane

docs.title: hideStrums
docs.text:
hideStrums([duration])showStrums([duration])

Fades your whole strumline (receptors, notes, holds) out / in.

hideStrums(beats(2))
after(beats(8), function() showStrums(beats(1)) end)

docs.text:
moveStrums(x, y[, duration])

Moves the whole strumline by that many pixels (right, down). moveStrums(0, 0) = home.

moveStrums(-120, 0, beats(2))     -- slide left over two beats

Changes strums.x, strums.y

docs.title: resetLanes
docs.text:
resetLanes([duration[, ease]])

Every lane back to normal: position, wobble, angle, size, opacity, colour, note opacity, scroll direction - and the ways in, speeds and note angles.

resetLanes(beats(1))

The score line, the song title and the hearts.

hideHud(beats(2))

hideJudgments()

docs.title: flash
docs.text:
flash([colour[, duration]])

A flash over the whole picture that fades out - white unless you give a colour. One beat unless you give a duration.

flash()                          -- white, one beat
flash(#FF3040, beats(0.5))       -- red, half a beat

Psych: cameraFlash · Changes flash.color, flash.alpha

docs.title: fadeOut
docs.text:
fadeOut([colour[, duration]])fadeIn([duration])

Fades the picture to a colour (black unless given) and stays there; fadeIn fades back.

fadeOut(#000000, beats(0.5))                      -- a cut to black
after(beats(4), function() fadeIn(beats(2)) end)

Psych: cameraFade · Changes screen.color, screen.alpha

docs.title: zoom
docs.text:
zoom(z[, duration])

Zooms to z (1 = normal, 1.2 = closer) and stays there. At once without a duration. In a fight the world camera zooms along.

zoom(1.15, beats(1))

Shakes that hard (0.01 is a good start) and calms down over the duration.

shake(0.02, beats(2))

Psych: cameraShake · Changes camera.shake

docs.title: Fighters
docs.text:
In a fight they work on the fighters in the world; in practice (the Retro TV) pose, setPose, setSkin, setModel and bind(who, x, y) work on the two puppets beside the lanes. focus, swapFighters and the places of bind need a fight fights.

who is a fighter name: "player", "opponent", "boyfriend", "dad", or "both" where it makes sense.

docs.title: focus
docs.text:
focus(who[, duration])

The fight camera leans toward "opponent" or "player", or back to "center".

function onBeat(b)
    if song.singer == "opponent" then focus("opponent")
    elseif song.singer == "player" then focus("player") end
end

Psych: cameraSetTarget · Changes camera.x, camera.z, camera.yaw

docs.title: swapFighters
docs.text:
swapFighters([duration])

The fighters jump over each other and trade places. Call it again to swap back.

swapFighters(beats(1))

docs.title: pose
docs.text:
pose(who, name)

Plays one of the fighters' poses: "left", "down", "up", "right", "death", or "none" to let go. A pose holds like a held note until "none".

pose("opponent", "up")
after(beats(2), function() pose("opponent", "none") end)

Psych: playAnim / characterPlayAnim · Kade: playActorAnimation

docs.title: setPose
docs.text:
setPose(who, pose, part, pitch[, yaw[, roll]])clearPose(who[, pose])

The song's own pose for a fighter, built part by part: for "idle", "left", "down", "up" or "right" (poses), one body part ("head", "body", "leftArm", "rightArm", "leftLeg", "rightLeg") at these angles in degrees - the same signs as player.head.pitch. Call it once per part; the first call on a pose starts it from the rest pose.

From then on, when a note of that direction comes, the fighter pops into your pose (a little overdone), holds it and eases back - exactly like MineFunkin's own poses. A song idle stays still with a small dip every second beat. clearPose gives MineFunkin's pose back - one, or all five without a name. The song's end clears them too.

In a fight the players standing around see these poses too: your game sends them along.

-- Our own "up": both arms up, head back, a slight lean.
function onStart()
    setPose("both", "up", "leftArm", 0, 0, 160)
    setPose("both", "up", "rightArm", 0, 0, 160)
    setPose("both", "up", "head", -20)
    setPose("both", "up", "body", -8)
end

Psych: a character's animations in its JSON, playAnim · Kade: playAnim

docs.title: setSkin
docs.text:
setSkin(who, skin)

A fighter's Minecraft skin: a 64x64 skin .png from the song folder, "opponent" / "player" (that fighter's own skin), or "" (back to its own).

setSkin("player", "opponent")       -- the fighters wear each other's skin
setSkin("opponent", "player")

Psych: the "Change Character" event · Kade: changeDadCharacter

docs.title: setModel
docs.text:
setModel(who, model)

The arm shape: "slim" (Alex), "wide" (Steve) or "default" (what the skin says).

setModel("both", "slim")

docs.title: bind
docs.text:
bind(who, place)bind(who, x, y[, height])unbind(who)

A place: bind(who, "bf") puts a fighter on Boyfriend's place (in front, bottom right - the camera stands behind it), "dad" on the opponent's (far, left); the other fighter takes the other place. The camera never moves for it, and focus, atPlace and everything that asks for a place follow it.

A spot on the screen: bind(who, x, y[, height]) pins a fighter like a sprite: its feet at x, y (shares of the screen, 0-1), and with height that tall as a share of the screen. The same as setting pinned, screenX, screenY, screenHeight.

unbind(who) lets go of both: back on the fight's own places (you in front), off the screen spot.

-- The Boyfriend part always in front, whichever side the one watching plays.
function onStart()
    bind("boyfriend", "bf")
end

-- Like a Psych stage: Boyfriend bottom right, the opponent bottom left, half the screen tall.
bind("boyfriend", 0.8, 0.98, 0.5)
bind("dad", 0.22, 0.98, 0.5)

Psych: a stage's boyfriend / opponent positions, setCharacterX

docs.title: setShaderFloat
docs.text:
setShaderFloat(slot, "name", value)

Sets a uniform float / int / bool of the song's shader in that slot - the way Psych scripts drive a .frag file. Up to 16 names per slot; a name the shader doesn't declare does nothing. A value that isn't set is 0, except iTime, which runs with the song's seconds.

function onStart()
    shader[0].file = "chroma.frag"
    setShaderFloat(0, "intensity", 0.5)
end

function onBeat(b)
    setShaderFloat(0, "intensity", 1.5)
end

Psych: setShaderFloat(tag, name, value) - with the slot instead of the tag

docs.title: setHealth
docs.text:
setHealth(share)addHealth(share)

Your health bar: setHealth sets it (1 = full, 0 = empty, which fails you), addHealth changes it by that share of the bar - minus drains, plus heals. fights Practice has no health, so these do nothing there.

-- Health drain: the opponent's notes take a little, but never the last bit.
function onOpponentHit(n)
    if player.health > 0.1 then addHealth(-0.01) end
end

Psych: setHealth / addHealth · Read it as player.health

docs.title: Sound
docs.text: The sounds themselves start with the actions playSound and loopSound - see Sounds and music.

docs.title: stopSound
docs.text:
stopSound("name")

Stops the sound started under that name.

stopSound("rain")

Psych: stopSound(tag)

docs.title: soundVolume
docs.text:
soundVolume("name", volume[, duration])

Fades a named sound to that volume (0-1). At once without a duration.

soundVolume("rain", 0, beats(4))

Psych: soundFadeIn / soundFadeOut / setSoundVolume

docs.title: trigger
docs.text:
trigger("Event Name"[, value1[, value2]])

Runs that event's onEvent right now, as if the chart had it here. The values are text, like a chart's. A name the song doesn't have does nothing - the event log says so once, with the name it probably should have been.

function onSection(n)
    if n == 16 then trigger("Hide HUD", "0", "1") end   -- a built-in event, with its chart values
end

Psych: triggerEvent(name, value1, value2)

docs.title: call
docs.text:
call("name"[, values...])callIn("Event Name", "name"[, values...])

call runs your function of that name in every other event of the song that has one, with up to 6 values. callIn runs it in one event only, picked by its name or alias - an event added later with a function of the same name doesn't join in. Calls can go 64 deep.

call("bigHit", 2)                  -- every event with a function bigHit(strength) runs it
callIn("Impact", "hit", 1.5)       -- only the Impact event's hit(1.5)

Psych: callOnLuas(name, args)

docs.title: preload
docs.text:
preload("picture.png")

Starts loading a picture now, so it shows the moment you first use it. Put it in onStart.

function onStart()
    preload("stage/fire.png")
end

Psych: precacheImage

docs.title: inspect
docs.text:
inspect("property")

Writes to the event log what a property is right now and why: its value and default, its range and unit, which event set it, the tween moving it, and what other events wrote under it. "strum[2].x" for one slot. The answer to "why is my HUD invisible?".

function onSection(n)
    if n == 8 then inspect("hud.alpha") end
end

The chart editor's State panel shows the same for every property at the playhead, without a script.

docs.title: What a shortcut changes
docs.text:
Every shortcut is made of properties - the same ones you can set yourself. That matters when you mix them with your own code: the last thing that sets a property wins. So hideHud() and a tween(hud.alpha, ...) of your own at the same time fight each other.

Shortcut Changes flipScroll, setScroll strums.scroll, strum[lane].scroll hideStrums, showStrums strums.alpha hideLane, showLane strum[lane].alpha moveStrums strums.x, strums.y hideHud, showHud hud.alpha hideJudgments, showJudgments judgments.alpha flash flash.color, flash.alpha fadeOut, fadeIn screen.color, screen.alpha zoom camera.zoom shake camera.shake focus camera.x, camera.z, camera.yaw swapFighters player. / opponent. x, y, z, turn pose, setSkin, setModel player.pose, .skin, .model (and the same for opponent.) setPose, clearPose no property - the fighter's pose designs bind, unbind player.place / opponent.place, or .pinned, .screenX, .screenY, .screenHeight setShaderFloat the shader's own values (not shader[n].a ... d) inspect nothing - it only writes to the log setHealth, addHealth your health (read it as player.health) stopSound, soundVolume only the named sound trigger, call, callIn whatever the event or function they run changes preload nothing - it only loads

docs.title: song
docs.text:
What kind of run this is (practice, a fight, a replay, someone watching), how far the song is, and who's singing right now. Read only.

How to use it

Read only. For a script that should only run in some modes there's also the only key of the event header: only = "fight" / only = "practice".

Time, beat, step and BPM are the built-in values time, beat, step, bpm.

Psych: songLength, getSongPosition(), mustHitSection, isStoryMode · Kade: songPos

docs.title: Example code
docs.text:
-- The camera moves only in fights; practice stays calm.
function onBeat(b)
    if song.mode == "fight" then
        camera.yaw = b % 2 == 0 ? 2 : -2
    end
end

docs.title: strum[lane]
docs.text:
One of your four lanes: its receptor, its notes and its holds. This is where modcharts happen - move a lane, spin it, fade it, change where its notes come from.

How to use it

strum[0] = left, strum[1] = down, strum[2] = up, strum[3] = right - also in loops: for i = 0, 3 do strum[i].alpha = 0.5 end. Everything adds to the whole strumline's values (strums).

Two offsets: x / y and wobbleX / wobbleY add up. Let one effect own x (a sway, a slide) and another wobble (a jiggle on the beat) and they don't fight - setting a property stops a tween on it.

Shortcuts: hideLane / showLane, flipScroll, resetLanes. Recipes: Modcharts.

Psych: setPropertyFromGroup('playerStrums', i, 'x', ...), noteTweenX · Kade: receptor, setActorX

docs.title: Example code
docs.text:
-- Every lane sways on its own, a beat apart.
function onFrame(dt)
    for i = 0, 3 do
        strum[i].x = 20 * sin(time / 300 + i)
    end
end

docs.title: window
docs.text:
The game window itself: move it, size it, shake it, take its frame away - or make it see-through, so the whole song plays right on the desktop.

How to use it

window is always there - while a song plays. Positions and sizes count from where the window was when the song started, so a script works on every screen. When the song ends (or on pause) the window goes back home by itself; resetWindow([duration]) does it earlier.

  • Not everywhere: moving and placing need a system that lets programs place windows (not Wayland); transparent (desktop mode) is Windows only. The player can switch all of it off (Options › MineFunkin › Window & desktop › "Let songs use windows"). Read canPlace, canSeeThrough, status to know what really happens.
  • Pop-out windows (parts of the game in windows of their own): popout. The monitor's size: monitor.

The whole picture: Game window and pop-outs.

    tween(window.height, 0.5, beats(2), "cubicInOut")
    tween(window.x, 300, beats(4), "sineInOut")
    after(beats(8), function() resetWindow(beats(2)) end)
end

docs.title: Event scripts
docs.text:
A flash on the drop. Lanes spinning. Notes riding in on a wave. The camera swinging round, your opponent growing three times taller, a whole stage appearing behind the fighters, the game window shaking when you miss. In MineFunkin, every one of those is an event script: a small text file ending in .event, sitting right next to the song.

Even the built-in events - Screen Shake, HUD Bounce, Scroll Speed and the rest - are just such files. So a song can bring its own events, swap a built-in one for its own version, or listen to the whole song (every beat, every hit, every miss) without a single chart event, the way a Psych Engine song script does.

Here's how small one can be:

format 1.1

event { name = "Big Drop" }

function onEvent(p)
    flash()                -- a white flash
    zoom(1.15)             -- zoom in and stay there
    flipScroll()           -- downscroll becomes upscroll
end

Save it as big_drop.event in a song's folder, place Big Drop in the chart editor, done. Those three calls are shortcuts - one line for the stuff charts do all the time. Once you want more than that, you build it from properties, tween and callbacks, and the pages below show you how.

docs.title: Learn it in this order
docs.text:
You don't have to read everything. Go through the first four, then jump to whatever you want to build.

  1. Your first event - from an empty file to a working event, step by step.
  2. Templates - working files to copy and fill in.
  3. In the chart editor - placing events and setting their values.
  4. Song scripts - react to every beat, hit and miss of a song.
  5. Then pick what you need: modcharts, stages and sprites, the fight camera, the fighters, effects, shaders, sounds, the game window.

Coming from Psych or Kade? The Psych Engine and Kade Engine pages go through their APIs name by name and tell you what it's called here. Rather copy something that already works? Have a look at the cookbook, or take apart the Event Showcase - a whole song built to show off every feature. Stuck? Check the FAQ and errors and fixes; most problems are in there.

And whenever you need to look up a name, the Event API has every single one, each with an example.

docs.title: Three ways a script can run
docs.text:
How it works For example As a chart event You place it in the chart editor; onEvent runs when the song gets there. a flash on the drop As a song script No chart event at all: its onBeat, onHit, onFrame, ... run for the whole song. a modchart, a stage, a combo counter As a replacement Give your file the name of a built-in event, and the song uses yours instead. your own Screen Shake

In practice most events are a bit of both: onEvent flips a mode on or off, and onBeat or onFrame do the actual work while it's on. Song scripts goes into that.

docs.title: Where your files go
docs.text:
Put them in the song's folder, or in an events/ folder inside it. That's it - MineFunkin doesn't look anywhere else. The chart editor shows you the built-in events plus the files of the song you're editing, and never the files of other songs. If you change a file while the editor is open, press Reload at the bottom of the inspector.

When a server has a song, its event files travel along with it, so everybody plays the same thing.

If two of your files use the same name, the one that comes first alphabetically wins, and the editor tells you about the other one.

docs.title: Practice, fights, replays
docs.text:
Your events run everywhere the song does: practice at the Retro TV, fights at a Speaker (against the dummy or a real player), when someone watches a fight from inside, and in replays.

A few things only make sense with a real world around you - the fight camera, a stage painted onto the world, outlines around the fighters, effects on the world only, and health. They're marked fights wherever they show up. The fighters themselves work in practice too: there they're the two puppets next to the lanes.

If an event only belongs in one place, say so in its header with only = "fight", or check song.mode in the code. Song scripts shows both.

docs.title: Is this safe?
docs.text:
Yes - and on purpose. When you download a song from somebody, its scripts can only use what's in this wiki. They can't read or write your files (pictures, sounds and shaders come from the song's own folder only), they can't go on the internet, and they're stopped if they try to do too much work at once (limits).

A file with a mistake in it never runs at all. Instead the chart editor shows you the line, the column and, most of the time, a "did you mean ...?" - and the same goes into the event log.

docs.title: The fight camera
docs.text:
In a fight - at a Speaker, against the dummy or a real player - you watch the world through MineFunkin's fight camera. It stands just behind your fighter, with the opponent out ahead, and it's been tuned to frame the two of you nicely. Your scripts get to move it on top of that picture: lean over, push in, swing round, tilt for drama.

Practice at the Retro TV has no world, so there the camera properties simply do nothing. Nothing breaks - they're just ignored.

Eight properties move it: camera.x, .y, .z (in blocks), .yaw, .pitch, .roll (in degrees), .fov (the lens) and .nudge (how much it follows your hits). Defaults, ranges and the details are on the camera page.

One thing worth knowing before you start: "right" and "forward" belong to the fight, not to wherever the camera is looking right now. Forward is the way the camera looks when it's at home. So camera.z = 2 always moves towards the fight, however far you've turned camera.yaw. That makes moves much easier to combine.

camera.zoom, camera.bump and camera.shake work in fights too - the zoom and the beat pop zoom the world along with the HUD.

docs.title: The quick way: focus
docs.text:
A camera that drifts over to whoever's singing takes one line:

focus("opponent")            -- lean towards the opponent (over one beat)
focus("player", beats(2))    -- towards you, over two beats
focus("center")              -- back to the middle
focus("dad")                 -- towards whoever plays the opponent part, wherever they stand

focus moves camera.x, camera.z and camera.yaw a little - just a lean, not a jump. Pair it with song.singer and the camera follows the song by itself:

function onBeat(b)
    if song.singer == "opponent" then
        focus("opponent")
    elseif song.singer == "player" then
        focus("player")
    end
end

docs.title: Calming it down: camera.nudge
docs.text: On every hit, the fight camera pans a tiny bit towards the note's direction. It makes playing feel punchy, but it also gets in the way of your own camera moves. camera.nudge = 0 switches it off - for a calm part, or while your script is steering. camera.nudge = 2 makes it twice as strong, if you want more punch.

docs.title: Putting it back
docs.text:
Whatever you did, there's a way home:

resetCamera()                          -- at once
resetCamera(beats(2))                  -- gliding home over two beats
reset(camera, beats(1), "backOut")     -- the same, with an easing of your choice

resetCamera resets everything above (camera.nudge too), plus camera.zoom and camera.shake. And when the song ends, the camera goes home on its own - you can't leave anybody stuck in a weird angle.

docs.title: Recipes
docs.text:
Look over at the opponent. They stand ahead and to the left, so turn left a little and narrow the lens:

tween(camera.yaw, -6, beats(1), "sineInOut")
tween(camera.fov, -8, beats(1), "sineInOut")

From down low. Drop the camera, tilt it up, widen the lens - everybody looks taller and more dramatic:

camera.y = -1.2
camera.pitch = 12
camera.fov = 10

A slow push in, for a tense moment:

tween(camera.z, 1.5, beats(8), "sineInOut")
tween(camera.fov, -6, beats(8), "sineInOut")

A handheld camera that drifts around without ever jittering (that's what noise is for):

function onFrame(dt)
    camera.yaw = noise(time / 900) * 1.5
    camera.pitch = noise(time / 1100 + 40) * 1
    camera.roll = noise(time / 1300 + 80) * 1
end

A Dutch angle on every beat:

local side = 1

function onBeat(b)
    side = -side
    tween(camera.roll, side * 6, beats(0.5), "backOut")
end

Circling the fighters. If you only turn the camera, the fighters slide out of the picture. Move and turn together, and a point stays right in the middle. For a point d blocks straight ahead, turning by a degrees means moving to x = -d * sin(a), z = d * (1 - cos(a)):

local function orbit(angle, d)
    local a = angle * pi / 180
    camera.yaw = angle
    camera.x = -d * sin(a)
    camera.z = d * (1 - cos(a))
end

Swing it round the point between the fighters - pulling back and rising a little as it goes - and both of them stay in view:

Which way to swing

Your fighter stands close to the camera. Swing towards the side where the opponent ends up behind your fighter (with the default layout: negative angles, around -25°) and the opponent vanishes behind your back. Swing the other way, and you see both side by side.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• The camera only moves in your picture. The other fighter and everyone watching see their own.
  • Walls behind your fighter are still hidden (the camera looks past them), with or without your scripts.
  • Shader packs (Iris) work with a moved camera like with any other.
  • Players with Less motion switched on (Options › MineFunkin › Accessibility) get no nudge on hits, no beat pop and no shake. Your other camera moves still play - so make sure the song still reads well without the shaking.

docs.title: Cookbook
docs.text:
Small recipes to steal. Each one is complete and tested: put it in a file under a format 1.1 line and an event { name = "..." }, and it works. Recipes that need a chart event use onEvent; the others are song scripts that run for the whole song.

Click one open, copy it, change the numbers until it feels right. That's really all there is to it.

docs.title: Camera and HUD
docs.text:
Zoom pop on every downbeat 
function onBeat(b)
    if b % 4 == 0 then
        camera.bump += 0.035
    end
end
A slow zoom that stays 
params {
    zoom = number { from = "value1", default = 1.15, min = 0.5, max = 2, step = 0.05 },
    length = number { from = "value2", default = 4, min = 0, max = 32, step = 0.5, label = "Beats" },
}

function onEvent(p)
    tween(camera.zoom, p.zoom, beats(p.length), "sineInOut")
end

The shortcut for the same: zoom(p.zoom, beats(p.length)).

Shake on a hard hit 
function onEvent(p)
    camera.shake = 0.012
    tween(camera.shake, 0, beats(1), "quadOut")
end

Or with the shortcut: shake(0.012, beats(1)).

The playfield rocks with the beat 
local side = 1

function onBeat(b)
    side = -side
    hud.angle = side * 3
    tween(hud.angle, 0, beats(1), "quadOut")
end

docs.title: Flashes and colours
docs.text:
Red flash on a miss 
function onMiss(note)
    flash.color = #FF3040
    flash.alpha = 0.3
    tween(flash.alpha, 0, beats(0.5), "quadOut")
end
Cut to black and back 
params {
    hold = number { from = "value1", default = 2, min = 0, max = 16, step = 0.5, label = "Beats black" },
}

function onEvent(p)
    screen.color = #000000
    screen.alpha = 1
    after(beats(p.hold), function()
        tween(screen.alpha, 0, beats(1))
    end)
end

With the shortcuts: fadeOut(#000000, 0), then fadeIn(beats(1)) in the after.

Strum background in the colour of the last judgment 
function onHit(note)
    local c = note.judgment == "sick" ? #5CF2FF : note.judgment == "good" ? #5CFF8F : #FFB547
    underlay.color = c
    underlay.alpha = 0.8
    tween(underlay.color, #000000, beats(1))
    tween(underlay.alpha, 0.65, beats(1))
end

docs.title: Text
docs.text:
A line of lyrics that fades in and out 
params {
    line = text { from = "value1", label = "Line" },
    length = number { from = "value2", default = 4, min = 1, max = 16, step = 1, label = "Beats" },
}

local shown = 0

function onEvent(p)
    shown += 1
    local mine = shown
    text[7].value = p.line ?? ""
    text[7].y = 0.82
    text[7].alpha = 0
    tween(text[7].alpha, 1, beats(0.25))
    after(beats(p.length), function()
        if shown == mine then tween(text[7].alpha, 0, beats(0.5)) end
    end)
end

The counter makes sure a newer line isn't faded out by an older one's timer.

Live accuracy in a corner 
function onFrame(dt)
    text[3].value = round(player.accuracy * 10) / 10 .. " %"
    text[3].align = "right"
    text[3].x = 0.97
    text[3].y = 0.92
    text[3].size = 0.8
end
Combo shout every 50 
local next = 50

function onHit(note)
    if player.combo >= next then
        text[4].value = next .. " COMBO!"
        text[4].y = 0.6
        text[4].size = 1.6
        text[4].alpha = 1
        tween(text[4].size, 1.1, beats(0.5), "backOut")
        tween(text[4].alpha, 0, beats(1.5), "quadIn")
        next += 50
    end
end

function onMiss(note)
    next = 50
end

docs.title: Lanes
docs.text:
Lanes light up when they're pressed 
function onFrame(dt)
    for lane = 0, 3 do
        strum[lane].scale = strum[lane].pressed ? 1.12 : 1
    end
end
The opponent's notes shake your lanes 
function onOpponentHit(note)
    strum[note.lane].wobbleY = -10
    tween(strum[note.lane].wobbleY, 0, beats(0.5), "elasticOut")
end
Slow down, then speed up 
function onEvent(p)
    scrollTo(0.6, beats(2))
    after(beats(4), function() scrollTo(1.4, beats(1)) end)
end

More in Modcharts and strum[lane].

docs.title: Fighters (fights only)
docs.text:
Both fighters bounce on every beat 
function onBeat(b)
    for who = 0, 1 do
        puppet[who].squash = 0.18
        tween(puppet[who].squash, 0, beats(0.8), "elasticOut")
    end
end
The opponent flinches when you hit a sick 
function onHit(note)
    if note.judgment != "sick" then return end
    opponent.pitch = -8
    tween(opponent.pitch, 0, beats(0.5), "backOut")
end
The opponent turns red as your combo grows 
function onFrame(dt)
    local heat = min(1, player.combo / 100)
    opponent.color = mix(#FFFFFF, #FF4040, heat)
end

More in The fighters.

docs.title: Sound
docs.text:
A sound on the drop 
function onEvent(p)
    playSound("impact.ogg", 0.8)   -- a file in the song folder or events/
    camera.bump += 0.08
end
The opponent's voice drops out for a bar 
function onEvent(p)
    tween(volume.opponent, 0, beats(0.5))
    after(beats(4), function() tween(volume.opponent, 1, beats(0.5)) end)
end

docs.title: The game window
docs.text:
More in Game window and pop-outs.

The window shakes on every miss 
function onMiss(note)
    window.x = 14
    tween(window.x, 0, beats(0.5), "elasticOut")
end
The judgments in a window of their own, floating above the game 
function onEvent(p)
    popout[0].show = "judgments"
    tween(popout[0].y, -260, beats(2), "sineInOut")
end
Each lane flies out into its own window and circles the screen 
local circling = false

function onEvent(p)
    popout[0].show = "left"
    popout[1].show = "down"
    popout[2].show = "up"
    popout[3].show = "right"
    circling = true
    after(beats(16), function()
        circling = false
        resetWindow(beats(2))    -- glide home, then close
    end)
end

function onFrame(dt)
    if not circling then return end
    for i = 0, 3 do
        local a = time / 1000 + i * pi / 2
        popout[i].x = cos(a) * 300
        popout[i].y = sin(a) * 150
    end
end

docs.title: In the chart editor
docs.text:
The chart editor is where your events meet the song. Open it at a Retro TV (› Editor), pick a song, and you're in.

Here's the nice bit: you never have to tell the editor about your events. It reads everything from the event's own file - the name, the colour, the category, the description, and the controls for its parameters. Write a file, press Reload, and it's there.

The first time you open the editor, a short help pops up with the basics. You can get it back any time with ? Help in the tool bar.

docs.title: Finding your way around
docs.text: Part What it's for Document bar (top) Back, the song and difficulty (its menu lets you switch difficulty, copy events from another difficulty, or add a new one), whether you have unsaved changes, Undo, Redo, Save. Tool bar The tool (Select / Place / Erase), play / pause and the time, bar.beat and the BPM, the snap, the zoom, ? Help. Overview strip The whole song at a glance: its waveform, every event as a tick, BPM changes, and the box showing what the grid shows right now. Click or drag to jump; hover to see the time. Grid The bar ruler, the opponent's lanes, your lanes, and the EVENTS lane: four cells wide, with a single marker's name written next to it, and "+N" when a row holds more than fits. Inspector (right) Whatever you've selected - an event, a BPM change, notes - or the stamp (the next event you'll place). Too narrow? Drag its left edge. Footer The song's event files, ⚠ N (files that can't be used, unknown events), State, Reload. Status line (bottom) The keys for whatever the mouse is over, and what just happened.

docs.title: The three tools
docs.text:
Tool Key Click on an empty cell Click on something Select 1 lets go of the selection selects it Place 2 a note (note lanes) or the stamp's event (EVENTS lane); drag down for a hold selects it Erase 3 - deletes it (drag to delete several)

A right-click deletes, whatever tool you're holding. And with Place, you see a ghost of the next note or event before you click, so there are no surprises.

docs.title: Placing and editing events
docs.text:
1. With nothing selected, the inspector shows the stamp - the event Place will add. Pick its type: the picker searches names, categories and descriptions, can show only built-in events or only this song's, and tells you what the hovered one does right beside the list.
  2. Set its parameters.
  3. Take the Place tool and click the EVENTS lane where it should happen. Changed your mind? Drag the marker.

Click an event to select it, and the inspector shows it as SELECTED EVENT: its parameters as controls, plus Jump to, Use as stamp and Delete. Every change goes straight back into the event's value1 and value2, and each one is a single undo step (dragging a slider counts once, when you let go).

Selecting an event leaves your stamp alone - if you want to place more of the same, press Use as stamp. And if you change a selected event's type, its settings are converted: whatever both types share is kept, the rest starts at its default.

Colour settings have a swatch - click it for a row of colours (and "not set"). A setting that isn't at its default is drawn brighter, so you can see at a glance what you changed. Hover a setting's name for its kind, range and default.

Raw values, folded away at the bottom of the event view, shows value1 and value2 as plain text. That's the Psych Engine format, and it's what ends up in the chart file. An event without a file behind it (from a converted chart, or a file you deleted) shows up grey with just its raw values. Don't worry - it's kept and saved exactly as it was.

docs.title: When something's wrong
docs.text:
⚠ N in the footer opens a list of everything that doesn't work:

  • Errors - a song file that can't be used, with the line, the column, the message, and what that means in the game.
  • Warnings - a file that broke after it had worked. The editor keeps using the last working version until you fix it, so your song doesn't fall apart while you type.
  • Unknown events - chart events that no file answers to, how often they're in the chart, and Jump to the next one.

Copy puts a message on the clipboard (handy when you ask someone for help). Reload reads the song folder again: change a file in your text editor, save, press Reload. Everything here also goes into logs/minefunkin-events.log.

docs.title: State: what your scripts did up to here
docs.text:
Ever wondered why the HUD is upside down at bar 40? State in the footer answers that. It runs the song's scripts from the start up to the playhead - just like the game would, only nobody's playing - and lists every property that isn't at its default there, grouped (CAMERA, HUD, LANES, ...).

Click a row to see which event set it, the tween that's moving it, and what other events wrote under it. The filter field narrows the list down. Pause somewhere else and it works it all out again. Things it can't show (sounds, health, the window) are listed at the end.

It's the same answer inspect writes to the log during a song.

docs.title: Saving
docs.text:
Save (or Ctrl+S) writes the chart. The bar tells you whether you have unsaved changes, that it saved, or that saving failed (hover it to see why). If you press Back, switch difficulty or add one with unsaved changes, the editor asks once: save and go on, throw the changes away, or stay.

Editing a server's song also sends it to the server. The status line tells you whether that got going - the server doesn't answer back, so the editor won't pretend to know more than that.

docs.title: Keys
docs.text:
Key 1 / 2 / 3 Select / Place / Erase Space play / pause ← / → step back / forward (on a focused slider: change it) [ / ] coarser / finer snap Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y undo / redo Ctrl+S save Ctrl+wheel zoom the grid Tab / Shift+Tab move between controls; Enter presses Esc close a popup, then the problems / state panel, then clear the selection, then leave the editor

In the note lanes: drag to select, drag down while placing to make a hold, hold Alt to place between the snap cells. With notes selected: drag to move them, drag a tail to change the hold, H marks a forced miss, Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V copy and paste at the playhead.

docs.title: Effects (fx)
docs.text:
Sometimes a song needs the whole picture to change: the colour drains out on a sad part, the screen glitches when the villain shows up, everything goes pixelated on the drop. That's what fx is for - built-in effects laid over the picture, no shader writing needed.

There are sixteen of them: grayscale, sepia, invert, hue, saturation, contrast, brightness, chromatic, blur, pixelate, wave, glitch, scanlines, grain, bulge and bloom, plus fx.target to choose what they cover. What each number means is on fx.

They only run while the song plays - never over the pause menu or the results, so nobody has to read a menu through a glitch. And they're all off by default. While none is on, nothing is computed at all, so they cost you nothing until you use them.

docs.title: Screen, world or terrain
docs.text:
This is the clever part: you decide what gets the effect.

fx.target What gets the effect "screen" (default) everything: the world, the HUD, the strumline, your texts and pictures "world" only the world - the notes and the HUD stay sharp, so even a heavy effect stays playable "terrain" the world without the two fighters: everything around them changes, they stay as they are

"world" and "terrain" need a fight. Practice at the Retro TV has no world, so there they do nothing.

The same fx.pixelate = 8, fx.hue = 150 twice. Left, "world": the arrows and the score stay crisp. Right, "screen": everything gets pixelated.

-- The world turns into an old photo, the two of you stay in colour.
function onEvent(p)
    fx.target = "terrain"
    tween(fx.sepia, 1, beats(2), "sineInOut")
end

With "terrain", anything that stands in front of a fighter (a block, an arrow) gets the effect like the rest of the world - only the fighters themselves are spared, with their armour, cape and shadow. One small catch: they're drawn over the finished world, so while a "terrain" effect runs, rain and particles don't show in front of them, and water in front of a fighter hides it.

docs.title: Switching off
docs.text:
When the moment's over:

resetFx()            -- everything off at once, the target back to "screen"
resetFx(beats(1))    -- fades out (the target stays until it's gone)

Your own shaders count too: resetFx switches them off as well. And when the song ends, everything goes off by itself.

docs.title: Recipes
docs.text:
A punch on every miss. The colour drains and the picture splits for a moment - the player feels that miss:

function onMiss(note)
    fx.chromatic = 8
    fx.saturation = 0
    tween(fx.chromatic, 0, beats(0.5), "quadOut")
    tween(fx.saturation, 1, beats(0.5), "quadOut")
end

An old tape that never quite sits still:

local active = false

function onEvent(p)
    active = true
    fx.scanlines = 0.7
    fx.grain = 0.35
    fx.sepia = 0.3
end

function onFrame(dt)
    if not active then return end
    fx.wave = 1 + 2.5 * abs(noise(time / 700))
end

A glitch burst for half a beat, for when something goes very wrong:

fx.glitch = 1
fx.chromatic = 10
fx.pixelate = 6
tween(fx.glitch, 0, beats(0.5), "quadIn")
tween(fx.chromatic, 0, beats(0.5), "quadOut")
tween(fx.pixelate, 0, beats(0.5), "expoOut")

Drained of colour, and back again:

tween(fx.saturation, 0.15, beats(2))
tween(fx.contrast, 1.25, beats(2))
-- later:
tween(fx.saturation, 1, beats(1))
tween(fx.contrast, 1, beats(1))

Colours walking round the wheel, slowly, forever:

function onFrame(dt)
    fx.hue += 40 * dt / beats(1)   -- 40 degrees per beat
end

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• MineFunkin draws the effects itself, on top of Minecraft's own picture. So they get along fine with shader packs (Iris): the pack draws the world, your effects go on top.
  • The order: your own shaders by slot, then the built-in effects. With several targets in use, "terrain" comes first, then "world", then "screen" - each one works on what the one before it left behind.
  • Players with Fewer flashes switched on (Options › MineFunkin › Accessibility) get invert and glitch at 0.3 at most and brightness at 1.3 at most. The rest of your effect stays as it is.
  • Heavy effects over the notes (pixelate, wave, glitch, blur) make a song really hard to read. Keep them short, put them where the player has a break - or just use "world", which leaves the notes alone.

docs.title: The fighters
docs.text:
The two fighters are the stars of every song - so of course you can play with them. Move them, turn them, squash them like jelly, paint them red, make one three times taller, swap their places mid-song, or take over their animation completely and choreograph your own dance.

player is you (the one the camera looks over), opponent is the other one. puppet[0] and puppet[1] are the same two by number, which comes in handy in loops and functions.

Here's the important bit: all of this happens only in your own picture. The real players don't move an inch, and nobody else (your opponent, the people watching) sees it. That's what makes it safe to go wild. The one exception is poses a song designs with setPose - those, the players standing around see too.

In practice (the Retro TV) there's no world, but the two puppets next to the lanes follow most of it: position, size, squash, turn, tint, poses, body parts, pinning and skins. Outlines, clipping, depth and facing only work in fights.

There's also boyfriend and dad: the same two fighters, but named by the chart's sides - see Places and fighter names.

docs.title: The whole fighter
docs.text:
Both fighters have the same set of properties - position and turn (in blocks and degrees), scale, squash, color, alpha, visible, animate, pose, skin, model, the pinning ones, outlines and clipping. Every one of them, with defaults and ranges, is on Fighters. What works for player. works the same for opponent. and puppet[i]..

Left: player.squash = 0.4, opponent.squash = -0.45. Right: opponent.color = #FF5050, .alpha = 0.55, .scale = 1.5, .turn = 40.

For the common moves there are one-liners: swapFighters(), pose("opponent", "up"), setSkin("player", "skins/bf.png"), setModel("both", "slim") - see Shortcuts.

docs.title: Pinned to the screen
docs.text:
In Psych, characters are sprites: you put them somewhere on the screen and that's where they are. A MineFunkin fighter normally stands where the fight puts it, and the camera looks at it. Pin it, and it behaves like a sprite instead: it stays on its spot on the screen, whatever the camera does.

  • screenX / screenY say where its feet are: 0.5, 0.9 = in the middle, near the bottom. Below 0 or above 1 is off the screen - that's how you slide it in from a side or bring it up from below.
  • Its size: screenHeight = how tall it is on the screen (1.4 = taller than the screen - feet below the bottom edge, from the hips up). Or depth = how far from the camera it stands, in blocks: near = big, and then the camera's zoom still makes it bigger or smaller. Both 0 = its own distance (your own fighter is close to the camera, the opponent far away).
  • facing = "camera" turns it to look straight at you, like a character sprite in the middle of a Psych stage.
  • homeX / homeY tell you where the fight would put it - start a slide from there and it doesn't jump.
  • x, y, z still move it on top. A pinned fighter has no shadow (it may stand anywhere).
  • pinned = false puts it back where the fight wants it, at once. Slide it back to homeX / homeY first if it should move there.
format 1.1
-- The opponent slides in from the right into the middle, then back where it belongs.
event { name = "Center Stage" }

function onEvent(p)
    opponent.pinned = true
    opponent.screenX = 1.3
    opponent.screenY = opponent.homeY
    tween(opponent.screenX, 0.5, beats(2), "cubicInOut")
    after(beats(8), function()
        tween(opponent.screenX, opponent.homeX, beats(2), "cubicInOut")
        after(beats(2), function() opponent.pinned = false end)
    end)
end

-- Big in the middle, from the hips up, looking at you.
opponent.pinned = true
opponent.screenX = 0.5
opponent.screenY = 1.45          -- feet below the bottom edge
opponent.screenHeight = 1.3
opponent.facing = "camera"

docs.title: Places: bind
docs.text:
A fight has two places: Boyfriend's ("bf", in front, bottom right, with the camera behind it) and the opponent's ("dad", further away, on the left). Normally you always stand in front - even when you play the opponent side, because the camera belongs behind you. But a song built like a classic stage might want Boyfriend's part in front, no matter who plays it. One line in onStart does that:

function onStart()
    bind("boyfriend", "bf")      -- Boyfriend's part in front, whichever side the one watching plays
end

Now if you play the opponent side, you stand far left, and the other fighter is the one in front of the camera. The camera itself doesn't move. player.place says where a fighter stands, atPlace("dad") gives the fighter on a place, and focus("dad") turns the camera to it. unbind("boyfriend") puts everyone back.

bind(who, x, y[, height]) pins a fighter to a spot on the screen instead - a shorter way to write the pinning above.

docs.title: Cut to a box: clip
docs.text:
clipLeft, clipTop, clipRight, clipBottom (shares of the screen) cut a fighter off outside a box. Perfect for a fighter inside a window frame, on a TV, or peeking through a rift in your stage art. Fights only.

-- Only inside the frame drawn at 0.3-0.7 x 0.2-0.8.
player.clipLeft = 0.3
player.clipRight = 0.7
player.clipTop = 0.2
player.clipBottom = 0.8

docs.title: Outlines
docs.text:
outlineAlpha draws a line around a fighter, in outlineColor and outlineWidth (pixels at 1080p, 0 = about 3). With outlineOnly = true the fighter itself disappears and only the outline is left - a silhouette drawn with a pen, like the creepy intro of a horror mod. Fights only.

-- Both of them as white outlines, fading in.
for i = 0, 1 do
    puppet[i].outlineOnly = true
    puppet[i].outlineAlpha = 0
    tween(puppet[i].outlineAlpha, 1, seconds(4))
end

A fighter who glows in the world (a potion, another mod) doesn't glow on your own fight screen - it would get in the way of the song's look. Everybody watching from outside still sees the glow, and it's back once the fight is over.

docs.title: Body parts
docs.text:
You can move every limb on its own. player.head, .body, .leftArm, .rightArm, .leftLeg and .rightLeg each have .pitch, .yaw, .roll (degrees), .x, .y, .z (model pixels, 16 = a block), .scale and .squash - what each one does is on Body parts.

"Right", "left" and "forward" are always the figure's own. You see your own fighter from behind, so its right is your right. The opponent faces you, so its right is on your left. Don't worry, it's simpler than it sounds: both arms at roll = 90 is a T-pose for either of them, and an arm straight up is roll around 165.

player.rightArm.roll = 90, player.leftArm.pitch = 90, player.head.pitch = 25; opponent.rightArm.roll = 160, opponent.leftLeg.pitch = 45, opponent.head.roll = 25.

-- A wave: the right arm goes up and swings.
player.rightArm.roll = 150
for i = 0, 3 do
    after(beats(i * 0.5), function()
        tween(player.rightArm.roll, i % 2 == 0 ? 120 : 160, beats(0.5), "sineInOut")
    end)
end
after(beats(2), function() resetPuppet("player", beats(0.5)) end)

docs.title: On top of the animation, or instead of it
docs.text:
Normally everything you set goes on top of MineFunkin's own animation. The idle, the note poses with their pop and rebound, the squash and stretch - all of that keeps running underneath, and your values are added to whatever the animation is doing right then.

Set animate = false and the animation stops: the fighter stands still in its rest pose, and your values are the whole pose. That's how you build your own moves:

local function armsUp(who)
    puppet[who].animate = false
    tween(puppet[who].leftArm.roll, 165, beats(0.25), "backOut")
    tween(puppet[who].rightArm.roll, 165, beats(0.25), "backOut")
    tween(puppet[who].head.pitch, -15, beats(0.25), "backOut")
end

function onEvent(p)
    armsUp(0)
    armsUp(1)
    after(beats(2), function() resetPuppet("both", beats(1)) end)
end

String eight moves like that together (clap, spread, reach, point, squat, kick, jump, spin), one per beat, have the opponent dance them mirrored, and you've got a whole routine:

docs.title: pose: MineFunkin's own poses
docs.text:
Want a fighter to strike a pose without a note? pose plays MineFunkin's poses exactly the way a note would:

Value "left", "down", "up", "right" Pops into that pose at the moment it's set and holds it, like a held note. "death" Plays the death: the fighter jolts back and sits down, and stays down. "none" Lets go: a held pose eases out like a released note, the death ends. The notes decide again.

Switching straight from one direction to another pops the new one. And while a pose is set, the notes leave it alone.

-- The opponent "sings" the chord with you, then drops.
opponent.pose = "left"
after(beats(1), function() opponent.pose = "right" end)
after(beats(2), function() opponent.pose = "death" end)
after(beats(6), function() opponent.pose = "none" end)

animate = false wins over pose: a fighter without animation stays in its rest pose.

docs.title: Your own poses: setPose
docs.text:
Don't like how the fighters pose? Give them your own. A song can replace MineFunkin's poses - the idle and each direction - and the notes play yours with MineFunkin's pop, hold and ease. You build a pose part by part, in degrees, just like player.head.pitch:

function onStart()
    -- "up": both arms high, head back.
    setPose("both", "up", "leftArm", 0, 0, 160)
    setPose("both", "up", "rightArm", 0, 0, 160)
    setPose("both", "up", "head", -20)
    -- "idle": hands on the hips.
    setPose("both", "idle", "leftArm", 0, 0, 35)
    setPose("both", "idle", "rightArm", 0, 0, 35)
end

The first call on a pose starts it from the rest pose, and every further call adds a part. clearPose("both", "up") gives back MineFunkin's own (clearPose("both") = all five). In a fight, the players standing around see your song's poses too. All the details: setPose.

docs.title: Skins: skin and model
docs.text:
A fighter can wear a different Minecraft skin for part of the song - a costume change, a fake-out, or the two swapping looks:

Value of player.skin "" its own skin (the default) "player", "opponent" that fighter's own skin - so the two can swap "skins/bf.png" a 64x64 Minecraft skin .png from the song folder (or its events/ or skins/ folder) 
-- Halfway through, the opponent turns into Boyfriend.
setSkin("opponent", "skins/bf.png")
setModel("opponent", "slim")

-- And the two swap looks:
setSkin("player", "opponent")
setSkin("opponent", "player")

model picks the arm shape: "slim" arms are 3 pixels wide (Alex), "wide" 4 (Steve). "default" goes with whatever the skin itself says. A song can use up to 8 skin files, 1 MB each. Like everything on this page, only you see the change - and in practice, the puppets wear it too.

docs.title: Squash and stretch with springy easings
docs.text:
player.squash = 0.4
tween(player.squash, 0, beats(1), "elasticOut")   -- lands like jelly

elasticOut, backOut and bounceOut overshoot and then settle - the same springy feel as the pop and rebound of MineFunkin's own poses. They make almost anything look more alive.

docs.title: Recipes
docs.text:
Squash on the kick:

function onBeat(b)
    player.squash = 0.22
    tween(player.squash, 0, beats(0.9), "elasticOut")
    after(beats(0.5), function()
        opponent.squash = 0.22
        tween(opponent.squash, 0, beats(0.9), "elasticOut")
    end)
end

Swap places. The shortcut does it in one line, with the two jumping past each other:

swapFighters(beats(1))     -- again = back

Or by hand, if you want your own jump: in the default fight layout the opponent stands 7.4 blocks ahead and 3 to the left of you. Move each fighter to the other's spot and turn it 180°, so they still face each other:

local function hop(who, x, z, turn)
    tween(puppet[who].x, x, beats(2), "sineInOut")
    tween(puppet[who].z, z, beats(2), "sineInOut")
    tween(puppet[who].turn, turn, beats(2), "sineInOut")
    tween(puppet[who].y, 2.5, beats(1), "quadOut")
    after(beats(1), function() tween(puppet[who].y, 0, beats(1), "quadIn") end)
end

function onEvent(p)
    hop(0, -3, 7.4, 180)
    hop(1, 3, -7.4, 180)
end

Float. Write .y and .roll every frame from sin(), and they bob around like they're underwater:

function onFrame(dt)
    local t = time / 1000
    player.y = 0.7 + 0.25 * sin(t * 1.7)
    player.roll = 7 * sin(t * 1.1)
    opponent.y = 0.9 + 0.3 * sin(t * 1.3 + 1)
end

A giant. Nothing says "boss fight" quite like it:

opponent.scale = 1
tween(opponent.scale, 2.2, beats(1.5), "elasticOut")

docs.title: Putting them back
docs.text:
resetPuppet("player")             -- at once
resetPuppet("opponent", beats(1)) -- over a beat
resetPuppet("both", beats(2))     -- or 0 / 1 for one of them

When the song ends, both go back on their own.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Armor, capes and head items follow the pose and the tint. Elytra and shoulder parrots don't follow the body parts.
  • A hidden fighter (visible = false, alpha = 0 or scale = 0) isn't drawn at all - it costs nothing.
  • Two things writing the same property every frame fight each other: the later one wins, and setting a property stops a tween on it. Give each effect its own properties.

docs.title: Coming from Kade Engine
docs.text:
Kade Engine modcharts are a modchart.lua per song with hooks (start, update, beatHit, ...), receptors and characters addressed by number, and global variables like camHudAngle. Good news: MineFunkin's modcharts work the same way - a song script with callbacks - so most of a Kade modchart translates line by line.

This page maps the names (Kade Engine 1.4-1.8's modchart API), and at the end translates all of Kade's own example modcharts, so you can see a few whole ones side by side.

docs.title: The big differences
docs.text:
Five things to keep in mind - they'll save you some head-scratching:

  • No compiling. A Kade modchart needs a game built from source. Here the script is just a .event file in the song's folder, and the chart editor's Reload picks up your changes while you work. No waiting for a build.
