  • Your four lanes, not eight receptors. Kade numbers the receptors 0-7 (0-3 the opponent's, 4-7 yours). MineFunkin's strum[0] ... strum[3] are your lanes - Kade's 4-7. In a fight only yours are on screen; in practice the opponent's receptors beside them fade with strums.opponentAlpha.
  • Offsets, not positions. setActorX(x, 4) puts receptor 4 at screen position x. strum[0].x = 30 moves lane 0 30 pixels away from its home. So Kade's defaultStrum4X + 30 is just 30 here, and 0 is home.
  • Milliseconds. onFrame(dt) gets milliseconds (Kade's elapsed is seconds), time is the song time in ms. Durations are written beats(2), seconds(1).
  • The characters are Minecraft players. boyfriend is player, dad is opponent - the real fighters in the world, in a fight. There's no girlfriend; a picture on the stage can play her part.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text: Kade MineFunkin start(song) onStart() update(elapsed) onFrame(dt) - dt in ms beatHit(beat) onBeat(b) stepHit(step) onStep(n) keyPressed(key) onKeyPress(lane) - the lane 0-3, not "left" / "down" / ... playerOneSing(note, position) onHit(note) playerTwoSing(note, position) onOpponentHit(note) playerOneMiss(note, position) onMiss(note) playerOneTurn() / playerTwoTurn() read song.singer ("player" / "opponent") in onBeat

docs.title: Receptors
docs.text: Kade MineFunkin setActorX(x, i) / getActorX(i) strum[lane].x (an offset from home) setActorY(y, i) / getActorY(i) strum[lane].y setActorAngle(a, i) / getActorAngle(i) strum[lane].angle setActorAlpha(a, i) strum[lane].alpha (or hideLane / showLane) setActorScale(s, i) strum[lane].scale defaultStrum4X ... defaultStrum7Y 0 - the home of every offset; strums.spacing is the distance between two lanes receptor.defaultX / defaultY (1.8's objects) strum[lane].homeX / homeY - where the receptor rests on the screen, in pixels tweenPos(i, x, y, time) tween(strum[lane].x, x, seconds(time)) + the same for .y tweenAngle(i, angle, time) tween(strum[lane].angle, angle, seconds(time)) tweenFadeIn(i, alpha, time) / tweenFadeOut tween(strum[lane].alpha, alpha, seconds(time)) tweenPosXAngle / tweenPosYAngle two tweens: .x (or .y) and .angle setActorVelocityX, setActorAccelerationX, setActorDragX no physics - work the position out in onFrame from time, or tween it setStrumlineY(y) / strumLineY strums.y strumLine1Visible = false strums.opponentAlpha = 0 (practice) strumLine2Visible = false strums.alpha = 0 (or hideStrums)

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: Kade MineFunkin getRenderedNotes() notes.count - see notes one by one getRenderedNoteX(i), getRenderedNoteY(i) note[i].distance (ms until the hit) - positions are worked out from that getRenderedNoteType(i) note[i].lane getRenderedNoteStrumtime(i) note[i].time isSustain(i), note.isSustain note[i].hold > 0 note.beat (1.8's objects) note[i].beat setRenderedNotePos(x, y, i) note[i].x, note[i].y - offsets, set every frame setRenderedNoteAlpha(a, i) note[i].alpha setRenderedNoteScale(s, i) note[i].scale setRenderedNoteAngle(a, i) note[i].angle createWiggle(freq, amplitude, speed) + setNoteWiggle / setSustainWiggle the ripple modifier: set(0, 30, "ripple"), ripple.freq, ripple.speed - only the lanes wave, like Kade's

docs.title: Camera, HUD and window
docs.text: Kade MineFunkin camNotes / camSustains (1.8: .angle, .x, .y, tweenZoom, .alpha) the lanes' own modifiers: turnZ, x, y, zoom, fade - e.g. ease(beat, 2, "cubicOut", 120, "zoom") camHudAngle / setHudAngle(a) hud.angle setHudPosition(x, y) / getHudX() hud.x, hud.y hudZoom / setHudZoom(z) camera.zoom (zooms the playfield, and in a fight the world with it) cameraZoom / setCamZoom(z) the fight camera's lens: camera.fov - see the fight camera cameraAngle camera.roll setCamPosition(x, y), followXOffset, followYOffset camera.x, camera.y showOnlyStrums = true hideHud() + hideJudgments() setWindowPos(x, y) / getWindowX() window.x, window.y - offsets from where it was (game window) resizeWindow(w, h) / getWindowWidth() window.width, window.height (factors) getScreenWidth() / getScreenHeight() monitor.width, monitor.height

docs.title: Characters and sprites
docs.text: Kade MineFunkin playActorAnimation("boyfriend", "singUP", true, false) pose("player", "up") (pose) changeBoyfriendCharacter(id) / changeDadCharacter(id) setSkin("player", "skins/bf.png") (setSkin) setActorX(x, "dad") opponent.x (blocks, in the fight's frame - see the fighters) makeSprite(image, id, drawBehind) image[n].file = "image.png", image[n].layer = "stage" (behind) or "back" (in front)

docs.title: Global variables
docs.text: Kade MineFunkin curBeat, curStep, songPos beat, step, time bpm, crochet bpm, beats(1) (one beat in ms) downscroll player.downscroll scrollspeed scroll.speed (change it with scrollTo) mustHit song.singer == "player" screenWidth, screenHeight / hudWidth, hudHeight screen.width, screen.height difficulty, fpsCap, flashing, distractions not available

docs.title: Kade's examples, translated
docs.text: Kade's wiki ships eight example modcharts. Here's each one next to its MineFunkin version - you'll notice most of them get a bit shorter.

docs.title: The full example (receptors in a circle)
docs.text:
KadeMineFunkin 
function update(elapsed)
    local currentBeat = (songPos / 1000) * (bpm / 60)
    for i = 0, 7 do
        setActorX(_G['defaultStrum'..i..'X'] + 32 * math.sin((currentBeat + i * 0.25) * math.pi), i)
        setActorY(_G['defaultStrum'..i..'Y'] + 32 * math.cos((currentBeat + i * 0.25) * math.pi), i)
    end
end

function onFrame(dt)
    local b = time / beats(1)               -- the beat as a fraction, like Kade's currentBeat
    for lane = 0, 3 do
        strum[lane].x = 32 * sin((b + lane * 0.25) * pi)
        strum[lane].y = 32 * cos((b + lane * 0.25) * pi)
    end
end

docs.title: Spinning receptors
docs.text:
KadeMineFunkin 
function update(elapsed)
    for i = 0, 7 do
        setActorAngle(getActorAngle(i) + 15, i)
    end
end

function onFrame(dt)
    for lane = 0, 3 do
        strum[lane].angle = time / 3          -- a full turn a little faster than every second
    end
end

Kade adds 15 degrees per frame, so it spins faster on a faster computer (someone with 240 fps gets a very different song!). Working the angle out from time spins at the same speed for everyone.

docs.title: The spinning HUD
docs.text:
KadeMineFunkin 
function update(elapsed)
    camHudAngle = camHudAngle + 0.005
end

function onFrame(dt)
    hud.angle = time / 200
end

docs.title: Spin at a specific part of the song
docs.text:
KadeMineFunkin 
function update(elapsed)
    if curStep >= 352 and curStep < 400 then
        for i = 0, 7 do
            setActorAngle(getActorAngle(i) + 15, i)
        end
    else
        for i = 0, 7 do
            setActorAngle(0, i)
        end
    end
end

function onFrame(dt)
    local spinning = step >= 352 and step < 400
    for lane = 0, 3 do
        strum[lane].angle = spinning ? time / 3 : 0
    end
end

docs.title: Showing and hiding the receptors and the HUD
docs.text:
KadeMineFunkin 
function start(song)
    showOnlyStrums = true
    strumLine1Visible = false
end

function onStart()
    hideHud()
    hideJudgments()
    strums.opponentAlpha = 0       -- the opponent's receptors (practice)
end

docs.title: Looping through the notes on screen
docs.text:
KadeMineFunkin 
function update(elapsed)
    for i = 0, getRenderedNotes() do
        setRenderedNotePos(getRenderedNoteX(i), getRenderedNoteY(i) + 10 * math.sin(songPos / 100), i)
    end
end

function onFrame(dt)
    for i = 0, notes.count - 1 do
        note[i].y = 10 * sin(time / 100)    -- an offset: 0 = where the note would be anyway
    end
end

docs.title: Centering your side
docs.text: Kade moves the player's receptors to the middle of the screen. In a MineFunkin fight, your lanes already are in the middle - nothing to do. In practice, fade the opponent's receptors out (strums.opponentAlpha = 0) and slide yours over with moveStrums if you like.

docs.title: Jumping arrows
docs.text:
KadeMineFunkin 
function beatHit(beat)
    for i = 0, 7 do
        setActorY(_G['defaultStrum'..i..'Y'] - 20, i)
        tweenPosYAngle(i, _G['defaultStrum'..i..'Y'], 0, 0.3)
    end
end

function onBeat(b)
    for lane = 0, 3 do
        strum[lane].y = -20
        tween(strum[lane].y, 0, beats(0.5), "quadOut")
    end
end

Want more? Lots of modchart moves - with pictures - are in the Modcharts guide.

docs.title: Modcharts
docs.text:
Lanes that sway like they've had one too many. Arrows spinning on their way in. Notes riding in on a wave, or sneaking in from the side. That's a modchart - and it's probably the most fun you can have with event scripts.

In MineFunkin a modchart is nothing special: just event files. Usually one song script runs the whole thing, or you place events in the chart to switch effects on and off. Everything on this page works everywhere - in practice at the Retro TV and in fights.

There are two ways to write one, and you can mix them. This page moves the lanes with properties (strum[0].x = ..., worked out in onFrame) - the Psych and Kade way. The other is modifiers, where you plan sway, downscroll, turnZ and seventy others on the song's beats, in 3D, on as many playfields as you like. For a long, planned modchart that's the better fit.

Grab what you like, change the numbers, see what happens. That's honestly how most good modcharts get made. Every property used here is explained in full on strum[lane], strums and note[i].

docs.title: Start with this
docs.text:
Here's an empty modchart, ready to fill in. Save it as modchart.event in the song's folder:

format 1.1
-- The song's modchart: everything that moves the lanes, in one place.

event {
    name = "Modchart",
    category = "Song script",
    description = "Runs for the whole song - no chart event needed.",
}

function onStart()
    -- set things up before the countdown
end

function onFrame(dt)
    -- things that move all the time; work them out from time or beat
end

function onBeat(b)
    -- things that happen on a beat
end

function onStep(n)
    -- things that happen on an exact step (four per beat)
end

Kade: modchart.lua with start, update, beatHit, stepHit · Psych: a script in data/song-name/

docs.title: The three tools
docs.text:
Everything you can move falls into one of three groups:

Tool Moves Properties Lanes a receptor and everything in its lane strum[lane].x, .y, .angle, .scale, .alpha, ... and the whole strumline strums.* The way in where a lane's notes come from and how fast strum[lane].direction, .speed, .noteAngle Notes one by one each note on its own note[i].x, .y, .alpha, .angle, .scale, .visible

docs.title: At a specific part of the song
docs.text:
An effect that runs through the whole song gets old quickly. Here are three ways to switch one on and off:

-- 1. By step, in the script itself (step 64 = bar 5).
function onFrame(dt)
    if step >= 64 and step < 128 then
        for lane = 0, 3 do
            strum[lane].angle = time / 3        -- spinning from bar 5 to bar 9
        end
    end
end

function onStep(n)
    if n == 128 then
        for lane = 0, 3 do tween(strum[lane].angle, 0, beats(1)) end
    end
end

-- 2. By a chart event: place it where it starts, and again where it stops.
params {
    on = bool { from = "value1", default = true, label = "On" },
}

local active = false

function onEvent(p)
    active = p.on
    if not active then resetLanes(beats(1)) end
end

function onFrame(dt)
    if not active then return end
    -- the effect
end

-- 3. By section (every 4 beats).
function onSection(n)
    if n == 16 then flipScroll() end
    if n == 24 then flipScroll() end
end

The first keeps the whole modchart in one file, which is nice for reading it later. The second lets you drag it around in the chart editor until it sits right. Pick whatever feels better - you can mix them, too.

docs.title: Sway: from side to side
docs.text:
function onFrame(dt)
    for lane = 0, 3 do
        strum[lane].wobbleX = 14 * sin(time / 1000 * 3.2 + lane * 0.9)
    end
end

docs.title: Flip sides: left becomes right
docs.text:
function onEvent(p)
    for lane = 0, 3 do
        tween(strum[lane].x, (3 - 2 * lane) * strums.spacing, beats(0.75), "backOut")
    end
end

Lane 0 moves three lanes to the right, lane 3 three to the left, and the middle two swap. Your keys stay the same - so the left arrow is suddenly on the right. Mean, but fun. Tween them back to 0 to undo it.

docs.title: Split scroll: two up, two down
docs.text:
function onEvent(p)
    flipScroll(2)
    flipScroll(3)
    after(beats(8), function() resetLanes() end)
end

docs.title: Vanishing beats: the notes go, the receptors stay
docs.text:
function onBeat(b)
    if b % 4 != 2 then return end
    for lane = 0, 3 do
        strum[lane].noteAlpha = 0
        tween(strum[lane].noteAlpha, 1, beats(1), "quadIn")
    end
end

noteAlpha fades only the notes and holds - the receptors stay, so the player still knows where to hit. Just not what's coming.

docs.title: Lanes in the singer's colour
docs.text:
function onOpponentHit(note)
    strum[note.lane].color = #FF6060
    tween(strum[note.lane].color, #FFFFFF, beats(0.5))
end

docs.title: Spin, one lane after the other
docs.text:
function onEvent(p)
    for lane = 0, 3 do
        after(beats(0.25 * lane), function()
            strum[lane].angle = 0
            tween(strum[lane].angle, 360, beats(1), "backOut")
        end)
    end
end

Ever wondered why each lane gets its own number inside after, even though the loop has moved on? Every function() ... end remembers the locals as they were the moment it was made.

docs.title: Pop on the beat
docs.text:
function onBeat(b)
    for lane = 0, 3 do
        after(steps(lane * 0.5), function()
            strum[lane].scale = 1.25
            tween(strum[lane].scale, 1, beats(0.75), "elasticOut")
        end)
    end
end

docs.title: Circles
docs.text:
function onFrame(dt)
    local t = time / beats(4) * 2 * pi   -- one circle per bar
    for lane = 0, 3 do
        local a = t + lane * pi / 2
        strum[lane].x = 24 * cos(a)
        strum[lane].y = 24 * sin(a)
    end
end

docs.title: Spread apart on every eighth (Accordion)
docs.text:
function onStep(n)
    if n % 2 != 0 then return end
    for lane = 0, 3 do
        strum[lane].x = (lane - 1.5) * strums.spacing * 0.6
        tween(strum[lane].x, 0, steps(1.8), "quadOut")
    end
end

docs.title: Ghost lanes: the next lane fades every beat
docs.text:
function onBeat(b)
    local lane = b % 4
    strum[lane].alpha = 0.2
    tween(strum[lane].alpha, 1, beats(1.5), "quadIn")
end

docs.title: The whole strumline jumps (Zigzag)
docs.text:
local side = 1

function onBeat(b)
    side = -side
    tween(strums.x, side * 40, beats(0.5), "backOut")
end

docs.title: Side doors
docs.text:
function onEvent(p)
    strum[0].direction = -90     -- lane 0's notes come in from the right ...
    strum[3].direction = 90      -- ... lane 3's from the left
    after(beats(8), function() resetLanes(beats(1)) end)
end

direction turns the lane's way in clockwise around its receptor. The notes themselves stay upright, so the arrows still point the way you press - only where they come from changes.

docs.title: Tilted and slow
docs.text:
function onEvent(p)
    for lane = 0, 3 do
        strum[lane].direction = 30     -- every lane comes in at a slant
        strum[lane].speed = 0.6        -- and slower
    end
end

function onFrame(dt)
    strum[1].noteAngle = time / 3      -- lane 1's notes spin on their way in
end

docs.title: One lane faster
docs.text:
function onEvent(p)
    strum[2].speed = 2        -- the up lane's notes come twice as fast
end

A faster lane shows its notes later and they fly in quicker - the classic "trap lane". resetLanes() puts the speed back along with everything else.

docs.title: Notes one by one
docs.text:
This is where it gets really wild. note[0] ... note[notes.count - 1] are your notes on their way in, the next one first, and you can move every single one of them.

Set them in onFrame, every frame - they go back to normal before each frame, so you can't break anything for good. Most effects are built from note[i].distance: how many ms until the note has to be hit. Far away, close by, and everything in between.

docs.title: Sway notes: a wave they ride in on
docs.text:
function onFrame(dt)
    for i = 0, notes.count - 1 do
        local d = note[i].distance
        note[i].x = sin(d / 120 + time / 400) * 30
        note[i].alpha = clamp(1.6 - d / 700, 0, 1)    -- far away = see-through
    end
end

Landing exactly on the receptor

At distance 0 the wave above is still somewhere between -30 and 30 pixels. To make every note land right on its receptor, let the offset shrink near it: multiply by clamp(d / 300, 0, 1).

docs.title: Hide near and hide far
docs.text:
function onFrame(dt)
    for i = 0, notes.count - 1 do
        local d = note[i].distance
        -- Hide near: notes vanish as they get close (between 450 and 250 ms before the hit).
        note[i].alpha = smoothstep(250, 450, d)
    end
end

Swap the two numbers (smoothstep(450, 250, d) → 1 near, 0 far) and it's hide far: the notes only show up at the very last moment. Both are properly hard, so keep them short.

docs.title: Grow as they come
docs.text:
function onFrame(dt)
    for i = 0, notes.count - 1 do
        note[i].scale = 0.5 + 0.5 * (1 - clamp(note[i].distance / 1000, 0, 1))
    end
end

docs.title: Every other note from the other side
docs.text:
function onFrame(dt)
    for i = 0, notes.count - 1 do
        local d = note[i].distance
        local side = note[i].time / beats(1) % 2 < 1 ? 1 : -1      -- by beat: left, right, left, ...
        note[i].x = side * clamp(d / 4, 0, 160)                     -- 0 on the receptor
    end
end

docs.title: Spinning, but only in one lane
docs.text:
function onFrame(dt)
    for i = 0, notes.count - 1 do
        if note[i].lane == 1 then note[i].angle = note[i].distance / 3 end
    end
end

(For a whole lane at once, strum[1].noteAngle is shorter.)

docs.title: Held notes glow
docs.text:
function onFrame(dt)
    for i = 0, notes.count - 1 do
        if note[i].held then note[i].scale = 1.15 end
    end
end

docs.title: Modchart classics
docs.text: The big moves from Taro / Kade style Lua modcharts, the way the Event Showcase does them. The showcase's files ease them in and out nicely; here you get just the core of each, so it's easy to see how it works.

docs.title: Kicked on the drums
docs.text:
local flip = 1

-- Sideways on 0, 0.75, 1.5 and 2.25 of every bar, each time the other way.
function onStep(n)
    local s = n % 16

    if s == 0 or s == 3 or s == 6 or s == 9 then
        flip = -flip
        for lane = 0, 3 do
            strum[lane].wobbleX = 24 * flip
            tween(strum[lane].wobbleX, 0, beats(0.75), "cubicOut")
        end
    end
end

docs.title: Off the screen and back
docs.text:
function onFrame(dt)
    local b = time / beats(1)
    local far = screen.height * 1.2

    for lane = 0, 3 do
        local side = lane % 2 == 0 ? 1 : -1
        strum[lane].y = clamp(30 * side * tan(b * 0.25 * pi), -far, far)
    end
end

tan() runs off to infinity at beat 2 of every bar: half the lanes shoot off the top, half off the bottom, and then they come back in from the other side. Looks amazing, plays terribly - so keep it to bars where the player has no notes.

docs.title: Across the screen, wrapping round
docs.text:
function onFrame(dt)
    local w = screen.width
    local s = strums.spacing
    local pos = time / beats(8) * w    -- a screen width every two bars

    for lane = 0, 3 do
        local home = w / 2 + (lane - 1.5) * s
        local x = (w / 8 + lane * w / 4 + pos) % w
        strum[lane].x = x - home
    end
end

home is where the lane normally sits (the strumline is centred), and x is where it should be now: a quarter of the screen apart, sliding right. The % wraps it back round when it reaches the edge.

docs.title: Upside down, the world upright
docs.text:
function onEvent(p)
    hud.extras = false
    tween(hud.angle, 180, beats(4), "cubicInOut")
    tween(camera.roll, -180, beats(4), "cubicInOut")

    for lane = 0, 3 do
        tween(strum[lane].x, (3 - 2 * lane) * strums.spacing, beats(4), "cubicInOut")
        tween(strum[lane].angle, -180, beats(4), "cubicInOut")
    end
end

Just turning the HUD over would put the lanes in reverse order with every arrow upside down. Mirroring them and turning the arrows back makes it play like plain old downscroll - it only looks crazy. In a fight the camera rolls along with hud.angle, and camera.roll turns it back, so the world stays the right way up.

docs.title: A ring (Halo)
docs.text:
function onFrame(dt)
    local s = strums.spacing
    local turn = time / beats(4) * 2 * pi    -- one turn a bar

    for lane = 0, 3 do
        local a = turn + lane * pi / 2
        local depth = cos(a)                 -- 1 = at the front, -1 = at the back
        strum[lane].x = 2.4 * s * sin(a) - (lane - 1.5) * s
        strum[lane].y = 0.55 * s * depth
        strum[lane].scale = 1 - 0.2 * (1 - depth)
        strum[lane].alpha = 1 - 0.25 * (1 - depth)
    end
end

- (lane - 1.5) * s cancels the lane's own place, so all four ride the same ring around the middle. The ones at the back are smaller and fainter, which sells the 3D.

Kade Engine's own example modcharts (spinning receptors, the spinning HUD, jumping arrows, ...) are translated one by one on Coming from Kade Engine.

docs.title: Effects that fight each other
docs.text:
Here's the one thing that trips everybody up: a property can only be driven by one thing at a time. Setting it stops a tween on it, and two scripts writing it every frame just overwrite each other (the event log tells you which two).

The fix is easy. Give every effect that runs at the same time its own channel: one uses x, the next wobbleX, a third angle. The ways in and note[i] are channels of their own and stack with everything. More on that on strum[lane].

docs.title: Keep it playable
docs.text:
Everything on this page makes the song harder, and some of it a lot harder. A modchart should be a fun surprise, not a wall. A few rules of thumb:

  • Big changes (mirroring, splitting the scroll, a new way in) work best right before a little break, so the player can see the new layout before the notes arrive.
  • A wobble of a few pixels makes the lanes feel alive and costs nothing. A wobble of a whole lane width is a different song.
  • Don't fade a lane out completely while notes are coming in it. Hide near / hide far: short bursts only.
  • Save the wildest stuff (lanes off the screen, the playfield turning over) for bars where only the opponent sings.
  • Scattering the lanes to random places (scatterStrums(), the built-in Note Scramble) is the hardest of all, because nobody can learn it. Use it rarely - or better, not at all.

docs.title: Modifiers
docs.text:
Some modcharts are just a long list of lines like "at beat 32, over 2 beats, ease sway to 100". MineFunkin has that built in.

A modifier is a number that bends how a playfield is drawn - sway makes the lanes sway, downscroll flips the scroll, turnZ turns the whole field, cam.z pulls the camera back. There are about seventy of them, they work in 3D, and you can have up to six extra playfields next to yours. Hitting never changes: whatever the field looks like, you press at the same moment.

Two ways to modchart

The Modcharts page moves lanes with properties (strum[0].x = ...) in onFrame - the Psych and Kade way. Modifiers are the planned way: you write when and to what, the game works out every frame in between. Mix them freely.

docs.title: Your first one
docs.text:
Save this as modchart.event in the song's folder and play the song:

format 1.1

event { name = "Modchart", category = "Song script" }

function onStart()
    ease(16, 2, "cubicOut", 100, "sway")      -- beat 16: sway in over 2 beats
    ease(16, 2, "cubicOut", 50, "hover")      -- and bob up and down
    ease(30, 2, "cubicIn", 0, "sway")         -- and calm down again
    ease(30, 2, "cubicIn", 0, "hover")
    set(32, 100, "downscroll")                -- beat 32: the scroll flips
    set(40, 0, "downscroll")                  -- beat 40: back
end

Everything happens in onStart, before the song plays: you plan the changes on the song's beats. That's all a modchart of this kind is - a list.

  • ease(beat, beats, easing, value, modifier) - from beat on, over beats beats, to value.
  • set(beat, value, modifier) - jumps there at beat.
  • add(beat, beats, easing, amount, modifier) - amount more than it is at that moment.

Beats count from the song's start (beat 0) and follow tempo changes. Half beats are fine: ease(32.5, 0.25, ...).

docs.title: How the numbers work
docs.text:
Most modifiers are percent: 0 = off, 100 = the full effect, 200 = twice that, -100 = the other way. A few are pixels (x, slideY, cam.z ...) - measured on a 1280 x 720 screen, so a number fits whatever size the game window is - and a few degrees (turnZ, faceY ...). Every one of them, with what it does, is on the Modifiers page of the Event API.

When two changes overlap, the one that started last decides, and it starts from wherever the value is at that moment. So you never have to work out "where is it right now?" - just say where it should go:

ease(8, 4, "linear", 100, "sway")     -- 0 -> 100 over beats 8-12
ease(10, 1, "linear", 0, "sway")      -- at beat 10 it's 50: from 50 down to 0

If you do want a fixed start, give it as the last value: ease(10, 1, "linear", 0, "sway", 1, 200) starts at 200.

docs.title: One lane, or all four
docs.text:
Many modifiers have a form for a single lane: add the lane's number (0 left, 1 down, 2 up, 3 right).

set(48, 100, "downscroll1")   -- only the down lane scrolls the other way
set(48, 100, "downscroll3")   -- and the right lane
ease(48, 2, "backOut", -40, "slideY0")  -- the left lane hops up 40 px

The lane's own value adds to the field's: sway 50 and sway2 50 = lane 2 sways at 100.

docs.title: More playfields
docs.text:
Your notes are on field 1. copyField() gives you another one - a copy of your notes with modifiers of its own. You play once; every copy reacts.

local left = 0
local right = 0

function onStart()
    left = copyField(1)
    right = copyField(1)
    set(0, -320, "x", left)
    set(0, 320, "x", right)
    set(0, 60, "fade", left)                -- the copies are see-through
    set(0, 60, "fade", right)
    ease(64, 4, "sineInOut", 100, "flipSides", right)   -- one of them mirrors itself
end

The last value of ease, set and add is the field: a number, or a text like "1 2" or "all". Left out = every field. copyField(0) shows the opponent's notes instead, played by themselves - field 0 itself (the opponent's own row) is never drawn with modifiers, because a fight never shows the opponent's lanes.

docs.title: 3D
docs.text:
Fields live in a little 3D space: z brings a field toward you, turnX tips it back like a road, turnY turns it sideways, faceY flips the arrows like cards. Each field has a camera you can move (cam.z, cam.rotY) and a lens (cam.fov, 45 = normal, wider = stronger 3D).

function onStart()
    ease(96, 4, "cubicOut", -50, "turnX")        -- tip the field back
    ease(96, 4, "cubicOut", 600, "cam.z")        -- and step back to see it
    ease(104, 2, "sineInOut", 360, "faceY")      -- every arrow flips once
    ease(112, 4, "cubicIn", 0, "turnX")
    ease(112, 4, "cubicIn", 0, "cam.z")
end

Arrows are flat pictures: seen from the side they get thin, like a card. From behind they still show their arrow the right way round - left stays left, right stays right.

docs.title: Changing them live
docs.text:
Sometimes a value can't be planned - it answers the player, or you work it out from something else. Then use setMod and read with mod():

-- The field tips toward the lane you just hit, and settles.
function onHit(n)
    setMod("turnZ", (n.lane - 1.5) * 6)
end

function onFrame(dt)
    setMod("turnZ", mod("turnZ") * 0.9)
end

setMod in onFrame is fine - it doesn't pile anything up. It does win over a planned ease on the same modifier from that moment on, so give live values their own modifiers.

docs.title: Your own modifiers
docs.text:
customMod("name") makes a modifier of your own: you plan it with ease like any other, it draws nothing, and in onFrame you turn it into whatever you like. That's how two planned values can add up, or how a planned curve drives a screen effect:

function onStart()
    customMod("glitch")
    ease(128, 0.5, "cubicOut", 1, "glitch")
    ease(128.5, 2, "cubicIn", 0, "glitch")
end

function onFrame(dt)
    fx.glitch = mod("glitch")
end

Declare your own ones in onStart of every file that uses them (twice is fine). A name the game doesn't know - and you didn't declare - is an error when the file loads, with a "did you mean ...?".

docs.title: Coming from Psych or Kade
docs.text:
The names are MineFunkin's own, so a port means rewriting the lines with our names (a name the game doesn't know is an error with a "did you mean ...?"):

Engine Theirs Here Psych (modcharting tools) ease(32, 2, 'cubeOut', '100, drunk') ease(32, 2, "cubicOut", 100, "sway") Psych (modcharting tools) setMod('drunk', 1), addPlayfield() setMod("sway", 100), copyField(1) Kade 1.8 camNotes.angle, createWiggle turnZ, the ripple modifier

Modifier names from Psych's modcharting tools and ours:

Theirs Ours drunk, tipsy, bumpy, tornado, beat sway, hover, bulge, twister, kick confusion, dizzy, tiny, pulse twirl, tumble, shrinkArrows, breathe confusionXOffset / YOffset / Offset faceX, faceY, faceZ reverse, flip, invert downscroll, flipSides, swapPairs movex, movey, movez slideX, slideY, slideZ rotationx, rotationy, rotationz turnX, turnY, turnZ mini shrink xmod, boost, brake, wave speed, speedUp, slowDown, speedWave dark, stealth fadeStrums, fadeNotes hidden, sudden (+ offset) hideNear, hideFar (+ .offset, .fade) Kade's note wiggle ripple (+ .freq, .speed)

Easings are the usual names ("sineInOut", "cubicOut" ...). Every modifier, with what it does, is on the Modifiers page.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• It's the drawing only. Notes are judged exactly as without modifiers - in practice and in fights.
  • Seeking is free. A modifier's value depends only on the beat, so skipping in a replay, watching a fight from inside or the editor's preview land on exactly the same picture.
  • A script that breaks takes its changes with it. Its planned modifiers go, the others stay.
  • Limits: 200 000 planned changes per song, 8 fields (yours, the opponent's, 6 of your own), 256 own modifiers.
  • Modifiers reset with the song: a restart starts from your onStart again.

docs.title: Coming from Psych Engine
docs.text:
Welcome over! If you've written Psych Engine Lua before, you already know most of this - the ideas are the same, only some names are different. This page walks through Psych's Lua API in the order it's sorted there - script types, callbacks, then the function pages one by one - and tells you what each thing is called in a .event file.

Keep it open in a tab while you port your first song. After that, you probably won't need it much.

docs.title: The big differences
docs.text:
A handful of things work differently on purpose. Once these click, the rest is mostly renaming:

  • One file per event. Psych splits a custom event into Name.lua + Name.txt; here it's one .event file with an event { } header, a params { } block for the editor's controls, and the code.
  • No setProperty strings. Everything you can change has its own name (camera.zoom, strum[2].x, player.pose). The upside: a typo is an error the moment the file loads, with a "did you mean ...?" - instead of silently doing nothing while you wonder why.
  • No tags. Psych names every sprite, tween and timer with a tag. Here texts and pictures are slots (text[0] ... text[7], image[0] ... image[31]), a tween belongs to the property it moves, and timers only need a name if you want to cancel them.
  • Durations are milliseconds, written beats(2), steps(4) or seconds(1) - they follow the song's tempo by themselves.
  • No globals. Declare every variable with local (or shared, to share it between files).
  • The characters are Minecraft players. boyfriend and dad are the two fighters in the world (player, opponent) during a fight. In practice at the Retro TV there's no world, so they're the two puppets next to the lanes.

docs.title: Script types
docs.text: Psych MineFunkin Event (custom_events/Name.lua + .txt) a .event file in the song folder with onEvent - see Your first event Song script (data/song-name/script.lua) a .event file without onEvent - every callback runs for the whole song: Song scripts Stage script (stages/name.lua) a song script that sets up pictures in onStart: Stages and sprites Note type (custom_notetypes/) not available - the one special note is the Forced-Miss Note (note[i].trap) Character script not available - the characters are the fighters; the fighters page shows what scripts can do with them Global script (scripts/) not available - scripts belong to a song, so a downloaded song can't change other songs

docs.title: Callbacks
docs.text: Psych MineFunkin onCreate / onCreatePost onStart onSongStart onSongStart onCountdownTick(counter) onCountdown(n) - 3, 2, 1, then 0 for "go" onUpdate(elapsed) / onUpdatePost onFrame(dt) - dt in ms onBeatHit / onStepHit / onSectionHit onBeat(b) / onStep(n) / onSection(n) onEvent(name, value1, value2) onEvent(p) - typed p.name values, raw p.value1, p.value2 goodNoteHit / opponentNoteHit onHit(note) / onOpponentHit(note) noteMiss / noteMissPress onMiss(note) (both) onGhostTap / onKeyPress / onKeyRelease onGhostTap / onKeyPress / onKeyRelease - the lane 0-3 onPause / onResume onPause / onResume - a pause can't be refused onGameOver onFail onEndSong onEnd onTweenCompleted(tag) / onTimerCompleted(tag) put the code in an after with the tween's duration, or in the timer's function onSpawnNote, onMoveCamera, onRecalculateRating, onNextDialogue, onSkipDialogue not available

docs.title: PlayState and Reflection
docs.text: Psych MineFunkin setProperty("camGame.zoom", z), defaultCamZoom camera.zoom, the fight camera's lens camera.fov (the fight camera) setProperty("camHUD.alpha", a), camHUD.angle hud.alpha, hud.angle setProperty("scoreTxt.visible", false), healthBar.alpha hud.scoreAlpha, hud.healthAlpha setProperty("scoreTxt.x", x), scoreTxt.scale hud.scoreX, hud.scoreScale (also title*, health*) - hud setProperty("skipCountdown", true) hud.countdown = false in onStart setProperty("boyfriend.stunned", true), cutscene input locks strums.input = false setProperty("boyfriend.x", x) player.x - the fighters getProperty("health") / setHealth / addHealth player.health / setHealth / addHealth getPropertyFromGroup("notes", i, "x"), setPropertyFromGroup(...) note[i].x and friends - notes one by one setPropertyFromGroup("strumLineNotes", i, "x" / "angle" / "alpha" / "direction") strum[lane].x, .angle, .alpha, .direction (strum[lane]) - Psych counts a straight way in as 90, MineFunkin as 0 setPropertyFromClass("ClientPrefs", "downScroll", ...) flipScroll / setScroll setPropertyFromClass("openfl.Lib", "application.window.x", ...) window.x - an offset from where it was (game window) setProperty / getProperty on anything else, runHaxeCode not available - see left out on purpose

docs.title: Spritesheet and FlxAnimate
docs.text: Psych MineFunkin makeLuaSprite(tag, image, x, y) + addLuaSprite image[n].file, .x, .y (shares of the screen) - image[n] makeAnimatedLuaSprite + addAnimationByPrefix + playAnim image[n].file (+ the .xml), image[n].anim = "prefix", image[n].frame = 0 - Psych sprites addAnimationByIndices a prefix that matches only those frames, or a grid sheet with frames makeGraphic(tag, w, h, color) image[n].file = "solid" + .color, .width, .height scaleObject, setGraphicSize image[n].width, .height setScrollFactor(tag, x, y) image[n].follow - moving with the camera setObjectOrder, addLuaSprite(tag, true / false) image[n].order, image[n].layer setProperty(tag .. ".flipX", true) image[n].flipX = true setBlendMode(tag, "add") image[n].blend = "add" - blend modes setProperty(tag .. ".antialiasing", false) image[n].smooth = false (the default: sharp pixels) a video sprite / startVideo image[n].file = "videos/name/" - a folder of frames (videos) objectsOverlap, getMouseX not available FlxAnimate (texture atlases from Animate) not available - convert them to a sheet

docs.title: Text
docs.text: Psych MineFunkin makeLuaText(tag, text, width, x, y) + addLuaText text[n].value, .x, .y, .wrap setTextString, setTextColor, setTextSize text[n].value, .color, .size setTextFont text[n].font - Minecraft's fonts: "default", "uniform", "alt", "illager" setTextBorder(tag, size, color) text[n].outline (the colour; one pixel wide) setTextAlignment text[n].align setTextWidth, setTextAutoSize text[n].wrap

docs.title: Sound
docs.text: Psych MineFunkin playSound(file, volume, tag) playSound("file.ogg", volume, "tag") playMusic(file, volume, loop) loopSound - the song's own music is the song's audio stopSound(tag) stopSound soundFadeIn / soundFadeOut / setSoundVolume soundVolume("tag", volume, duration) setProperty("vocals.volume", v), inst.volume volume.player, volume.opponent, volume.inst - sounds and music getSoundTime, setSoundTime, setSoundPitch, pauseSound not available

docs.title: Shaders
docs.text: Psych MineFunkin initLuaShader + setSpriteShader(tag, shader) shader[0].file = "my.frag" - the Psych .frag file as it is, on the whole picture, the world, or the world behind the fighters (your own shaders) setShaderFloat(tag, name, value) setShaderFloat(slot, name, value) - int / bool uniforms too setShaderFloatArray not available - use single values ready-made shader effects the built-in fx.*: chromatic, bloom, blur, glitch, wave, ...

docs.title: Camera
docs.text: Psych MineFunkin cameraFlash, cameraFade, cameraShake flash, fadeOut, shake cameraSetTarget("dad"), camFollow focus("opponent"), or camera.x, camera.yaw, ... + resetCamera doTweenZoom tween(camera.zoom, ...) or zoom setCameraScroll, getCameraFollowX camera.x, camera.y, camera.z

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Psych MineFunkin keyJustPressed("left"), keyPressed("left"), keyReleased onKeyPress(lane), strum[lane].pressed, onKeyRelease keyboardJustPressed("SPACE"), mouse functions not available - only the lane keys reach scripts

docs.title: Tween and Timer
docs.text: Psych MineFunkin doTweenX, doTweenAlpha, doTweenAngle, doTweenColor, startTween tween(prop, to, duration, ease) on any number or colour property noteTweenX, noteTweenAlpha, noteTweenAngle, noteTweenDirection tween(strum[lane].x, ...), .alpha, .angle, .direction cancelTween(tag) stopTween(prop) runTimer(tag, 1) after(seconds(1), function() ... end, "tag") runTimer(tag, 0.5, 8) every(seconds(0.5), function() ... end, 8, "tag") cancelTimer(tag) cancel("tag")

docs.title: Character
docs.text: Psych MineFunkin characterPlayAnim("boyfriend", "singUP"), playAnim pose("boyfriend", "up") or boyfriend.pose = "up" a character's own animations (its JSON) setPose("dad", "left", "rightArm", ...) - the song's own poses, played by the notes boyfriend / dad boyfriend / dad - the fighters by the chart's sides (fighter names) triggerEvent("Change Character", ...) setSkin("opponent", "skins/rival.png") setProperty("dad.alpha", a), .angle, .scale dad.alpha, .turn, .scale - the fighters getCharacterX / setCharacterX dad.x (blocks, in the fight's frame), or pinned to the screen: bind("dad", x, y)

docs.title: Precache, Score and Script
docs.text: Psych MineFunkin precacheImage, precacheSound preload("picture.png"); sounds are read the first time they play getScore, getMisses, rating, combo player.score, player.misses, player.accuracy, player.combo - read only setScore, setMisses, setRatingPercent not available - scores stay honest for the leaderboards triggerEvent(name, v1, v2) trigger("Name", v1, v2) callOnLuas(func, args) / callOnScripts call("func", ...) setOnLuas(var, value) / setVar shared variables - song scripts addLuaScript, removeLuaScript, isRunning not available close() an active variable the callbacks check

docs.title: Uncategorized
docs.text: Psych MineFunkin debugPrint log(...) - it goes to the event log getRandomInt / getRandomFloat / getRandomBool randomInt(a, b) / random(a, b) / chance(p) stringStartsWith, stringEndsWith, stringSplit, stringTrim startsWith, endsWith, sub + find, trim - functions getSongPosition(), curBeat, curStep, curSection, bpm, crochet time, beat, step, floor(beat / 4), bpm, beats(1) getColorFromHex("FF0000") #FF0000 cond and a or b cond ? a : b (and / or work too, but 0 counts as false here) File I/O, Save Data, Achievements, Discord, Language, Substate, dialogue not available

docs.title: A whole event, side by side
docs.text:
Here's a Psych event that flashes the screen and zooms in, with the colour in value1 - and the same thing here:

Psych (Flash Zoom.lua + .txt)MineFunkin (flash_zoom.event) 
function onEvent(name, value1, value2)
    if name == "Flash Zoom" then
        cameraFlash("camGame", value1 ~= "" and value1 or "FFFFFF", 0.5)
        doTweenZoom("fz", "camGame", 1.2, 0.5, "sineOut")
        runTimer("fzBack", 2)
    end
end

function onTimerCompleted(tag)
    if tag == "fzBack" then
        doTweenZoom("fz", "camGame", 1, 0.5, "sineInOut")
    end
end

format 1.1

event {
    name = "Flash Zoom",
    description = "Flashes and zooms in, back after two seconds.",
}

params {
    tint = color { from = "value1", default = #FFFFFF, label = "Colour" },
}

function onEvent(p)
    flash(p.tint, seconds(0.5))
    zoom(1.2, seconds(0.5))
    after(seconds(2), function() zoom(1, seconds(0.5)) end)
end

Notice how much shorter it got? No name check, no timer tag, no onTimerCompleted. And the params block gives the event a real colour picker in the chart editor - while the chart file still stores value1 as text, just like Psych. So a Psych chart's events keep their values when you bring it over.

docs.title: Left out on purpose
docs.text:
Some of Psych's Lua can reach into the whole game - and into your computer. MineFunkin's scripts can't, and that's a feature: a song you download can't do anything to your game or your files. So these are gone for good:

  • runHaxeCode / HScript, and reaching any object by name (setProperty on whatever exists, getPropertyFromClass) - a script gets the properties of this wiki, nothing else;
  • reading and writing files, save data (initSaveData, flushSaveData), the clipboard, the internet;
  • loading more scripts while the song runs (addLuaScript), changing the chart or the stage files;
  • setting the score or misses.

Everything else a Psych chart usually does - tweens, timers, sprites and animations, texts, the camera, the characters, the notes one by one, sounds, health, shaders, even the game window - has a counterpart above. If you get stuck on something that isn't listed, the FAQ is a good next stop.

docs.title: Your own shaders
docs.text:
The built-in effects cover a lot. But when you want something nobody has thought of yet - a ripple from the middle of the screen, a kaleidoscope, a shockwave on the drop - you write your own shader.

A song can bring its own GLSL fragment shaders: .fsh files (MineFunkin's own kind) or .frag files written for Psych Engine, in the song's folder, its events/ folder or its shaders/ folder. A script switches them on through four slots, shader[0] to shader[3]. Up to four run at once, in slot order, right before the built-in effects.

A slot has a file, an amount (how much of it shows), four numbers a ... d you can hand to the shader, a target, and a read-only status - all on the shader[n] page.

Never written a shader? No shame - they look scarier than they are. The examples below work as they are, so start by changing their numbers and see what happens.

docs.title: The file
docs.text:
The file holds one function, effect. It runs for every single pixel on the screen: it gets that pixel's position (0 to 1, from the bottom left) and returns the colour that should be there.

// ripple.fsh - rings from the middle, a purple glow on the beat.
vec4 effect(vec2 uv) {
    vec2 d = uv - 0.5;
    d.x *= resolution.x / resolution.y;
    float r = length(d);
    float pulse = 1.0 - fract(beat);
    float wave = sin(r * 40.0 - time * 8.0) * 0.01 * (0.4 + pulse) * params.x;
    vec3 c = pixel(uv + normalize(d + 1e-5) * wave).rgb;
    c += vec3(0.2, 0.05, 0.3) * pulse * smoothstep(0.6, 0.0, r) * params.y;
    return vec4(c, 1.0);
}

And here's the script that switches it on, fading it in over two beats:

function onEvent(p)
    shader[0].file = "ripple.fsh"
    shader[0].a = 1
    shader[0].b = 1
    shader[0].amount = 0
    tween(shader[0].amount, 1, beats(2))
end

docs.title: What the file can use
docs.text:
pixel(uv) the picture at that spot (a vec4) resolution the picture's size in pixels time the song time in seconds (in scripts it's milliseconds) beat the song position in beats, with fractions: fract(beat) goes 0 → 1 every beat amount the slot's amount params the slot's a, b, c, d as params.x, .y, .z, .w

Those names are taken, so don't declare your own time, beat, params and so on. Everything else is plain GLSL 3.30: your own functions, constants, loops, #defines. You don't need a #version line (it's ignored anyway).

The result is mixed with the picture by amount and is always opaque - so amount is the easy way to fade a shader in and out.

docs.title: Handing the shader a moment
docs.text:
A shader has no memory: every frame it starts from scratch. So how do you make something happen from a certain moment on, like a shockwave on the drop? Hand it the song time of that moment, and let it count from there:

function onEvent(p)
    shader[1].file = "shockwave.fsh"
    shader[1].a = 1        -- strength
    shader[1].b = 1.1      -- speed
    shader[1].c = time / 1000   -- now, in seconds
end

// shockwave.fsh - a ring that runs out from the middle, bending the picture as it passes.
vec4 effect(vec2 uv) {
    float age = time - params.z;
    if (age < 0.0 || age > 1.6) {
        return pixel(uv);
    }

    vec2 aspect = vec2(resolution.x / resolution.y, 1.0);
    vec2 d = (uv - 0.5) * aspect;
    float r = length(d);
    float ring = r - age * params.y;
    float bend = exp(-(ring * ring) / 0.0049) * params.x * (1.0 - age / 1.6);
    vec2 dir = d / max(r, 0.0001);
    vec4 c = pixel(uv - dir / aspect * bend * 0.035);
    c.rgb += bend * 0.18 * vec3(1.0, 0.55, 0.85);
    return c;
}

docs.title: More examples
docs.text:
The examples on this page, as they look in a fight: the shockwave's ring, the warp's zoom blur, the kaleidoscope on "screen" (it folds the notes and the HUD too - on "world" they'd stay put), and the CRT's curved old screen.

warp.fsh - a zoom blur that kicks on every beat 
vec4 effect(vec2 uv) {
    float kick = pow(1.0 - fract(beat), 3.0);
    float amount = (0.015 + 0.07 * kick) * params.x;
    vec2 dir = uv - 0.5;
    vec3 sum = vec3(0.0);

    for (int i = 0; i < 12; i++) {
        float t = float(i) / 11.0;
        sum += pixel(uv - dir * amount * t).rgb;
    }

    return vec4(sum / 12.0, 1.0);
}
kaleido.fsh - the picture folded into turning mirrored slices 
// params.x = slices, params.y = turning speed (radians per second)
vec4 effect(vec2 uv) {
    float aspect = resolution.x / resolution.y;
    vec2 p = (uv - 0.5) * vec2(aspect, 1.0);
    float r = length(p);
    float slices = max(2.0, params.x);
    float slice = 6.2831853 / slices;
    float a = mod(atan(p.y, p.x) + time * params.y, slice);
    a = abs(a - slice * 0.5);
    float sweep = -2.3 + time * params.y * 0.6;
    vec2 q = vec2(cos(a + sweep), sin(a + sweep)) * r * 0.85;
    return pixel(clamp(q / vec2(aspect, 1.0) + 0.5, 0.001, 0.999));
}
crt.fsh - a curved old screen 
vec4 effect(vec2 uv) {
    vec2 c = uv * 2.0 - 1.0;
    c *= 1.0 + 0.08 * params.x * dot(c, c);
    vec2 st = c * 0.5 + 0.5;
    if (st.x < 0.0 || st.x > 1.0 || st.y < 0.0 || st.y > 1.0) {
        return vec4(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0);
    }
    vec3 col = pixel(st).rgb;
    col *= 0.85 + 0.15 * sin(st.y * resolution.y * 3.14159);
    return vec4(col, 1.0);
}

docs.title: Shaders from Psych Engine (.frag)
docs.text:
Got a shader from a Psych mod? A .frag file written for Psych (Flixel) runs as it is - put it where .fsh files go and name it in shader[n].file. MineFunkin gives it everything Flixel would: #pragma header, bitmap, openfl_TextureCoordv, openfl_TextureSize, flixel_texture2D, texture2D and gl_FragColor all work.

Its own uniform float / int / bool values (the first eight) are set from a script with setShaderFloat - Psych's call, with the slot instead of the tag:

function onStart()
    shader[0].file = "chroma.frag"
    setShaderFloat(0, "intensity", 0.5)
end

function onBeat(b)
    setShaderFloat(0, "intensity", 1.5)
end

A value you don't set is 0 - except iTime, which runs along with the song's seconds. uniform vec2 iResolution (or vec3) is the picture's size. Your own .fsh files can declare uniform float values the same way.

docs.title: Which shaders run: the check
docs.text:
A little honesty here: a shader runs on the player's graphics card, and once it has started drawing, nothing can stop it. A loop that never ends freezes the whole game. That's why the player decides which song shaders run (Options › MineFunkin › Song effects):

Setting Off No song shader runs. All checked Every song's shaders must pass MineFunkin's check. Own songs unchecked (default) The player's own songs run freely; songs from a server must pass the check. All unchecked Everything runs.

The check makes sure a shader always finishes. A checked file may only loop with for over number bounds - a literal, a #define N 12 or a const int N = 12; - with the counter declared in the loop's head and not changed inside it. At most 8192 loop rounds and 256 picture reads per pixel (nested loops and function calls multiplied). No out / inout parameters, no preprocessor lines except #define NAME number and #pragma header / #pragma body. A file that doesn't pass isn't run: shader[n].status says "refused", and the event log says why. If your song will be played on servers, write with the check in mind - every example on this page passes it.

The cost. MineFunkin measures how long every song shader takes on the graphics card. One that takes more than 25 ms per frame (on average over 30 frames) is switched off for the rest of the song, so nobody's stuck at 20 fps: status = "too heavy".

docs.title: When it doesn't compile
docs.text:
A shader with a mistake in it is switched off, and the graphics driver's message goes to the event log, with line numbers counted from the first line of your file:

[ERROR] Shader "broken.fsh" doesn't compile (lines count from the file's first line):
0:2(21): error: `undefinedThing' undeclared

0:2 means line 2 of your file. A file is read once per song, so after you've fixed it, restart the song.

docs.title: Limits and good to know
docs.text:
• .fsh or .frag, at most 32 KB a file, at most four at once. Only the song's own folder (and its events/ and shaders/ folders): a path that leads out of it is refused.
  • A file that isn't checked (your own songs, by default) can still freeze the game with a loop that never ends - so keep them simple, and test on a weaker machine if you can. Your players will thank you.
  • "world" and "terrain" shaders need a fight. In practice only "screen" ones run.
  • They get along with shader packs (Iris): the pack draws the world, your shader goes on top.

docs.title: The Event Showcase
docs.text:
Want to see what all of this looks like in one go? The Event Showcase is a complete song - two minutes, 140 BPM, intro to outro - where every single effect is an event file in the song's folder. 31 of them, plus 2 shaders.

Every big feature gets its own moment: texts and pictures, the callbacks, the HUD and the strum background, a whole modchart (lanes that jiggle, fly off the screen, scroll across it, turn upside down and ride a ring), the fight camera, the fighters (a dance, a death, a giant, swapping places), built-in effects and the song's own shaders. While it plays, a caption in the top left names each feature right as it starts.

And it's meant to be taken apart: the event files are commented, so open them up, read them, and copy whatever you like into your own songs.

Download the song (.zip)

Unzip it into your songs folder (.minecraft/MineFunkin/client/songs/) and play Event Showcase at a Speaker - against the dummy or a friend. That's where it shines: the camera and the fighters only exist in a fight. In practice at the Retro TV everything else still runs.

docs.title: The song, part by part
docs.text:
Part Bars What happens Intro 1-4 The screen switches on like an old TV - a dot, a line, the picture - with the title on it. The playfield starts to drift. Verse 1 5-12 Call and response. The camera follows whoever sings, your hits pop their lanes, your strumline leans toward the opponent's notes, the combo meter shouts at 25. Verse 2 13-20 A spotlight follows the melody, then the lanes get kicked around on the drum pattern. Build 21-24 Zoom, dark edges, shake and a 3-2-1. On the opponent's bar the lanes fly off the screen, then they spin. Drop 25-32 An impact: a shockwave knocks both fighters back. The playfield punches on the kicks, the strum background lights up, another shockwave, the lanes hop in turns. The dance 33-40 Both fighters stop their own animation and dance eight moves, mirrored. The camera swings round them; the words come in one by one. Fake death 41-44 The opponent drops dead, the colour drains, the lanes fall off the screen. A heartbeat - then it rises as a giant and the lanes shoot back up. Breakdown 45-48 The lanes spread across the whole screen and scroll sideways, wrapping round at the edges. Rebuild 49-52 The fighters jump over each other and swap places; two lanes come from the other side. Final drop 53-68 Every kick hits the picture, the logo bumps under the notes, the fighters swap back. The playfield turns upside down for four bars - the world stays upright - and back. Then a swap ping-pong. Outro 69-72 The lanes ride a ring, then drop out of it. The live score - and the TV switches off.

Notice how the wildest moves (the lanes off the screen, the playfield turning over) only happen on bars where the opponent sings? That's on purpose - nobody has to play through them. And every effect keeps to its own property ("channel") or its own bars, so they stack without fighting each other - see strum[lane].

docs.title: What each file shows
docs.text:
Looking for an example of something specific? Find it here, then open that file:

File Part of the song Shows power_on.event intro a song shader (shaders/crt.fsh) driven by its four numbers: a dot, a line, the picture; the title on the "top" layer caption.event every part a counter kept for the whole song, a newer caption cancelling an older one's slide-out cam_sway.event from the intro on onFrame(dt), noise(), easing a variable by hand, reading shared hype judge_glow.event from verse 1 on onHit / onMiss, note.judgment / note.offset, a function that returns a value cam_follow.event verse 1 on onHit / onOpponentHit easing camera.z / .x / .yaw toward whoever sings (fights) opponent_echo.event verse 1 onOpponentHit, lanes turned into directions, a vignette pulse combo_meter.event the whole song a song script: no chart event, only onHit / onMiss and player.combo spotlight.event verse 2 onHit and onOpponentHit sharing one function, strum[lane].alpha per lane jiggle.event verse 2, the drops a modchart's kick: wobbleX / wobbleY jolted on a drum pattern from onStep(n) build_up.event build onStep patterns that speed up, a 3-2-1 scheduled in a for loop, writing shared hype kade_sway.event build .x / .y from sin() every frame; "wild" takes tan(), so the lanes fly off the screen and come back spin.event build, the end .angle from 360 to 0: once or every bar, counted from where the event sits the_drop.event both drops an impact, kick / snare patterns in onBeat, hsv() colours, hud.angle shockwave.event every impact a shader (shaders/shockwave.fsh) handed its start time; the fighters' pitch / squash / z lane_lights.event drop the strum background (underlay.color / .alpha / .width) flaring on the beat hop.event drops max(0, sin()) as a bouncing ball, isDown to hop toward the middle dance_routine.event the dance animate = false, body parts, eight moves as functions, a mirror flag, puppet[i] orbit_cam.event the dance camera.x / .y / .z / .yaw / .pitch together: circling the fighters word_by_word.event the dance six parameters from the parts of one value, after() keeping each step, break fake_death.event fake death opponent.pose = "death", fx.saturation draining the colour, the camera looking down drop_out.event fake death a sequence of tweens per lane with after(): fall off, come back with "elasticOut" rise.event fake death opponent.scale with "elasticOut", a white flash, the colour back scroller.event breakdown the lanes across screen.width, wrapping round with %; an ease written by hand switcheroo.event rebuild, final drop the fighters jump and swap places: .x / .z in the fight's frame, .turn 180 scroll_twist.event rebuild text properties (strum[lane].scroll), player.downscroll kick_hit.event final drop fx.chromatic + fx.bloom on every beat logo_bump.event final drop the song's logo.png on the "lanes" layer: on the strum background, under the notes upside_down.event final drop hud.angle 180 with camera.roll -180 so the world stays upright, the lanes mirrored with strums.spacing halo.event outro .x / .y / .scale / .alpha from one angle per lane: a ring with depth finale.event outro live player.score / player.accuracy on the "top" layer, onEnd power_off.event the end the same shader played backwards, ending on screen.color

docs.title: The files
docs.text:
All of them, in the order the song shows them (each file's first comment line has the same number).

power_on.event 
format 1.1
-- Event Showcase 1/31: the song switches on like an old TV - a dot, a line, then the picture - with the
-- title flickering in on the curved screen. After two bars the TV look fades away.
-- Shows: a song's own shader (shaders/crt.fsh) driven by its four numbers, after() for a sequence.

event {
    name = "Power On",
    color = #5CF2FF,
    category = "Screen",
    description = "The screen opens from a dot like an old TV, with the title on it.",
}

params {
    title    = text { from = "value1", default = "EVENT SHOWCASE", label = "Title" },
    subtitle = text { from = "value2", label = "Subtitle" },
}

local glowing = false

function onEvent(p)
    -- crt.fsh: a = curvature, b = open sideways, c = open up and down, d = scanlines.
    shader[0].file = "crt.fsh"
    shader[0].amount = 1
    shader[0].a = 1
    shader[0].b = 0
    shader[0].c = 0
    shader[0].d = 1

    -- A dot grows into a line, the line opens into the picture.
    tween(shader[0].b, 1, beats(1), "expoOut")
    after(beats(1), function() tween(shader[0].c, 1, beats(2), "expoOut") end)

    text[0].value = upper(p.title)
    text[0].x = 0.5
    text[0].y = 0.34
    text[0].size = 3.2
    text[0].color = #5CF2FF
    text[0].layer = "top"
    text[0].alpha = 0

    text[1].value = p.subtitle ?? ""
    text[1].x = 0.5
    text[1].y = 0.46
    text[1].size = 1
    text[1].color = #FF6EC7
    text[1].layer = "top"
    text[1].alpha = 0

    -- The title warms up with the tube: it flickers for a beat, then holds.
    after(beats(2.5), function() glowing = true end)
    after(beats(3.5), function()
        glowing = false
        text[0].alpha = 1
        tween(text[1].alpha, 1, beats(1))
    end)

    -- Two and a half bars later the TV look fades out and the title goes.
    after(beats(10), function()
        tween(shader[0].a, 0, beats(2), "sineInOut")
        tween(shader[0].d, 0, beats(2), "sineInOut")
        tween(shader[0].amount, 0, beats(2), "sineInOut")
        tween(text[0].alpha, 0, beats(1))
        tween(text[0].size, 4, beats(1), "expoIn")
        tween(text[1].alpha, 0, beats(1))
    end)

    after(beats(12), function()
        shader[0].file = ""
        text[0].value = ""
        text[1].value = ""
    end)
end

function onFrame(dt)
    if glowing then
        text[0].alpha = chance(0.6) ? random(0.5, 1) : 0.1
    end
end
shaders/crt.fsh 
// Overdrive's old TV: a curved screen with rounded corners and scanlines, which can open out of a
// line and close into a dot like a CRT switching on and off.
// params.x = curvature (0-1), .y = how far it's open sideways (0-1), .z = how far it's open up and
// down (0-1), .w = scanlines (0-1).
vec4 effect(vec2 uv) {
    vec2 c = uv * 2.0 - 1.0;
    c *= 1.0 + 0.1 * params.x * dot(c, c);

    // The picture squeezed into the open part: a thin line is the whole picture pressed flat.
    vec2 open = max(vec2(params.y, params.z), vec2(0.004));
    vec2 q = c / open;

    // A rounded rectangle: the corners round off with the curvature.
    float n = mix(40.0, 7.0, clamp(params.x, 0.0, 1.0));
    float e = pow(pow(abs(q.x), n) + pow(abs(q.y), n), 1.0 / n);

    if (e > 1.0) {
        return vec4(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0);
    }

    vec2 st = q * 0.5 + 0.5;
    vec3 col = pixel(st).rgb;

    // All the light pressed into the line: the tighter, the brighter.
    float squeeze = (1.0 - open.x) + (1.0 - open.y);
    col *= 1.0 + 3.0 * squeeze;

    col *= 1.0 - params.w * 0.2 * (0.5 + 0.5 * sin(st.y * resolution.y * 3.14159));
    // A brighter band rolling slowly down the tube.
    col *= 1.0 + 0.05 * params.w * sin((st.y + time * 0.3) * 6.2831);
    // Darker toward the curved edges.
    col *= mix(1.0, smoothstep(1.0, 0.8, e), params.x);

    return vec4(col, 1.0);
}
caption.event 
format 1.1
-- Event Showcase 2/31: names what's on screen. Each caption slides in from the left with its number and
-- slides out again; a newer one takes the place of an older one.
-- Shows: a counter kept for the whole song, a closure that checks whether it's still the newest.

event {
    name = "Caption",
    color = #B9A6FF,
    category = "Text",
    description = "A numbered caption top left: the event and what it uses.",
}

params {
    title = text { from = "value1", label = "Event" },
    line  = text { from = "value2", label = "What it uses" },
}

local count = 0

local function slideIn(slot, delay)
    text[slot].x = -0.5
    text[slot].alpha = 1
    after(delay, function() tween(text[slot].x, 0.03, beats(0.6), "backOut") end)
end

function onEvent(p)
    count += 1
    local mine = count

    text[5].value = (count < 10 ? "0" : "") .. count .. "  " .. upper(p.title ?? "?")
    text[5].align = "left"
    text[5].y = 0.11
    text[5].size = 1.1
    text[5].color = #5CF2FF
    text[5].layer = "top"
    slideIn(5, 0)

    text[6].value = p.line ?? ""
    text[6].align = "left"
    text[6].y = 0.11 + 0.065
    text[6].size = 0.7
    text[6].color = #F2ECFF
    text[6].layer = "top"
    slideIn(6, beats(0.15))

    after(beats(7), function()
        if count == mine then
            tween(text[5].x, -0.6, beats(0.6), "backIn")
            tween(text[6].x, -0.6, beats(0.6), "backIn")
        end
    end)
end
cam_sway.event 
format 1.1
-- Event Showcase 3/31: a handheld-camera drift.
-- Shows: onFrame(dt), noise() (smooth and repeatable), easing a script variable by hand, and reading
-- the shared "hype" value other events write - the louder the song gets, the more it sways.

event {
    name = "Cam Sway",
    color = #7CC8FF,
    category = "Screen",
    description = "The playfield drifts like a handheld camera. Off eases it back to rest.",
}

params {
    enabled = switch { from = "value1", label = "On" },
    amount  = number { from = "value2", default = 6, min = 0, max = 40, step = 1, label = "Drift (px)" },
}

shared hype = 0

local target = 0
local amp = 0
local moving = false

function onEvent(p)
    target = p.enabled ? p.amount : 0
end

function onFrame(dt)
    local goal = target * (0.6 + hype)

    -- Ease toward the goal at the same speed whatever the frame rate is.
    amp += (goal - amp) * min(1, dt / 500)

    if amp < 0.05 and goal == 0 then
        if moving then
            moving = false
            hud.x = 0
            hud.y = 0
        end
        return
    end

    moving = true
    hud.x = noise(time / 1100) * amp
    hud.y = noise(time / 1400 + 37) * amp * 0.6
end
judge_glow.event 
format 1.1
-- Event Showcase 4/31: every hit pops its lane, every miss shakes it.
-- Shows: onHit(note) and onMiss(note) with note.lane / note.judgment / note.offset, a function of your
-- own that returns a value, and the shared "hype" making the pops bigger in the drops.

event {
    name = "Judge Glow",
    color = #FFD166,
    category = "Lanes",
    description = "Hit notes pop their lane (bigger for better judgments), misses flash red and shake the lane.",
}

params {
    enabled = switch { from = "value1", label = "On" },
}

shared hype = 0

local active = false

-- How far a judgment pops its lane.
local function popFor(judgment)
    if judgment == "sick" then return 0.3 end
    if judgment == "good" then return 0.18 end
    return 0.08
end

function onEvent(p)
    active = p.enabled
end

function onHit(note)
    if not active then return end

    local lane = note.lane
    strum[lane].scale = 1 + popFor(note.judgment) * (0.7 + 0.5 * hype)
    tween(strum[lane].scale, 1, steps(3), "backOut")

    -- A dead-on hit (within 15 ms) also nudges the camera.
    if abs(note.offset) < 15 then
        camera.bump += 0.006
    end
end

function onMiss(note)
    if not active then return end

    flash.color = #FF2050
    flash.alpha = 0.22
    tween(flash.alpha, 0, beats(0.5), "quadOut")

    strum[note.lane].wobbleX = 12
    tween(strum[note.lane].wobbleX, 0, beats(0.6), "elasticOut")
end
cam_follow.event 
format 1.1
-- Event Showcase 5/31: the fight camera follows whoever sings. The opponent sings: it leans in toward
-- them. You sing: it pulls back and turns toward you. A bar without notes: back to the middle.
-- Shows: onHit and onOpponentHit as input, one value eased every frame that drives three properties.

event {
    name = "Cam Follow",
    color = #FFB35C,
    category = "Camera",
    description = "The fight camera leans toward whoever sings (0 = off).",
}

params {
    amount = number { from = "value1", default = 1, min = 0, max = 2, step = 0.1, label = "Strength" },
}

local amount = 0
-- -1 = you sing, 1 = the opponent, 0 = nobody.
local target = 0
local level = 0
local lastNote = -100000

function onEvent(p)
    amount = p.amount

    -- Off: let go at once and glide home, so another camera event can take over right away.
    if amount == 0 and level != 0 then
        level = 0
        tween(camera.x, 0, beats(1), "sineInOut")
        tween(camera.z, 0, beats(1), "sineInOut")
        tween(camera.yaw, 0, beats(1), "sineInOut")
    end
end

function onHit(note)
    target = -1
    lastNote = time
end

function onOpponentHit(note)
    target = 1
    lastNote = time
end

function onFrame(dt)
    if amount == 0 then return end

    if time - lastNote > beats(4) then target = 0 end

    level += (target * amount - level) * min(1, dt / 450)

format 1.1
-- Event Showcase 9/31: the receptors get kicked around on the rhythm and settle again - the modchart
-- "kick": a sideways jolt on 0, 0.75, 1.5 and 2.25 of every bar, an up-and-down jolt on 3 and 3.5, each
-- the other way round than the last.
-- Shows: onStep(n) as a rhythm grid, the wobble channels (they stack on .x / .y), local functions.

event {
    name = "Jiggle",
    color = #5CF2FF,
    category = "Lanes",
    description = "The receptors jolt on a rhythm and settle (pixels, 0 = off).",
}

params {
    amount = number { from = "value1", default = 24, min = 0, max = 60, step = 1, label = "Pixels" },
    rhythm = choice { from = "value2", options = { "kick", "beat", "eighths" }, label = "Rhythm" },
}

local amount = 0
local rhythm = "kick"
local flipX = 1
local flipY = 1

-- The whole row sideways.
local function side()
    flipX = -flipX
    for lane = 0, 3 do
        strum[lane].wobbleX = amount * flipX
        tween(strum[lane].wobbleX, 0, beats(0.75), "cubicOut")
    end
end

-- Up and down, every lane a bit differently (the cosine of the lane), so the row zigzags.
local function updown()
    flipY = -flipY
    for lane = 0, 3 do
        strum[lane].wobbleY = amount * 0.8 * flipY * cos(lane * 2)
        tween(strum[lane].wobbleY, 0, beats(0.75), "cubicOut")
    end
end

function onEvent(p)
    amount = p.amount
    rhythm = p.rhythm
end

function onStep(n)
    if amount == 0 then return end

    local s = n % 16

    if rhythm == "kick" then
        if s == 0 or s == 3 or s == 6 or s == 9 then side() end
        if s == 12 or s == 14 then updown() end
    elseif rhythm == "beat" then
        if s % 4 == 0 then side() end
    elseif s % 2 == 0 then
        if s % 4 == 0 then side() else updown() end
    end
end

format 1.1
-- Event Showcase 10/31: the build-up before the drop.
-- Shows: onStep(step) with patterns that speed up (every 4th step, then every 2nd, then every one), a
-- for loop that schedules a 3-2-1 with after(), writing the shared "hype" value, and a beat of silence
-- at the end.

event {
    name = "Build Up",
    color = #FF8A3D,
    category = "Screen",
    description = "Zoom, dark edges, shake and flashes build up over the given beats; 3-2-1 at the end.",
}

params {
    length = number { from = "value1", default = 16, min = 4, max = 64, step = 1, label = "Length (beats)" },
}

shared hype = 0

local active = false
local startBeat = 0
local total = 16

function onEvent(p)
    active = true
    startBeat = beat
    total = p.length

    tween(camera.zoom, 1.12, beats(total - 1), "quadIn")
    vignette.color = #000000
    tween(vignette.alpha, 0.7, beats(total - 1), "quadIn")

    -- 3, 2, 1 on the last three beats.
    for i = 1, 3 do
        after(beats(total - 4 + i), function()
            text[3].value = str(4 - i)
            text[3].x = 0.5
            text[3].y = 0.42
            text[3].color = i == 3 ? #FF5050 : #FFFFFF
            text[3].alpha = 1
            text[3].size = 5
            tween(text[3].size, 3, beats(1), "expoOut")
            tween(text[3].alpha, 0, beats(1), "quadIn")
        end)
    end

    -- The end: everything drops away at once (the drop takes it from there).
    after(beats(total), function()
        active = false
        text[3].value = ""
        camera.shake = 0
        tween(camera.zoom, 1, steps(2))
        tween(vignette.alpha, 0, beats(1))
    end)
end

function onStep(s)
    if not active then return end

    local progress = clamp((beat - startBeat) / total, 0, 1)
    hype = progress

    -- The last beat is silence before the drop - nothing moves.
    if beat - startBeat >= total - 1 then
        camera.shake = 0
        return
    end

    camera.shake = 0.004 * progress ^ 2
    local every = progress < 0.5 ? 4 : progress < 0.75 ? 2 : 1

    if s % every == 0 then
        camera.bump += 0.008 + 0.02 * progress
        flash.color = #FFFFFF
        flash.alpha = 0.1 * progress
        tween(flash.alpha, 0, steps(1))
    end
end

-- modchart's "kade sway". Gentle: they bob up and down a little. Wild: the up-and-down is a tangent, so
-- once a bar they shoot off the screen (half up, half down) and come back from the other side.
-- Shows: the song position in beats with fractions (time / beats(1)), tan(), a level faded in and out.

    name = "Kade Sway",
    color = #8F7CFF,

    amount = number { from = "value2", default = 20, min = 0, max = 60, step = 1, label = "Pixels" },
}

local amount = 20
local target = 0
local level = 0

function onEvent(p)
    if p.mode != "off" then
        mode = p.mode
        amount = p.amount
    end

    target = p.mode == "off" ? 0 : 1
end

function onFrame(dt)
    if target == 0 and level < 0.001 then return end

    level += (target - level) * min(1, dt / 300)
    local b = time / beats(1)
    -- Far enough to be off the screen, not further.

        strum[lane].x = level * amount * sin((b + lane * 0.25) * pi)

        else

        end

-- Event Showcase 12/31: the receptors spin round and slow down into place - the modchart's "confusion"
-- spin. Once, or on every bar / every other bar, each time the other way.
-- Shows: onBeat(b) counted in bars from where the event sits, a guard so a beat never spins twice.

    name = "Spin",
    color = #C45CFF,
    category = "Lanes",
    description = "The receptors spin round and settle: once, or on every (other) bar until Stop.",
}

    mode  = choice { from = "value1", options = { "once", "every bar", "every 2 bars", "stop" }, label = "When" },
    turns = number { from = "value2", default = 1, min = 1, max = 3, step = 1, label = "Turns" },
}

local every = 0
local turns = 1
local dir = 1
local fromBar = 0
local lastBeat = -1

local function spinAt(b)
    if b == lastBeat then return end

    lastBeat = b
    dir = -dir

    for lane = 0, 3 do
        strum[lane].angle = 360 * turns * dir
        tween(strum[lane].angle, 0, beats(2), "cubicOut")
    end

    fromBar = round(time / beats(4))

    if p.mode != "stop" then spinAt(round(time / beats(1))) end

    if every == 0 or b % 4 != 0 then return end

    if (b / 4 - fromBar) % every == 0 then spinAt(b) end

-- Event Showcase 14/31: an impact. A ring runs out over the screen (shaders/shockwave.fsh) and knocks
-- both fighters back: tipped over their heels, squashed, pushed apart - then they spring back.
-- Shows: handing a shader its start time, a shader slot switched off again once it's done, the
-- fighters' pitch / squash / z with "elasticOut".

event {
    name = "Shockwave",
    color = #5CF2FF,
    category = "Screen",
    description = "A ring runs out over the screen and knocks both fighters back.",
}

params {
    strength = number { from = "value1", default = 1, min = 0.2, max = 2, step = 0.1, label = "Strength" },
}

local count = 0

    local s = p.strength
    count += 1
    local mine = count

    -- shockwave.fsh: a = strength, b = speed, c = when it started (song seconds).
    shader[1].file = "shockwave.fsh"
    shader[1].amount = 1
    shader[1].a = s
    shader[1].b = 1.3
    shader[1].c = time / 1000
    after(seconds(1.5), function()
        if count == mine then shader[1].file = "" end
    end)

    camera.shake = 0.012 * s
    tween(camera.shake, 0, beats(1), "quadOut")

    -- Both get pushed apart from wherever they stand right now (Switcheroo may have swapped them).
    local pz = player.z
    local oz = opponent.z
    local apart = player.z <= opponent.z ? 1 : -1
    player.pitch = -14 * s
    player.squash = 0.3 * s
    player.z = pz - 0.35 * s * apart
    opponent.pitch = -14 * s
    opponent.squash = 0.3 * s
    opponent.z = oz + 0.35 * s * apart

    tween(player.pitch, 0, beats(1.5), "elasticOut")
    tween(player.squash, 0, beats(1.2), "elasticOut")
    tween(player.z, pz, beats(1), "cubicOut")
    tween(opponent.pitch, 0, beats(1.5), "elasticOut")
    tween(opponent.squash, 0, beats(1.2), "elasticOut")
    tween(opponent.z, oz, beats(1), "cubicOut")
end
shaders/shockwave.fsh 
// A ring that runs out from the middle, bending the picture as it passes, with a cyan rim.
// params.x = strength, .y = speed (screen heights per second), .z = the moment it started (song
// seconds - a shader keeps no memory, so the script hands it the start).
vec4 effect(vec2 uv) {
    float age = time - params.z;

    if (age < 0.0 || age > 1.4) {
        return pixel(uv);
    }

    vec2 aspect = vec2(resolution.x / resolution.y, 1.0);
    vec2 d = (uv - 0.5) * aspect;
    float r = length(d);
    float ring = r - age * params.y;
    float fade = 1.0 - age / 1.4;
    float bend = exp(-(ring * ring) / 0.004) * params.x * fade;
    vec2 dir = d / max(r, 0.0001);

    // The three colours bent a little differently: a rainbow rim on the ring.
    vec2 off = dir / aspect * bend * 0.04;
    vec3 c = vec3(pixel(uv - off * 1.25).r, pixel(uv - off).g, pixel(uv - off * 0.75).b);
    c += bend * 0.22 * vec3(0.36, 0.95, 1.0);
    return vec4(c, 1.0);
}
