format 1.1
-- Event Showcase 17/31: both fighters drop MineFunkin's own animation and dance a routine of eight
-- moves, one per beat - the opponent mirrored, so they dance like a reflection.
-- Shows: player.animate = false, body parts (pitch / yaw / roll), your own functions as moves, a mirror
-- flag that swaps left and right, puppet[i] with a variable index.

event {
    name = "Dance Routine",
    color = #FFD15C,
    category = "Fighters",
    description = "Both fighters stop their own animation and dance eight moves, one per beat.",
}

params {
    on = bool { from = "value1", default = true, label = "On" },
}

local active = false
local moveTime = 0

-- One arm: side 0 = left, 1 = right. pitch + = forward, roll + = outward (see the docs).
local function arm(who, side, pitch, roll)
    if side == 0 then
        tween(puppet[who].leftArm.pitch, pitch, moveTime, "backOut")
        tween(puppet[who].leftArm.roll, roll, moveTime, "backOut")
    else
        tween(puppet[who].rightArm.pitch, pitch, moveTime, "backOut")
        tween(puppet[who].rightArm.roll, roll, moveTime, "backOut")
    end
end

local function leg(who, side, pitch, roll)
    if side == 0 then
        tween(puppet[who].leftLeg.pitch, pitch, moveTime, "backOut")
        tween(puppet[who].leftLeg.roll, roll, moveTime, "backOut")
    else
        tween(puppet[who].rightLeg.pitch, pitch, moveTime, "backOut")
        tween(puppet[who].rightLeg.roll, roll, moveTime, "backOut")
    end
end

local function lean(who, roll, nod)
    tween(puppet[who].body.roll, roll, moveTime, "backOut")
    tween(puppet[who].head.roll, -roll * 0.6, moveTime, "backOut")
    tween(puppet[who].head.pitch, nod, moveTime, "backOut")
end

-- The moves. `m` mirrors: the opponent uses its other arm and leans the other way.
local function clap(who, m)
    arm(who, 0, 75, -18)
    arm(who, 1, 75, -18)
    leg(who, 0, 0, 4)
    leg(who, 1, 0, 4)
    lean(who, 0, 10)
end

local function spread(who, m)
    arm(who, 0, 0, 90)
    arm(who, 1, 0, 90)
    lean(who, 0, -12)
end

local function reach(who, m)
    local up = m ? 0 : 1
    arm(who, up, 10, 165)
    arm(who, 1 - up, 0, 15)
    lean(who, m ? 10 : -10, -8)
end

local function point(who, m)
    local hand = m ? 0 : 1
    arm(who, hand, 95, 5)
    arm(who, 1 - hand, -25, 30)
    lean(who, m ? -6 : 6, 0)
end

local function squat(who, m)
    arm(who, 0, 50, 25)
    arm(who, 1, 50, 25)
    leg(who, 0, 0, 16)
    leg(who, 1, 0, 16)
    puppet[who].squash = 0.25
    tween(puppet[who].squash, 0, beats(1), "elasticOut")
    lean(who, 0, 15)
end

local function jump(who, m)
    arm(who, 0, 0, 165)
    arm(who, 1, 0, 165)
    leg(who, 0, 0, 0)
    leg(who, 1, 0, 0)
    lean(who, 0, -15)
    tween(puppet[who].y, 0.5, beats(0.25), "quadOut")
    after(beats(0.25), function() tween(puppet[who].y, 0, beats(0.25), "quadIn") end)
end

local function spin(who, m)
    arm(who, 0, 0, 70)
    arm(who, 1, 0, 70)
    lean(who, 0, 0)
    puppet[who].turn = 0
    tween(puppet[who].turn, m ? -360 : 360, beats(0.9), "quadInOut")
end

local function kick(who, m)
    local foot = m ? 0 : 1
    leg(who, foot, 70, 0)
    leg(who, 1 - foot, -10, 0)
    arm(who, foot, -30, 25)
    arm(who, 1 - foot, 40, 25)
    lean(who, 0, 0)
end

local function move(who, n)
    local m = who == 1
    local k = n % 8
    if k == 0 then clap(who, m)
    elseif k == 1 then spread(who, m)
    elseif k == 2 then reach(who, m)
    elseif k == 3 then point(who, m)
    elseif k == 4 then squat(who, m)
    elseif k == 5 then kick(who, m)
    elseif k == 6 then jump(who, m)
    else spin(who, m) end
end

function onEvent(p)
    active = p.on
    moveTime = beats(0.25)

    if p.on then
        player.animate = false
        opponent.animate = false
    else
        resetPuppet("both", beats(1))
    end
end

function onBeat(b)
    if not active then return end

    move(0, b)
    move(1, b)
end

format 1.1
-- Event Showcase 18/31: the camera swings around the fighters (fights only).
-- Shows: camera.x / .y / .z / .yaw / .pitch together - moving and turning so the point between the
-- fighters stays in the middle, pulling back and rising the further it swings so both stay in view.

event {
    name = "Orbit Cam",
    color = #7C6BFF,
    category = "Camera",
    description = "Swings the fight camera around the fighters to an angle (0 = home).",
}

params {
    angle  = number { from = "value1", default = 30, min = -60, max = 60, step = 1, label = "Angle" },
    length = number { from = "value2", default = 8, min = 0, max = 32, step = 0.5, label = "Beats" },
}

-- The point it circles, from the camera, in blocks (right, ahead): halfway between the fighters in the
-- default fight layout. Positive angles swing it to the left side, away from the line through both
-- fighters - around -25 the opponent would hide right behind you.
local pivotX = 0.55
local pivotZ = 7.25
local from = 0
local to = 0
local duration = 0
local elapsed = 0
local moving = false

function onEvent(p)
    from = camera.yaw
    to = p.angle
    duration = max(1, beats(p.length))
    elapsed = 0
    moving = true
end

function onFrame(dt)
    if not moving then return end

    elapsed += dt
    local t = clamp(elapsed / duration, 0, 1)
    -- sineInOut by hand: the angle eases, and x / z follow it on the circle.
    local k = 0.5 - 0.5 * cos(t * 3.14159265)
    local angle = lerp(from, to, k)
    local a = angle * 3.14159265 / 180
    -- Further round = further back (up to 1.6 times the distance at 30 degrees) and higher.
    local back = 1 + 0.02 * abs(angle)
    local rx = -pivotX * cos(a) - pivotZ * sin(a)
    local rz = pivotX * sin(a) - pivotZ * cos(a)

    camera.yaw = angle
    camera.x = pivotX + rx * back
    camera.z = pivotZ + rz * back
    camera.y = 0.04 * abs(angle)
    camera.pitch = -0.15 * abs(angle)

    if t >= 1 then moving = false end
end

format 1.1
-- Event Showcase 19/31: lyrics that appear word by word.
-- Shows: up to six parameters read from the parts of one value ("EVERY,EFFECT,YOU,SEE"), a for loop
-- that builds the line and schedules each step with after() - every after() keeps the line as it was
-- when it was scheduled - and "break" once the words run out.

event {
    name = "Word by Word",
    color = #FFE066,
    category = "Text",
    description = "value1 = up to six words, comma separated; value2 = beats per word, colour.",
}

params {
    w1 = text { from = "value1.1", label = "Word 1" },
    w2 = text { from = "value1.2", label = "Word 2" },
    w3 = text { from = "value1.3", label = "Word 3" },
    w4 = text { from = "value1.4", label = "Word 4" },
    w5 = text { from = "value1.5", label = "Word 5" },
    w6 = text { from = "value1.6", label = "Word 6" },
    per  = number { from = "value2.1", default = 1, min = 0.25, max = 4, step = 0.25, label = "Beats per word" },
    tint = color  { from = "value2.2", default = #FFFFFF, label = "Colour" },
}

local shown = 0

function onEvent(p)
    shown += 1
    local mine = shown
    local line = ""
    local words = 0

    text[2].x = 0.5
    text[2].y = 0.72
    text[2].color = p.tint
    text[2].alpha = 1

    for i = 1, 6 do
        local word = i == 1 ? p.w1 : i == 2 ? p.w2 : i == 3 ? p.w3 : i == 4 ? p.w4 : i == 5 ? p.w5 : p.w6
        if word == nil then break end

        line = words == 0 ? word : line .. " " .. word
        words += 1

        local upTo = line
        after(beats((i - 1) * p.per), function()
            if shown != mine then return end
            text[2].value = upTo
            text[2].size = 1.6
            tween(text[2].size, 1.25, beats(0.5), "backOut")
        end)
    end

    -- The line stays two beats after its last word, then fades.
    after(beats(words * p.per + 2), function()
        if shown == mine then
            tween(text[2].alpha, 0, beats(1))
        end
    end)
end

format 1.1
-- Event Showcase 23/31: the lanes spread out over the whole width of the screen and slide along it,
-- wrapping round at the edge - the modchart's scroller. Each one bobs toward the middle of the screen
-- while it travels. Switched off, they stop and glide home.
-- Shows: a lane's real spot on the screen (screen.width, strums.spacing), % to wrap round, an ease
-- written by hand (inOut) for values that aren't properties, the strum background faded meanwhile.

event {
    name = "Scroller",
    color = #5CFFB0,
    category = "Lanes",
    description = "The lanes spread across the screen and slide sideways, wrapping round at the edges.",
}

params {
    on    = bool   { from = "value1", default = true, label = "On" },
    speed = number { from = "value2", default = 1, min = -2, max = 2, step = 0.25, label = "Screens per 2 bars" },
}

-- 0 = idle, 1 = scrolling, 2 = gliding home.
local state = 0
local speed = 1
local onAt = 0
local offAt = 0
-- How far it has scrolled, in screen widths.
local pos = 0
-- The strum background's opacity before it faded.
local under = 0.65

local function inOut(t)
    t = clamp(t, 0, 1)
    return t < 0.5 ? 4 * t * t * t : 1 - pow(-2 * t + 2, 3) / 2
end

function onEvent(p)
    speed = p.speed

    if p.on and state != 1 then
        state = 1
        onAt = time
        pos = 0
        under = underlay.alpha
        tween(underlay.alpha, 0, beats(4))
    elseif not p.on and state == 1 then
        state = 2
        offAt = time
        tween(underlay.alpha, under, beats(2))
    end
end

function onFrame(dt)
    if state == 0 then return end

    local w = screen.width
    local s = strums.spacing

    -- A screen width every two bars, like the modchart (frozen while gliding home, so no lane wraps
    -- round on its way back).
    if state == 1 then pos += dt / beats(8) * speed end

    -- Spread from their own spacing to a quarter of the screen each, over a bar.
    local spread = inOut((time - onAt) / beats(4))
    local leave = state == 2 ? inOut((time - offAt) / beats(2)) : 0
    local gap = lerp(s, w / 4, spread)
    local left = lerp(w / 2 - 1.5 * s, w / 8, spread)
    local b = time / beats(1)

    for lane = 0, 3 do
        local home = w / 2 + (lane - 1.5) * s
        local x = (left + lane * gap + pos * w) % w
        local toMiddle = strum[lane].isDown ? -1 : 1
        local bob = toMiddle * screen.height * 0.05 * (1 + sin(b * pi + lane * pi / 2))

        strum[lane].x = (x - home) * (1 - leave)
        strum[lane].y = bob * spread * (1 - leave)
        -- A little see-through right at the edges, where a lane jumps round.
        strum[lane].alpha = lerp(1, clamp(0.35 + min(x, w - x) / 40, 0.35, 1), spread * (1 - leave))
    end

    if state == 2 and leave >= 1 then
        state = 0

        for lane = 0, 3 do
            strum[lane].x = 0
            strum[lane].y = 0
            strum[lane].alpha = 1
        end
    end
end

format 1.1
-- Event Showcase 24/31: the fighters jump over each other and swap places - and back, as often as you
-- like.
-- Shows: player.x / .z and opponent.x / .z in the fight's frame, .turn by 180 so they still face each
-- other, a jump arc from two tweens, a variable that remembers which side they're on.

event {
    name = "Switcheroo",
    color = #5CFFB5,
    category = "Fighters",
    description = "The fighters jump and swap places. swap = to the other side, on / off = swapped / home.",
}

params {
    mode = choice { from = "value1", options = { "swap", "on", "off" }, label = "Mode" },
}

-- Where the opponent stands from you, in blocks: the default fight layout (7.4 ahead, 3 to the left).
local ahead = 7.4
local side = -3
local swapped = false

local function hop(who, x, z, turn)
    local dur = beats(1)
    tween(puppet[who].x, x, dur, "sineInOut")
    tween(puppet[who].z, z, dur, "sineInOut")
    tween(puppet[who].turn, turn, dur, "sineInOut")
    -- The arc: up for half the time, down for the other half; stretched in the air, squashed on landing.
    tween(puppet[who].y, 2.5, dur / 2, "quadOut")
    after(dur / 2, function() tween(puppet[who].y, 0, dur / 2, "quadIn") end)
    puppet[who].squash = -0.2
    after(dur, function()
        puppet[who].squash = 0.3
        tween(puppet[who].squash, 0, beats(1), "elasticOut")
    end)
end

function onEvent(p)
    local want = p.mode == "swap" ? not swapped : p.mode == "on"

    if want == swapped then return end

    swapped = want

    if swapped then
        hop(0, side, ahead, 180)
        hop(1, -side, -ahead, 180)
    else
        hop(0, 0, 0, 0)
        hop(1, 0, 0, 0)
    end
end

halo.event 
format 1.1
-- Event Showcase 29/31: the lanes ride round in a ring like a carousel - the modchart's halo. The ones
-- at the back are smaller and fainter, so it reads as a ring seen from the front. Fall: the ring keeps
-- turning and the lanes drop off the screen one by one.
-- Shows: x / y / scale / alpha from one angle per lane, a ring centred on the screen however the lanes
-- are spaced.

event {
    name = "Halo",
    color = #FFE35C,
    category = "Lanes",
    description = "The lanes ride round in a ring. Fall = they drop off the screen from it.",
}

params {
    mode = choice { from = "value1", options = { "on", "fall", "off" }, label = "Mode" },
}

local mode = "off"
local onAt = 0
local fallAt = 0
local level = 0

function onEvent(p)
    if p.mode == "on" and mode == "off" then onAt = time end
    if p.mode == "fall" then fallAt = time end
    mode = p.mode
end

function onFrame(dt)
    if mode == "off" and level < 0.001 then return end

    level += ((mode == "off" ? 0 : 1) - level) * min(1, dt / 350)

    local s = strums.spacing
    local rx = s * 2.4
    local ry = s * 0.55
    -- One turn a bar.
    local turn = (time - onAt) / beats(4) * 2 * pi

    for lane = 0, 3 do
        -- Starts with lanes 0 and 1 on the left, 2 and 3 on the right.
        local ang = 2 * pi * lane / 4 - 0.75 * pi + turn
        -- 1 = at the front, -1 = at the back.
        local depth = cos(ang)
        local toMiddle = strum[lane].isDown ? -1 : 1
        local fall = 0

        if mode == "fall" then
            fall = pow(clamp((time - fallAt - beats(lane * 0.25)) / beats(3), 0, 1), 3) * screen.height * 1.3
        end

        -- Around the middle of the screen: undo the lane's own place, then the ring.
        strum[lane].x = level * (rx * sin(ang) - (lane - 1.5) * s)
        strum[lane].y = level * (ry * depth + toMiddle * ry) + fall
        strum[lane].scale = 1 - level * 0.2 * (1 - depth)
        strum[lane].alpha = 1 - level * 0.25 * (1 - depth)
    end

    if mode == "off" and level < 0.001 then
        for lane = 0, 3 do
            strum[lane].x = 0
            strum[lane].y = 0
            strum[lane].scale = 1
            strum[lane].alpha = 1
        end
    end
end

-- the screen fades to black under it - and onEnd.

    tween(strums.alpha, 0.55, beats(8), "sineInOut")

end

function onEnd()
    log("showcase finished: score", player.score, "accuracy", player.accuracy, "misses", player.misses)
end
power_off.event 
format 1.1
-- Event Showcase 31/31: the end - the old TV comes back and switches off. The picture squeezes into a
-- glowing line, the line into a dot, the dot fades out.
-- Shows: the same shader as Power On, played backwards, ending on screen.color.

event {
    name = "Power Off",
    color = #5CF2FF,
    category = "Screen",
    description = "The screen curves into an old TV and switches off into a dot (the collapse comes after one beat).",
}

function onEvent(p)
    shader[0].file = "crt.fsh"
    shader[0].amount = 1
    shader[0].a = 0
    shader[0].b = 1
    shader[0].c = 1
    shader[0].d = 0
    tween(shader[0].a, 1, beats(1), "sineOut")
    tween(shader[0].d, 1, beats(1), "sineOut")

    -- Pressed into a line (glowing brighter the thinner it gets), then into a dot.
    after(beats(1), function() tween(shader[0].c, 0, beats(0.4), "expoIn") end)
    after(beats(1.4), function() tween(shader[0].b, 0, beats(0.35), "expoIn") end)

    -- Black under the shader: the dot has nothing left to show and fades.
    after(beats(1.75), function()
        screen.color = #000000
        tween(screen.alpha, 1, beats(1))
    end)
end

docs.title: The music
docs.text:
Two simple synth leads play the melodies: a hollow square wave for you, and a nasal pulse for the opponent. They're the song's two vocal tracks, so a miss mutes your lead.

The music, both leads, the chart and the logo were made with a script; the event files and the shaders are written by hand.

docs.title: Song scripts
docs.text:
Some things don't happen at one moment - they happen all the time. The camera popping on every hit. A combo counter. The lanes swaying through a whole verse. For those you don't want to place an event on every note. You want a script that just listens to the whole song.

If you know Psych Engine, those are its song scripts. MineFunkin doesn't need a separate kind of file for them, because of one simple rule: every callback of every loaded event runs for the whole song - whether the chart ever places that event or not. So a file with only onBeat, onHit or onFrame and no onEvent is a song script.

format 1.1
-- A song script: the camera pops on every hit, harder on a "sick".

event {
    name = "Hit Pop",
    category = "Song script",
    description = "No chart event needed - it runs for the whole song.",
}

function onHit(note)
    camera.bump += note.judgment == "sick" ? 0.02 : 0.008
end

Drop it into the song's folder and it's on from the very first note. It still needs its event { name } line, though - that's how it shows up in the editor's footer and in the log.

docs.title: What a song script can listen to
docs.text:
When Callback the song is set up, the countdown, the music starts, the end onStart, onCountdown, onSongStart, onEnd every beat, step, section (4 beats), frame onBeat, onStep, onSection, onFrame your hits and misses, the opponent's notes onHit, onMiss, onOpponentHit the lane keys onKeyPress, onKeyRelease, onGhostTap pause, resume, health running out onPause, onResume, onFail

A song can have as many as you like, side by side - say one for the modchart, one for the stage, one for the sounds. Keeping them apart makes each one easier to find later.

docs.title: Song script or chart event?
Talking to each other: shared
docs.text:
Every file keeps its variables to itself. When two files need to agree on something, use shared: a shared variable is one single value for every file that declares it under the same name.

-- build_up.event
shared hype = 0

function onEvent(p)
    hype = 1
end

-- cam_sway.event (a song script)
shared hype = 0

function onFrame(dt)
    hud.angle = sin(time / 400) * 2 * (1 + hype)
end

Both say shared hype, so the moment Build Up sets it, Cam Sway sways harder. The first file that declares it decides the starting value, and like everything else it goes back to that when the song starts over.

docs.title: Starting another event: trigger and call
docs.text:
Sometimes one event should set off another. A script can fire an event as if the chart had placed it right there, or run a function another file defines:

format 1.1

event { name = "Drop Combo" }

function onEvent(p)
    trigger("Screen Shake", 0.6, 0.4)    -- runs that event's onEvent with value1 / value2
    call("spawnConfetti", 12)            -- every other file with a function spawnConfetti runs it
end

trigger takes the event's name and its two values, just like the chart editor writes them. call runs the function of that name in every other event file of the song that has one. Typo in the name? It's written to the event log once, and your script carries on.

docs.title: Practice or fight: only and song.mode
docs.text:
A song can be played at the Retro TV (practice, on your own) or at a Speaker (a fight, with people watching). Some things only make sense in one of them - a camera swinging round looks great in a fight, but practice has no world for it to swing through.

If a whole file belongs to fights only, say so in its header:

event {
    name = "Camera Swing",
    only = "fight",      -- runs only in fights (and their replays, and when someone watches from inside)
}

For smaller decisions inside a file, ask song.mode. It's "practice", "fight", "replay" or "watch":

function onBeat(b)
    if song.mode == "practice" then return end
    camera.yaw = b % 2 == 0 ? 2 : -2
end

docs.title: Cutscenes: no countdown, no keys
docs.text:
Want the song to open with a little scene before anyone has to play?

function onStart()
    hud.countdown = false        -- no 3-2-1-GO (onCountdown still runs, so you can do your own)
end

function onEvent(p)              -- placed where the cutscene starts
    strums.input = false         -- the lane keys do nothing ...
    after(seconds(8), function() strums.input = true end)   -- ... until it's over
end

Leave the chart empty under a cutscene - notes that come by while the keys are off count as misses.

docs.title: A song that starts later (practice)
docs.text: A difficulty can start somewhere in the middle of the song - great for a practice version of a long song's hard last part. That's a key in the song file, not a script: "start". Your scripts still see the whole song, though: everything before the start is run through quickly in the background, so effects and stages are exactly where they'd be.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Built-in events run first, then the song's own files in path order. If two scripts write the same property in the same frame, the later one wins. So give every effect that runs all the time its own property - the Event Showcase calls them "channels".
  • While the game is paused or counting down, onFrame, onBeat, onStep and the timers wait. Only onCountdown, onPause and onResume run then. Tweens follow the song's time, so they wait too.
  • A song script that crashes while running is switched off for the rest of that run. What went wrong is in the event log.
  • Players can switch off built-in events in their options (Options › MineFunkin › Song effects) - but never your song's own files.
  • An empty song script to start from is in Templates.

docs.title: Sounds and music
docs.text:
Sound is half the feeling of a song. A cymbal crash on the drop, rain under a slow part, thunder rolling every eight beats, the opponent's voice cutting out for a moment of silence - your scripts can do all of that.

There are two kinds of sound to play with: the song's own audio (the instrumental and the vocal tracks), which you can make louder or quieter, and sounds of your own, played from .ogg files in the song's folder.

docs.title: The song's audio
docs.text:
Three properties, each from 0 to 1, on top of whatever volume the player has set: volume.inst (the instrumental), volume.player (your vocals - the ones a miss mutes) and volume.opponent.

-- The opponent's voice drops out for the drop, then comes back.
function onEvent(p)
    tween(volume.opponent, 0, beats(2))
    after(beats(16), function() tween(volume.opponent, 1, beats(1)) end)
end

The volumes go back to 1 when the song ends, so you can't leave anyone in silence.

docs.title: Sounds of your own
docs.text:
A sound is an .ogg file in the song's folder or its events/ folder. Five calls are all you need:

Call What it does playSound("boom.ogg"[, volume]) Plays it once. playSound("boom.ogg", 1, "boom") ... under the name "boom", so you can fade or stop it later. loopSound("rain.ogg", 0.6, "rain") Plays it over and over until it's stopped (a loop always needs a name). soundVolume("rain", 0.2[, duration]) Fades it to that volume (0-1). stopSound("rain") Stops it. 
format 1.1

event { name = "Storm" }

function onEvent(p)
    loopSound("rain.ogg", 0.6, "rain")         -- until stopped or the song ends
    after(beats(16), function()
        soundVolume("rain", 0, beats(4))       -- fades out over 4 beats ...
    end)
    after(beats(20), function()
        stopSound("rain")                      -- ... and stops
    end)
end

function onBeat(b)
    if b % 8 == 0 then playSound("thunder.ogg", 1, "thunder") end   -- a new one replaces the one still ringing
end

docs.title: How they behave
docs.text:
A few rules, so nothing surprises you:

  • One name, one sound: a new sound under the same name stops the old one.
  • Volumes are 0-1, on top of MineFunkin's own volume (the sound tray, numpad +/-).
  • Pausing the song pauses the named sounds too; they go on with the song.
  • The song's end stops the loops; the other sounds ring out. A restart or leaving the song stops them all.
  • Limits: a sound may be at most 5 minutes long (for longer music, use the song's own audio), and at most 32 of a song's sounds play at once - so an accidental playSound in onFrame can't blow up anyone's speakers. The event log mentions it once when that happens, and names any sound file it can't find.
  • Each sound file is read once per song and let go when the song closes.

docs.title: A tick on every "sick"
docs.text:
A tiny reward for hitting it perfectly:

function onHit(note)
    if note.judgment == "sick" then playSound("tick.ogg", 0.4) end
end

docs.title: Your own countdown voice
docs.text:
Tired of the standard 3-2-1? Record your own:

format 1.1

event { name = "Countdown Voice", category = "Song script" }

function onCountdown(n)
    playSound(n == 0 ? "go.ogg" : n == 1 ? "one.ogg" : n == 2 ? "two.ogg" : "three.ogg")
end

docs.title: The music drops out on a miss
docs.text:
Harsh, but it makes every miss count:

function onMiss(note)
    volume.inst = 0.3
    tween(volume.inst, 1, beats(1), "quadIn")
end

docs.title: Rain that follows the song's mood
docs.text:
The rain gets quieter as the song gets louder - with a little help from a shared variable:

format 1.1

event { name = "Rain", category = "Song script" }

shared hype = 0      -- set by another event when the song gets loud (0-1)

function onStart()
    loopSound("rain.ogg", 0.5, "rain")
end

function onBeat(b)
    soundVolume("rain", 0.5 - 0.4 * hype, beats(1))     -- quieter when the song gets loud
end

Psych: playSound, playMusic, stopSound, soundFadeIn / soundFadeOut, setSoundVolume, setProperty("vocals.volume", ...)

docs.title: Stages and sprites
docs.text:
In a fight, the two fighters stand in the actual Minecraft world - which is great, until your song is set in a burning city and the fight happens in a birch forest. That's what a stage is for: pictures around the fighters. A sky behind them, animated fire, dust drifting in front of them, a logo glowing under the lanes.

There's no special stage file. A stage is just a song script that sets up a few pictures in onStart.

fights The world, the fight camera and the "stage" layer behind the fighters only exist in a fight. In practice at the Retro TV, the same pictures are drawn under the two puppets - so your stage still shows up there, it just doesn't move with a camera.

docs.title: Start with this
docs.text:
format 1.1
-- The song's stage: a background behind the fighters, fog in front of them.

event {
    name = "Stage",
    category = "Song script",
    description = "Sets up the song's stage pictures.",
}

function onStart()
    preload("stage/sky.png")
    preload("stage/fog.png")

    -- Behind the fighters, moving with the camera like the world.
    image[0].file = "stage/sky.png"
    image[0].layer = "stage"
    image[0].width = 1.5          -- bigger than the screen, so the camera's turns never show its edges
    image[0].height = 1.5
    image[0].follow = 1

    -- In front of the fighters, under the lanes and the HUD.
    image[1].file = "stage/fog.png"
    image[1].layer = "back"
    image[1].width = 1
    image[1].height = 1
    image[1].alpha = 0.5
end

Put the pictures in the song's folder (here in a stage/ folder inside it), save the script as stage.event next to the chart, and start a fight. That's a stage.

docs.title: Where a picture goes: layers
docs.text:
Every picture sits on a layer, which decides what it's in front of and what it's behind:

Layer In a fight Good for "stage" painted onto the world, behind the fighters the background, the sky, a floor, sprites behind the characters "back" in front of the fighters, behind the strum background fog, rain, bars, things in front of the characters "lanes" on the strum background, under the notes a logo, a glow behind the lanes "front" over the playfield and the HUD flashes of pictures, captions "top" over everything, even a fade to black a title that stays readable

Inside one layer, order sorts them: higher numbers are drawn later, so they end up on top.

image[2].layer = "stage"
image[2].order = 1           -- in front of image[0] (order 0), still behind the fighters

docs.title: Moving with the camera
docs.text:
Normally a picture stays exactly where you put it on the screen. But in a fight the camera never sits still: it turns towards whoever's singing, nudges a little on each of your hits and pops on the beat - and the fighters move with it. A background that stays put would look like the fighters are sliding around on top of it. (It looks as bad as it sounds.)

follow = 1 fixes that: the picture moves with the camera exactly like the world does.

  • x, y, width and height say where it sits while the camera rests (no turn, no zoom).
  • Values between 0 and 1 move it part of the way - like a scroll factor in Psych: 0.5 for far mountains that move half as much.
  • Only the camera's turns and zoom are followed, not camera.x / .y / .z - a picture has no depth.
  • A pinned fighter stays on its screen spot whatever the camera does: a picture behind a pinned fighter keeps follow = 0, or they drift apart.
  • In practice there's no fight camera: follow does nothing there.

docs.title: Animated pictures
docs.text: Animated backgrounds - fire, TV static, dust, a crowd bopping along - come as sheets of frames. MineFunkin plays both kinds you'll run into.

docs.title: A grid of frames (sprite sheet)
docs.text:
All frames are the same size and sit in a neat grid. Tell MineFunkin how the grid is cut and how fast to play it:

function onStart()
    image[3].file = "fire.png"      -- 4 frames across, 5 down, 20 of them used
    image[3].columns = 4
    image[3].rows = 5
    image[3].frames = 20
    image[3].fps = 24               -- plays by itself, over and over
    image[3].width = 1
    image[3].height = 1
    image[3].layer = "stage"

    image[4].file = "bars.png"      -- a one-shot animation ...
    image[4].columns = 4
    image[4].rows = 3
    image[4].fps = 24
    image[4].loop = false
end

function onBeat(b)
    image[4].frame = 0              -- ... that plays again on every beat
end

docs.title: Psych sprites (Sparrow atlases)
docs.text:
This is what Psych uses: a .png plus a Sparrow .xml of the same name. The frames are packed wherever they fit, trimmed, and sometimes turned on their side - you don't have to care about any of that. Put both files in the song's folder and name the animation you want:

format 1.1

event { name = "Dancing Crowd" }

function onStart()
    image[2].file = "crowd.png"          -- crowd.xml must sit right next to it
    image[2].anim = "crowd bop"          -- every frame whose name starts with this
    image[2].fps = 24
    image[2].width = 0.6
    image[2].y = 0.8
    image[2].layer = "stage"
end

function onHit(n)
    if n.judgment == "sick" then
        image[2].anim = "crowd cheer"    -- another animation of the same sprite
        image[2].frame = 0
        image[2].loop = false
    end
end
  • The frames play in the order of the number at the end of their names (crowd bop0000, crowd bop0001, ...), like Psych's addAnimationByPrefix.
  • frame, fps and loop work as for a sheet. Set frame = 0 to start an animation over.
  • width and height measure the frame's full box, so trimmed frames don't jump around; frames stored turned on their side are turned back.
  • flipX mirrors it - one sprite facing either way.
  • An .xml may be at most 2 MB with at most 4096 frames.

docs.title: Videos
docs.text:
Got a cutscene or a video background? It goes in as a folder of numbered frames: videos/intro/0001.jpg, 0002.jpg, ... (.jpg or .png). Name the folder with a / at the end and play it just like a sheet:

function onEvent(p)
    image[24].file = "videos/intro/"
    image[24].width = 1
    image[24].height = 1
    image[24].layer = "top"
    image[24].fps = 15
    image[24].loop = false
    image[24].frame = 0
end

Any video tool can cut a video into frames like that. With ffmpeg it's one line: ffmpeg -i intro.mp4 -vf fps=15,scale=820:-1 videos/intro/%04d.jpg. MineFunkin only decodes frames right before they're needed and lets go of the ones it has shown, so even a long video won't eat your memory.

The frames have no sound. Either mix the video's sound into the song's audio, or start it with playSound. And during a cutscene, strums.input = false stops the player's keys from doing anything.

docs.title: Blend modes
docs.text:
By default a picture is simply painted over what's under it. image[n].blend mixes it in other ways: "add" for light, fire and glows, "multiply" for shadows and tints, "screen" to brighten softly, "erase" to cut holes. All of them are on blend modes.

image[7].file = "stage/light.png"
image[7].blend = "add"
image[7].layer = "stage"
image[7].follow = 1

docs.title: Sharp or smooth
docs.text: Pictures are drawn with sharp pixels by default, like the rest of the game. Pixel art stays crisp, and sprites with see-through edges don't get weird coloured rims. Big painted art that's shown smaller or turned looks nicer smoothed, though: image[n].smooth = true (that's Psych's antialiasing).

docs.title: Plain boxes
docs.text:
Sometimes you don't need a picture at all, just a coloured box. "solid" is a white box you colour yourself - for bars, a curtain, a coloured sky, a floor:

format 1.1

event { name = "Red Curtain" }

function onEvent(p)
    image[6].file = "solid"
    image[6].color = #B01030
    image[6].width = 1             -- the whole width ...
    image[6].height = 1            -- ... and height
    image[6].layer = "back"
    image[6].alpha = 0
    tween(image[6].alpha, 0.8, beats(2))
end

docs.title: Loading on time
docs.text:
A picture loads in the background the first time it's drawn, and appears once it's ready - for a big one, that can be a few frames late. Usually nobody notices, but on a big moment you will. So preload whatever the stage shows later in onStart, and it loads during the countdown instead.

function onStart()
    preload("stage/fire.png")
    preload("stage/night.png")
end

docs.title: Coming from a Psych stage
docs.text:
A Psych stage is a stages/name.json (camera zoom, character spots) plus a stages/name.lua that makes the sprites. Good news: the Lua part translates almost line by line.

Psych stage Lua MineFunkin makeLuaSprite("sky", "sky", x, y) image[0].file = "sky.png" and x / y as a share of the screen (0.5 = the middle), not world pixels makeAnimatedLuaSprite + addAnimationByPrefix + playAnim image[n].file (+ the .xml), image[n].anim = "prefix", image[n].frame = 0 makeGraphic("black", w, h, "000000") image[n].file = "solid", image[n].color = #000000 scaleObject("sky", 1.2, 1.2) image[n].width / image[n].height setScrollFactor("sky", 0.5, 0.5) image[n].follow = 0.5 (one number for both directions) addLuaSprite("sky", false) (behind the characters) image[n].layer = "stage" addLuaSprite("fog", true) (in front of them) image[n].layer = "back" setObjectOrder image[n].order setProperty("sky.visible", false) image[n].alpha = 0 (or file = "") setProperty("sky.flipX", true) image[n].flipX = true precacheImage("sky") preload("sky.png") defaultCamZoom in the json camera.zoom / camera.fov - see the fight camera

The characters are the real Minecraft fighters, so character spots and character jsons have nothing to translate to - the fighters stand where the Speaker puts them. If you want them somewhere else, or looking like someone else, the fighters page shows you how to move, pin and re-skin them.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text: You have room for a lot - 32 pictures at once (image[0] ... image[31]) and up to 128 different picture files per song: .png, at most 8192 pixels a side and 16 MB as a file, 512 MB of video memory together. A video folder: up to 20,000 .jpg / .png frames, 2048 pixels a side, 8 MB a frame. Everything is freed when the song closes.

docs.title: Templates
docs.text:
Nobody likes starting from a blank file. So here are some that already work: copy one into a text editor, save it with .event at the end in the song's folder (or its events/ folder), and change it into whatever you need. Each one runs as it is - you can place it and press play before you've touched a line.

I want ... Template an event I place in the chart, that does one thing One moment an event that switches an effect on and off On and off something that runs for the whole song, no chart event Song script lanes and notes that move Modchart pictures around the fighters Stage every callback, to see what's there Everything

docs.title: One moment
docs.text:
The simplest kind: you place it in the chart, something happens right there.

format 1.1
-- What this event does, in one line.

event {
    name = "My Event",
    color = #7C6BFF,
    category = "Custom",
    description = "Shown in the chart editor.",
}

params {
    strength = number { from = "value1", default = 1, min = 0, max = 3, step = 0.1, label = "Strength" },
}

function onEvent(p)
    flash(#FFFFFF, beats(0.5))
    camera.bump += 0.03 * p.strength
end

docs.title: On and off
docs.text:
For effects that last a while. Place it once with On ticked where the effect starts, and once more with it unticked where it stops - the code in onBeat runs in between.

format 1.1
-- An effect that runs from one chart event to the next.

event {
    name = "My Effect",
    category = "Custom",
    description = "On: the effect runs. Off: it stops.",
}

params {
    on = bool { from = "value1", default = true, label = "On" },
}

local active = false

function onEvent(p)
    active = p.on

    if not active then
        resetLanes(beats(1))      -- put back what the effect moved
    end
end

function onBeat(b)
    if not active then return end
    -- the effect, on every beat
end

docs.title: Song script
docs.text:
No chart event needed at all. Every callback of every event file in the song runs from start to end, so this one simply listens - to every hit, every miss, whatever you put in.

format 1.1
-- Runs for the whole song.

event {
    name = "My Song Script",
    category = "Song script",
    description = "No chart event needed.",
}

function onStart()
    -- before the countdown
end

function onHit(note)
    -- every note you hit
end

function onMiss(note)
    -- every miss
end

docs.title: Modchart
docs.text:
All the lane movement of a song in one file, so you don't have to hunt for it later. This one makes the lanes wobble between steps 64 and 128, then puts them back.

format 1.1
-- The song's modchart: everything that moves the lanes, in one place.

event {
    name = "Modchart",
    category = "Song script",
    description = "Runs for the whole song.",
}

function onFrame(dt)
    -- moves all the time; work it out from time or beat
    if step >= 64 and step < 128 then
        for lane = 0, 3 do
            strum[lane].wobbleX = 12 * sin(time / 300 + lane)
        end
    end
end

function onStep(n)
    if n == 128 then resetLanes(beats(1)) end
end

Lots more ideas in the Modcharts guide.

docs.title: Stage
docs.text:
A background behind the fighters. Swap the file name for your own picture.

format 1.1
-- The song's stage pictures.

event {
    name = "Stage",
    category = "Song script",
    description = "A background behind the fighters.",
}

function onStart()
    preload("stage/background.png")

    image[0].file = "stage/background.png"
    image[0].layer = "stage"      -- behind the fighters
    image[0].width = 1.5
    image[0].height = 1.5
    image[0].follow = 1           -- moves with the fight camera
end

Animated sprites, layers and more in Stages and sprites.

docs.title: Everything
docs.text:
Every callback the game has, all empty. Handy when you want to see what's there - delete the ones you don't need.

format 1.1
-- Every callback the game has.

event {
    name = "Everything",
    category = "Custom",
}

function onStart() end            -- the song is set up, before the countdown
function onCountdown(n) end       -- 3, 2, 1, then 0 for "go"
function onSongStart() end        -- the music starts
function onEvent(p) end           -- the chart reaches this event
function onBeat(b) end            -- every beat
function onStep(n) end            -- every step (four per beat)
function onSection(n) end         -- every 4 beats
function onFrame(dt) end          -- every frame, dt = ms since the last one
function onHit(note) end          -- you hit a note
function onMiss(note) end         -- you missed
function onOpponentHit(note) end  -- the opponent plays a note
function onKeyPress(lane) end     -- a lane key goes down
function onKeyRelease(lane) end   -- a lane key comes up
function onGhostTap(lane) end     -- a press with nothing to hit
function onPause() end            -- the song is paused
function onResume() end           -- it goes on
function onFail() end             -- your health ran out (fights)
function onEnd() end              -- the song was played to its end

What each one gets and when exactly it runs: Callbacks.

docs.title: Your first event
docs.text:
Let's build one together. By the end of this page you'll have Beat Flash: an event that flashes the screen on every beat, in a colour you pick, until you switch it off again. Nothing fancy - but it's a real event you could put in a real chart, and on the way you'll meet almost everything the bigger ones are made of.

Each step adds one idea. Take your time; it's about ten minutes.

You'll need a song to try it on. Any folder in .minecraft/MineFunkin/client/songs/ works. The Event Showcase is a nice one, since it was made for playing around.

docs.title: 1. The file
docs.text:
Make a new text file called beat_flash.event and put it in the song's folder (next to its .mfkn chart), or in an events/ folder inside it. Every event file starts the same way: a line saying which version of the language it's written in (always format 1.1), and an event { } block with its name.

format 1.1

event {
    name = "Beat Flash",
}

Believe it or not, that's already a working event. It doesn't do anything yet, but the chart editor knows it: open the song in the editor (Retro TV → Editor), click the event type in the inspector, and there's Beat Flash under Custom.

Changing the file while the editor is open

The editor reads the song's folder when it opens. So after you save your file, press Reload at the bottom of the inspector. If you made a typo, that's also where you'll see it - with the line and what's wrong.

docs.title: 2. Make it do something
docs.text:
When the song reaches your event in the chart, the game calls onEvent. That's where your code goes:

format 1.1

event {
    name = "Beat Flash",
}

function onEvent(p)
    flash.color = #FFFFFF
    flash.alpha = 0.6
    tween(flash.alpha, 0, beats(0.5), "quadOut")
end

Read it out loud and it almost explains itself: make the flash white, show it at 60 %, then fade it to nothing over half a beat. Place the event somewhere (click the EVENTS lane), press Space, and when the song gets there - flash!

flash is a property: a value the game looks at every frame. You can set it right away, or animate it with tween. Times are in milliseconds, and beats(0.5) works out how many milliseconds half a beat is at this song's tempo, so you never have to do that maths yourself.

There's a shorter way

For a plain flash there's a shortcut: flash(#FFFFFF, beats(0.5)) does all of the above in one line. We're building it by hand here so you see how properties and tween work - you'll want them the moment you need something the shortcuts don't do.

docs.title: 3. Let people pick the colour
docs.text:
A flash that's always white gets boring fast. Parameters fix that: they describe the event's two values (value1 and value2 in the chart), and the editor turns them into proper controls.

params {
    tint = color { from = "value1", default = #FFFFFF, label = "Colour" },
}

function onEvent(p)
    flash.color = p.tint
    flash.alpha = 0.6
    tween(flash.alpha, 0, beats(0.5), "quadOut")
end

Press Reload, and the inspector now has a Colour field with a swatch. Whatever you pick ends up in value1 as #RRGGBB, and p.tint hands it back to you as a colour. Numbers with sliders, switches, lanes, dropdowns - all the kinds are on Parameters.

docs.title: 4. Flash on every beat
docs.text:
Now the fun part. Instead of flashing once, the event switches a mode on, and the flashing happens on every beat until another Beat Flash switches it off. For that you need two things: a variable that lives for the whole song (a local at the top of the file), and a second callback, onBeat.

params {
    on   = bool  { from = "value1", default = true, label = "On" },
    tint = color { from = "value2", default = #FFFFFF, label = "Colour" },
}

local active = false
local tint = #FFFFFF

function onEvent(p)
    active = p.on
    tint = p.tint
end

function onBeat(b)
    if not active then return end

    flash.color = tint
    flash.alpha = 0.45
    tween(flash.alpha, 0, beats(0.75), "quadOut")
end

Place one Beat Flash with On ticked where it should start, and another with On unticked where it should stop. onBeat gets called on every single beat of the song - it just leaves straight away while active is false.

Every callback runs, all the time

onBeat runs whether your event has fired yet or not. That's why it checks active first. It's also a neat trick: a file with only onBeat and no chart event at all still works - that's a song script.

docs.title: 5. Make it feel good
docs.text:
Two small touches make a big difference: the first beat of every bar hits harder, and the camera pops along with it.

function onBeat(b)
    if not active then return end

    local downbeat = b % 4 == 0
    flash.color = tint
    flash.alpha = downbeat ? 0.7 : 0.35
    tween(flash.alpha, 0, beats(0.75), "quadOut")

    if downbeat then
        camera.bump += 0.04
    end
end

b % 4 is what's left after dividing the beat by 4 - so it's 0 on the first beat of each bar. c ? a : b picks one of two values. And camera.bump is the game's own little zoom pop: it eases back by itself, so you add to it instead of tweening it.

docs.title: 6. When it doesn't do what you expect
docs.text:
It happens to everyone. Ask the script what it's thinking with log:

function onEvent(p)
    active = p.on
    tint = p.tint
    log("Beat Flash", active ? "on" : "off", "in", tint)
end

That line lands in logs/minefunkin-events.log, right next to Minecraft's latest.log - together with every chart event as it fires and every script error. Errors and fixes helps you read it.

docs.title: The whole file
docs.text:
Here's everything together, plus three header lines that make it look nice in the editor:

format 1.1
-- Flashes the screen on every beat until it's switched off again.

event {
    name = "Beat Flash",
    color = #FFE35C,
    category = "Screen",
    description = "Flashes the screen on every beat (harder on the first beat of a bar).",
}

params {
    on   = bool  { from = "value1", default = true, label = "On" },
    tint = color { from = "value2", default = #FFFFFF, label = "Colour" },
}

local active = false
local tint = #FFFFFF

function onEvent(p)
    active = p.on
    tint = p.tint
end

function onBeat(b)
    if not active then return end

    local downbeat = b % 4 == 0
    flash.color = tint
    flash.alpha = downbeat ? 0.7 : 0.35
    tween(flash.alpha, 0, beats(0.75), "quadOut")

    if downbeat then
        camera.bump += 0.04
    end
end

color is the marker's colour in the editor, category puts it into a group in the type picker, and description is what you see when you hover it there.

That's it - you made an event. 🎉

docs.title: Where to next
docs.text: If you want to ... Go to start your next one from a working file Templates - an on/off effect, a song script, a modchart, a stage do common stuff in one line Shortcuts - flashes, fades, zooms, hiding the HUD, flipping the scroll, swapping the fighters react to every hit, miss and beat Song scripts make the lanes sway, spin, fly in Modcharts put pictures and animated sprites around the fighters Stages and sprites play your own sounds, mute the song's tracks Sounds and music copy something small that just works Cookbook look up any name Event API

docs.title: The game window and pop-out windows
docs.text:
This is the one that makes people go "wait, how?". A song can reach out of the game: shake the whole window on a miss, make it jump on the drop, shrink it, take its border away. It can play on the desktop - the world disappears, your wallpaper shows through, and only the fighters, the arrows and the HUD are left floating over it. And it can put pieces of the game into pop-out windows of their own: borderless, see-through and always on top, anywhere on the screen.

A song with a three-line song script (below): window.transparent = true, and the player keeps playing like always.

Only on the player's own screen, only while the song plays

Nobody else sees any of it. On pause, at the end of the song and when it's closed, everything goes back to where it was - nobody's desktop is left in a mess. And a player who doesn't want any of this can switch it off under Options › MineFunkin › Window & desktop › Let songs use windows: then nothing on this page does anything, and everything stays in the game window. That page also tells you what works on your system.

docs.title: Three things to know first
docs.text:
There are three different things going on, and it helps to keep them apart:

  • The game window is Minecraft's own window. window.x, window.width, window.border, ... move and change it. Every value starts at "as it was when the song started", so window.x = 20 means "20 pixels to the right of where it was".
  • The song on the desktop is still that one game window - only the world in it turns see-through (window.transparent, Windows). The keys, Esc and the pause work as always.
  • A pop-out is an extra window that shows the parts of the game you name: popout[0].show = "strums". There are eight of them, popout[0] to popout[7]. A part shown in a pop-out is taken out of the game window, so it isn't there twice.

docs.title: The song on the desktop
docs.text:
format 1.1

event { name = "Desktop Mode" }

function onStart()
    window.transparent = true   -- the world goes, the desktop shows through
    window.fill = "desktop"     -- over the desktop above the taskbar (without it: the whole monitor)
    underlay.alpha = 0          -- bare arrows, no dark strip behind the lanes
end

Yes, that's the entire script behind the picture at the top. From the song's start, the world disappears and your desktop shows through the game window. Everything the song draws stays, right where it was: the fighters (in a fight - in practice, the puppets next to the lanes), the lanes, the HUD, the judgments, your scripts' texts and pictures. Meanwhile the window quietly covers the monitor without a frame - it's never real full screen.

What happens when ...

Keys, Esc As always - it's the game window. A click on the desktop (or Alt+Tab) The click goes through to the desktop and the game loses the keyboard: in practice and against the dummy the song pauses; against a player it goes on (nobody wants a pause request on every click) - click back into the song to play on. Pause The pause screen covers the whole monitor. Resume, and the desktop is back. End of the song The window goes home.

A few things worth knowing:

  • Whatever the song draws shows - over the desktop it's simply solid: the strip behind the lanes (underlay.alpha = 0 takes it away), a flash, the screen colours, the vignette. The cinematic bars of a fight are left out.
  • Effects on the "screen" target change only what's drawn, the desktop stays clear. "world" and "terrain" effects have no world to change.
  • Only on Windows. Elsewhere nothing changes (the world stays) and the event log says so once. Replays keep their arena.
  • How does it work? Windows can let one colour shine through a window (#131313, almost black). MineFunkin paints exactly the desktop part in that colour. Anything else that happens to be that exact colour (say, a dark skin in the light) gets nudged one invisible step off it, so nothing of the song can turn into a hole.

docs.title: Your first pop-out
docs.text:
format 1.1

event { name = "Lanes Out" }

function onEvent(p)
    popout[0].show = "strums"                      -- your four lanes get a window of their own
    tween(popout[0].x, 400, beats(2), "sineInOut") -- ... and it slides 400 pixels to the right
    after(beats(8), function()
        resetWindow(beats(1))                      -- flies home and closes
    end)
end

The pop-out opens exactly on top of where its parts were in the game window, at the same size - so at first, nothing seems to happen. Then it slides out: past the edge of the game window, onto the desktop, with the notes still coming. Then resetWindow(beats(1)) glides it home and closes it, and the lanes seem to fly back in. It looks like magic, and it's eight lines.

docs.title: What a pop-out can show
docs.text:
popout[n].show is a list of parts, separated by spaces, commas or +: "left right", "player, judgments", "score+health". "" closes the pop-out.

Part strums Your four lanes: receptors, notes, holds. left, down, up, right One of your lanes (lane0 ... lane3 work too). opponentStrums The opponent's receptor row (practice). player, opponent A fighter (see Fighters in a pop-out). judgments The "Sick!" popup, the ms label and the combo. score, title, health The score line, the song title, the hearts. hud is all three. text0 ... text7, image0 ... image31 One of the scripts' texts and pictures.

One pop-out can show several parts - it's then as big as all of them together ("left right" spans all four lanes). Everything about a part keeps working inside its pop-out: lane offsets, colours and scroll directions, a fighter's skin and pose, the judgments' size. The lanes and the HUD even zoom, bump, bounce and shake exactly like in the game window, so a pop-out sitting at home matches the game pixel for pixel.

Typo in a part (popout[0].show = "lefft")? That's an error when the file loads, with a friendly "did you mean left?".

docs.title: Moving and sizing a pop-out
docs.text:
A pop-out is placed and sized by popout[n].x, .y, .width, .height, .zoom, .cropX, .cropY, .alpha and .keep - each with its default and range on the popout page.

Putting a pop-out at a fixed spot on the screen. x and y are offsets from home, so to put a pop-out's middle at a certain spot of the monitor, subtract its home:

-- The middle of popout[0] 150 pixels from the monitor's top left corner.
popout[0].x = monitor.x + 150 - popout[0].homeX
popout[0].y = monitor.y + 150 - popout[0].homeY

monitor.x, monitor.y, monitor.width and monitor.height are the monitor the game is on, in pixels (read only).

A cut-out. A small width / height shows only part of what the pop-out would show; cropX / cropY move the view inside it, and zoom enlarges it. That's how you get a facecam:

-- The opponent's head as a small window in the top left corner of the screen.
popout[0].show = "opponent"
popout[0].keep = true           -- it stays in the world too
popout[0].width = 190
popout[0].height = 150
popout[0].zoom = 1.8
popout[0].cropY = -85           -- look further up: at the head

-- in onFrame, so it stays there:
popout[0].x = monitor.x + 130 - popout[0].homeX
popout[0].y = monitor.y + 110 - popout[0].homeY

The right cropY depends on the zoom and on how big the game window is (a bigger window draws the fighter bigger). Try it with the window size your players will likely have, and check that the head stays in the frame.

docs.title: Fighters in a pop-out
docs.text:
In a fight (at a Speaker), player and opponent are the actual fighters from the world: the 3D model with its armour, skin and pose, every player.* effect included - cut out of the world and drawn into the pop-out on a see-through background. While it's popped out, it's gone from the world (unless you set keep).

popout[n].view "full" (default) The whole fighter, legs and feet too, as the fight camera sees it. "camera" Exactly what the screen shows of it. Your own fighter stands right in front of the camera, so it's cut off at the bottom edge - put that edge on the taskbar and it seems to stand on it.

In practice (the Retro TV) and in replays there's no world, so player and opponent are the puppets next to the lanes.

docs.title: The game window
docs.text:
The window itself: window.x, .y, .width, .height, .fullscreen, .border, .alpha, .title, .fill - and read-only answers like window.status, window.canPlace - all on the window page.

-- The window shakes on every miss.
function onMiss(n)
    window.x = 14
    tween(window.x, 0, beats(0.5), "elasticOut")
end

-- The window jumps on the drop and the title changes.
function onEvent(p)
    window.title = "DROP!"
    window.y = -60
    tween(window.y, 0, beats(1), "bounceOut")
end

Some safety rails, so a song can't make the game unusable: the window never leaves the monitor completely (at least 64 pixels stay on it, and the title bar stays reachable), full screen flips at most once a second, and the size changes at most 30 times a second. Every size change rebuilds the game's picture, so don't tween width / height every frame for long.

docs.title: Putting it back: resetWindow
docs.text:
resetWindow()            -- the game window back, every pop-out closed - at once
resetWindow(beats(2))    -- the window and the pop-outs glide home first, then the pop-outs close

A pop-out at home sits exactly over its parts' place, so with a duration they seem to fly back into the game. The song's end, a pause and closing the song all do this by themselves too.

docs.title: Where it works
docs.text:
Not every system lets a program do all of this:

Windows Everything. macOS Everything but window.transparent (the world stays). Linux with X11 Everything but window.transparent. A pop-out's see-through background needs a compositor (most desktops have one); without one it has a black background. Linux with Wayland No program may place its own windows there: the pop-outs stay off (popout[n].open is false) and window.x / window.y / window.alpha do nothing. Size, full screen and the title work; window.transparent doesn't.

The event log says once when something isn't possible on this computer. A script can also check popout[n].open and do something else instead.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Clicks go through a pop-out to whatever is under it, and the keyboard stays with the game window. For a whole song on the desktop, use window.transparent - one window, nothing to keep in step.
  • With a shader pack (Iris), a fighter in a pop-out is drawn with Minecraft's own look, not the pack's - the pack only draws the world.
  • Each pop-out costs about as much as drawing its parts once more. A fighter in a pop-out is drawn once, into its pop-out instead of the world (twice with keep).
  • At most eight pop-outs, each at most 4096 pixels a side.
  • If your players stream or record: a pop-out is a real window, so capturing only the game window misses it - a display capture gets it. A window capture of a song on the desktop shows the see-through part in the key colour (almost black).

docs.title: Built-in events
docs.text:
These 21 come with MineFunkin, so every song can use them without bringing a single file. They're written in the same language as yours - nothing special about them. Which means: if you don't like how one works, put a file with the same name in your song's folder, and your song uses yours instead.

Event Category Parameters (value1 / value2) Add Camera Zoom Camera stage zoom (Psych's camGame - not used) / HUD zoom (default 0.03; the pops add up to 1.35 at most) Beat Bump Camera custom bop on / every N beats, zoom Screen Shake Camera duration (s), intensity / - Set Camera Zoom Camera zoom / ease over (beats) Countdown HUD - Hide HUD (alias Goodbye Hud) HUD opacity / duration (s) HUD Bounce HUD on / intensity, OFF = puppets stay still Move Playfield HUD right px, down px / over (beats) Note Scramble (alias Missingno) Notes ease rate / - Note Scramble Reset Notes - Note Wobble Notes on/off, unified/offset / speed, size (px) Strum Fade Notes opacity / over (beats) Lane Position ALL (alias LaneOrientationAll) Scroll down/up / - Lane Position Single (alias LaneOrientationSingle) Scroll lane / down/up/toggle Scroll Speed (aliases Change Scroll Speed, Change Scrollspeed) Scroll speed / duration (s), flags classic, modern, multiplier Miss Flash Screen on / strength Show Image Screen picture (.png) / show for (s), width, flag back Vignette Screen strength / colour, fade (beats) White Flash Screen duration (s) / colour White Screen Screen on / colour, fade (s) Lyrics Text text / show for (beats), colour

The chart editor shows their names, descriptions and settings in the player's language (German too); charts and scripts always use the English names above.

The built-in files are good starting points for your own. They are in the mod JAR under assets/minefunkin/events/. Copy one into a song folder (it replaces the built-in for that song) and change it there. For example, HUD Bounce:

format 1.1

event {
    name = "HUD Bounce",
    color = #7C6BFF,
    category = "HUD",
    description = "Rocks the HUD on every beat (in fights the camera rolls with it). Off stops it.",
}

params {
    bouncing  = switch { from = "value1", label = "On" },
    intensity = number { from = "value2.1", default = 1, min = 0, max = 5, step = 0.05, label = "Intensity" },
    still     = flag   { from = "value2", word = "OFF", label = "Keep puppets still" },
}

local active = false
local strength = 1
local lastBeat = nil

function onEvent(p)
    active = p.bouncing
    strength = p.intensity
    hud.extras = not p.still
end

-- Checked every frame, so it bounces at once when switched on.
function onFrame(dt)
    if not active or beat == lastBeat then return end
    lastBeat = beat

    local even = beat % 2 == 0
    hud.angle = (even ? 2.5 : -2.5) * strength
    tween(hud.angle, 0, beats(0.92), "backOut")
    camera.bump += (even ? 0.0195 : 0.0065) * strength
end

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text: The questions people actually ask. If yours isn't here, errors and fixes probably has it.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
Where do my event files go?

In the song's folder (next to its .mfkn chart), or in an events/ folder inside it. Songs live in .minecraft/MineFunkin/client/songs/<song>/. Nothing else is read - an event file in another song's folder isn't offered for this one. See where event files live.

Do I need to know how to code?

Nope. Lots of great events are three lines long. Start with the shortcuts: flash(), zoom(1.2), hideHud(), flipScroll() - one line each. Your first event takes you from an empty file to a real event, one small step at a time, and the templates are working files you can just copy.

I have older songs or event files (format 1.0) - what now?

Format 1.0 is from MineFunkin's development builds before the first release. MineFunkin only plays format 1.1, but updating is one click. Old songs have a yellow ⚠ in the song list: select one and press Update all old songs (or ⋯ › Update old songs), and every one of them is converted at once. Nothing gets lost - the originals go into each song's backup/ folder. New files always start with format 1.1. More on old songs.

How do I test an event quickly?

Open the song in the chart editor (Retro TV → Editor), place the event, press Space. When you change the file, press Reload at the bottom of the inspector - no restarting needed. For anything to do with the world (the fight camera, the fighters, the stage behind them), start a fight against the dummy at a Speaker. The dummy never gets tired of testing with you.

docs.title: When it doesn't work
docs.text:
My event isn't in the editor's list.

Look at the editor's footer: ⚠ N opens the list of files that can't be used, each with its line and why. Nine times out of ten it's a typo (the message says "did you mean ...?"), a missing format 1.1 line, or code outside a function. Fix it, press Reload, done. Errors and fixes explains every message.

My event is in the chart but nothing happens.
  • Is the event's name in the chart the same as name = ... in the file (case doesn't matter)?
  • Does it need a fight? The fight camera, focus, swapFighters, the "stage" layer, outlines and health only exist in a fight at a Speaker - in practice at the Retro TV they do nothing.
  • Does its header say only = "fight" or only = "practice"? Then it runs only there.
  • Put a log("here") into onEvent and look at logs/minefunkin-events.log: every chart event is written there as it fires, with its values, and so are script errors.
Two effects cancel each other out.

A property holds just one value, so two scripts setting the same one every frame overwrite each other (the event log names both). Give each effect its own property - x for one, wobbleX for the other - and they'll get along. See channels.

My picture shows up a moment too late.

Pictures load the first time they're drawn, which can take a few frames. preload them in onStart, and they load during the countdown instead.

A script stopped working halfway through the song.

A script that crashes while running (a lane that doesn't exist, text where a number is needed) is switched off for the rest of the run, so the song can go on. The event log tells you which line. Fix it and restart the song.

docs.title: Fights and other players
docs.text:
Do other players see my effects?

Every player runs the song's scripts in their own game, so in a player fight both fighters see the effects on their own screen - a server's songs bring their event files along. Players standing around the fight see none of it from outside. But they can watch from inside (right-click the Speaker), and then they see everything, three seconds behind. The one thing that's sent along is the song's own poses (setPose): the players around see the fighters strike them.

Can a modchart make the song harder to score?

Harder to read, yes - harder to score, no. Judging goes by time, not by where a note is drawn. A note that a script moved, turned or faded is hit and judged exactly like any other.

Do scripts run in replays?

Yes - a replay plays the song's events just like the run did. Only the see-through game window is left out, since a replay plays in its own little arena.

docs.title: Coming from Psych or Kade
docs.text:
Can I use my Psych Engine Lua files?

Not as they are - .event is MineFunkin's own language. But most lines translate one to one, and Coming from Psych Engine goes through Psych's whole API with you. A Psych chart's events keep their values when the chart is converted, so you only rewrite the scripts, not the chart.

And Kade Engine modcharts?

Same idea: Coming from Kade Engine maps every hook, function and variable, and translates Kade's example modcharts.

Can I use my Psych shaders (.frag)?

Yes, as they are: put the .frag in the song folder, set shader[0].file = "name.frag" and its values with setShaderFloat. See shaders from Psych.

My shader runs in my own song, but not on a server.

By default, songs from a server have to pass MineFunkin's shader check - your own songs don't. shader[n].status says "refused", and the event log says why. Usually it's a while loop, or a loop without a fixed number of rounds.

Can I use Psych sprites (a .png with an .xml)?

Yes: put both in the song folder and set image[n].anim to the animation's name. See Psych sprites.

docs.title: Safety
docs.text:
Can a downloaded song harm my game or computer?

No - and that was a big deal when the language was designed. A script can only use what this wiki lists: it can't read or write files, reach the internet, change your settings or other songs, or run other code. It gets the pictures, sounds and shaders of its own song folder and nothing else, and hard limits stop it from doing too much work. Shaders from a server are checked before they run (Options › MineFunkin › Song effects).

Some players have flashing or motion turned down.

Options › MineFunkin › Accessibility has Fewer flashes (flashes kept faint, fx.invert / fx.glitch at 0.3 and fx.brightness at 1.3 at most) and Less motion (no camera bump, shake or hit nudge). Your song still plays for them, just a bit calmer. So don't build a moment that only works with a full-screen flash.

Can I switch events off?

The built-in ones, yes: Options › MineFunkin › Song effects › Built-in events. A song's own files belong to the song, though, so those always run.

docs.title: Limits, the event log and versions
Limits and safety
docs.text:
Why limits at all? Because you'll download songs from people you don't know, and a song should never be able to freeze your game - by accident or on purpose. The limits are generous; a normal song never gets near them. If yours does, the event log tells you which one.

  • One call into the scripts (an event, a frame, a hit) may run at most 50,000 statements.
  • A for loop may run at most 10,000 rounds. Functions may call each other at most 64 deep.
  • At most 512 afters and everys may wait at once. An every runs at most once a frame.
  • trigger: events may trigger each other at most 8 deep.
  • A script that fails while running is switched off for the rest of the run, and the failure is logged with its line. Examples: a lane that doesn't exist, text where a number is needed, a choice property set to a word it doesn't take.
  • Writing a non-number (a division by zero) to a number property is ignored.
  • Opacities and volumes go from 0 to 1 (hud.bars 0-3, camera.nudge 0-5). A constant outside that is an error when the file loads; a value worked out while the song runs is kept inside, and the log says so once.
  • log: at most 200 lines per event per run.
  • Texts: at most 16,384 characters. Making a longer one - joining with .. / + / +=, upper, lower, replace - switches that script off (it isn't cut short).
  • Top-level locals get their starting values when the song starts, so they can read the game (local w = screen.width). One that fails there switches its script off.
  • Pictures: .png, at most 8192 pixels a side and 16 MB as a file, at most 128 different pictures and 512 MB of video memory per song. They are freed when the song closes. A sprite's .xml: at most 2 MB and 4096 frames. A video folder: at most 20,000 frames (.jpg / .png), 2048 pixels a side, 8 MB a frame.
  • Shaders: .fsh or .frag, at most 32 KB a file, at most four at once. Which run is the player's choice (the shader check); one that takes over 25 ms a frame is switched off.
  • Skins (setSkin, player.skin): 64x64 .png, at most 1 MB each and 8 per song.
  • Windows: at most eight pop-outs, each at most 4096 pixels a side. The game window keeps 64 pixels on its monitor, at least 0.2 opacity, one full-screen flip a second. All of it only while the song plays, and only if the player allows it (Options › MineFunkin › Window & desktop › "Let songs use windows").
  • Sounds: .ogg, at most 5 minutes each (longer ones aren't played - the log says so), at most 32 of a song's own sounds playing at once (one more is left out, said once). Each is decoded once per song and let go when it closes.
  • Modifiers: at most 200,000 planned changes per song (one per field each ease / set / add touches; past that they're left out, said once), 8 playfields (yours, the opponent's, 6 from copyField), 256 modifiers of your own (customMod). A value is kept within ±10,000,000; one ease lasts at most 100,000 beats.
  • Sounds, pictures and shaders are only found inside the song's own folder (and its events/ folder, or shaders/ for shaders). A path that leads out of it is refused.

Error messages and what to do about them: Errors and fixes.

docs.title: The event log
docs.text:
logs/minefunkin-events.log, next to latest.log, collects everything that happens with events. It starts fresh every time the game starts; the one before is kept as minefunkin-events.prev.log. It writes down:

  • the built-in events, and per song the event files it brings (and which built-in each replaces);
  • every file that can't be used, with the reason (also listed in the chart editor);
  • every song start (mode, chart event count), chart events no file defines, and events switched off in the options;
  • every chart event as it fires, with its values;
  • script errors, missing sounds, pictures or shaders, shaders that don't compile (with the driver's message), and the scripts' own log lines.

Warnings and errors also go to latest.log. Past 8 MB the file only takes warnings and errors.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text:
The first line of every file says which version of the language it's written in. MineFunkin runs only format 1.1 - one version, so you never have to wonder which features you can use:

Version format 1.1 The one that runs - write every file like this. format 1.0 The version of MineFunkin's development builds before the first release. It doesn't run anymore: Song Select's update button turns a song's 1.0 files into 1.1 in one go - see old songs. anything else A version newer than this MineFunkin. Not run; it's listed as a problem: "written for event format 1.2, this MineFunkin runs 1.1 - a newer MineFunkin is needed".

That's why the first release already starts at 1.1: version 1.0 was only used while MineFunkin was still in development. You'll only meet it in songs made with those early builds.

Some names came to 1.1 after its first files were written: note, notes, every, cancel, stopTween, loopSound, trigger, call, callIn, preload, setHealth, addHealth, stopSound, soundVolume, randomInt, sub, find, replace, trim, startsWith, endsWith, noteSlot, boyfriend, dad, bind, unbind, inspect, atPlace. They stay yours if a file already uses them for its own things: a variable or parameter of that name (function onHit(note)) hides the built-in one inside it, and a function of the file's own (local function preload(...)) is called instead of the built-in.

docs.title: Old songs and the update button
docs.text:
Just so you know

You most likely won't need this. Every released MineFunkin uses format 1.1, and only songs made with the development builds before the first release are in an older format. This section is here so you know how it works if a later MineFunkin ever moves on from 1.1 - old songs will then be updated the same way.

A song with any file in an old format - an event file in format 1.0, or a chart or song file in the old song format 1 - shows up in Song Select with a yellow ⚠, and can't be played yet. Don't worry, fixing it is one click: select it and press Update all old songs (or ⋯ › Update old songs), and every such song is converted at once:

  • Charts and song files are written in format 1.1. The notes, events, BPM changes and audio links stay exactly as they were.
  • Event files get format 1.1 as their first line, and nothing else changes - with one exception: a name the file used for its own things that 1.1 uses itself (a variable called volume, a function called zoom, a helper called onPause, which 1.1 would start calling by itself) is renamed to myVolume, myZoom, myOnPause, and a comment under the format line lists what was renamed.
  • Every original is copied into the song's backup/ folder first, just in case.

On a server, the admin converts the songs in server_songs/ with /minefunkin convert. The server log says at start when there are old songs.

docs.title: Errors and fixes
docs.text: Something's not working? Don't panic - almost every problem has been hit by someone before, and MineFunkin tries hard to tell you exactly what's wrong. This page helps you read what it says.

docs.title: Nothing happens
docs.text:
The most frustrating kind of bug: no error, just ... nothing. Work down this list, one by one - the answer is usually in the first four:

  1. Is the file where the song is? In the song's folder or its events/ folder. Files of other songs are never read.
  2. Does the editor list it? Open the song in the chart editor. If the file is listed under can't be used at the bottom of the inspector, the reason is right there (see below).
  3. Does the chart call it by its name? The chart event's type must be the file's event { name } or one of its aliases (case doesn't matter). The log lists chart events no file defines.
  4. Is it a fight thing? The camera, the fighters and "world" / "terrain" effects only exist in a fight (at a Speaker). In practice they do nothing.
  5. Is it a window thing? Pop-outs and the game window do nothing when the player switched off Let songs use windows in the options, pop-outs can't open on Linux with Wayland, and window.transparent works on Windows only.
  6. Is it switched off? Players can switch off built-in events under Options › MineFunkin › Song effects.
  7. Did it fail while running? A script that runs into an error is switched off for the rest of the run. The log says where.
  8. Does another script overwrite it? Two scripts setting the same property every frame: only the last one shows. The log names both.
  9. Paused or counting down? Nothing runs then.

docs.title: The event log
docs.text:
Your best friend when debugging. logs/minefunkin-events.log, right next to Minecraft's latest.log, has everything that happens with events. It starts fresh every time the game starts; the one before is kept as minefunkin-events.prev.log.

[18:21:04] [INFO] Built-in events (21): Add Camera Zoom, Beat Bump, Countdown, ...
[18:21:09] [INFO] Song "showcase": 31 event files of its own: "Build Up" (events/build_up.event), ...
[18:21:09] [WARN] Song "fxtest": fxtest.event can't be used - line 5:17: 'beat' is a reserved word - pick another name
[18:21:12] [INFO] Song started: "Event Showcase" [Normal] (fight) - 101 chart events
[18:21:13] [INFO]     0.000s  Power On  [EVENT SHOWCASE] [every effect is a .event file in this song's folder]
[18:21:38] [INFO] Shader "ripple.fsh" loaded
[18:21:40] [INFO] Beat Flash on in #FFE35C

It writes down the built-ins and each song's own files, every file that can't be used, every song start, every chart event as it fires (with its values), chart events no file answers to, script errors, missing sounds, pictures and shaders, and your own log(...) lines. Warnings and errors also go into latest.log. Once the file passes 8 MB it only takes warnings and errors, so it can't fill your disk.

docs.title: When a file can't be used
docs.text:
A file with a mistake in it never runs at all - better than half-running and doing weird things. The message gives you the line and column (line 5:17) and says what's wrong, often with a guess at what you meant. The most common ones:

Message What to do 'beat' is a reserved word - pick another name That name is taken (see the list below). Rename your variable or parameter: function onBeat(n) instead of onBeat(beat). unknown name 'x' - declare it first with local Every variable needs a local (or shared) first. There are no globals. Also check the spelling. unknown property strums.alhpa - did you mean alpha? A typo, or a property that doesn't exist. The message suggests the closest names. unknown function flipscroll() - did you mean flipScroll?
