Names are case-sensitive: flipScroll, not flipscroll. strums.alpha goes from 0 to 1, not 5 A constant outside what the property takes (opacities and volumes 0-1, hud.bars 0-3, camera.nudge 0-5). text[i].layer takes "back", "lanes", "front", "top" - not "middle" A word a property or shortcut doesn't take (often with a "did you mean ...?"), or a lane that doesn't exist. flipScroll is called like this: flipScroll() or flipScroll(lane) A shortcut with too many or too few values. the file never names its event - add: event { name = "My Event" } Every file needs event { name = "..." }, even a song script. the top of the file holds event { }, params { }, local / shared variables and functions Code outside a function. Move it into onStart, onEvent or another callback. functions are defined at the top of the file, not inside another function Define helpers at the top level, call them from inside. Inside a function, use function() ... end only as an after callback. the file ends inside a block - an 'end' is missing An if, for or function without its end. expected ... A syntax slip: a missing then / do, a bracket, a comma between parameters. only number and colour properties can be animated tween on text or a switch. Set those directly. note[i] goes back every frame - set it in onFrame instead of tweening it note[i] is a different note from frame to frame. Work its values out in onFrame (see notes one by one). 'note' is your own variable here, so note[i] isn't reachable A parameter or variable called note (function onHit(note)) hides the list of notes. Rename yours: function onHit(n). loopSound needs a name to stop it by loopSound("rain.ogg", 0.5, "rain") - a loop has to be stoppable. every is called like this: every(time, function() ... end[, times][, "name"]) Too many values, or the count after the name. unknown easing "bounce" See the list of easings. 'break' only works inside a for loop written for event format 1.0 - MineFunkin only runs 1.1 now; Song Select's update button converts it An old file. Press Update old songs in Song Select - it converts the whole song, the originals go into its backup/ folder (more). written for event format 2.0, this MineFunkin runs 1.1 - a newer MineFunkin is needed The file is for a newer MineFunkin.

docs.title: Taken names
docs.text:
These names already mean something, so you can't use them for your own variables, parameters or functions:

  • Words of the language: and, break, do, else, elseif, end, false, for, function, if, in, local, nil, not, or, return, then, true, while, repeat, until, goto, shared, format, event, params
  • Built-in values: time, beat, step, bpm, pi
  • Property groups: camera, hud, screen, flash, vignette, strum, strums, scroll, underlay, player, opponent, puppet, song, text, image, fx, shader, judgments, volume, window, popout, monitor, note, notes
  • The shortcuts: flash, zoom, shake, focus, pose, ...
  • Every function and action: sin, snap, random, tween, after, log, ...

Not taken: the names that came later - note, notes, every, cancel, stopTween, loopSound, trigger, call, callIn, preload, setHealth, addHealth, stopSound, soundVolume, randomInt, sub, find, replace, trim, startsWith, endsWith, noteSlot, boyfriend, dad, bind, unbind, inspect, atPlace. A variable, parameter or function of yours with one of these names wins inside your file (see Versions).

step, time and snap are the ones everybody trips over at least once: call yours n, dur or moveTime instead.

docs.title: Errors while it runs
docs.text:
These happen while the song plays. They switch that one script off for the rest of the run (the song itself goes on), and land in the log with their line:

Message Cause there's no fighter 2 - fighters are 0 (you) and 1 (the opponent) puppet[2]: only 0 and 1 exist. a lane that doesn't exist strum[4]: lanes are 0-3. text where a number is needed e.g. hud.angle = "big". a choice property set to a word it doesn't take e.g. text[0].layer = "middle". too much work in one go (more than 50000 steps) More than 50,000 statements in one call - usually a loop that's far too big. this loop runs more than 10000 times A for loop with more than 10,000 rounds. functions call each other more than 64 deep A function that calls itself without stopping. too many 'after's waiting (more than 512) Usually an after (or every) scheduled every frame. there's no note 130 note[i] past what's listed: loop up to notes.count - 1. events trigger each other more than 8 deep Two events that trigger each other in a circle. the event has no parameter 'x' p.x for a parameter the event doesn't declare.

Writing something that isn't a number (say, a division by zero) into a number property is quietly ignored.

docs.title: Warnings in the log
docs.text:
These don't stop anything - the log just mentions them once, so you know:

Warning Meaning a value kept inside its range A number worked out while the song runs was outside what the property takes (strums.alpha = 1.4) and was set to the nearest allowed value. two scripts set the same property every frame Both write it in onFrame, so only the last one shows. Give each its own property (x and wobbleX) or its own part of the song. a picture, sound or shader that isn't found Check the file name and that it's in the song's folder. trigger - there's no event "X" in this song A trigger("X") for an event the song doesn't have - a typo (the warning says what was probably meant) or a song file that's missing. Nothing happens, the script goes on. a pop-out or window change that isn't possible here "Let songs use windows" switched off, Wayland, no compositor for see-through windows, or window.transparent on a system other than Windows.

docs.title: Shaders
docs.text:
A .fsh that doesn't compile is switched off, and the graphics driver's message goes to the log:

[ERROR] Shader "broken.fsh" doesn't compile (lines count from the file's first line):
0:2(21): error: `undefinedThing' undeclared

0:2 = line 2 of your file. Shader files are read once per song, so restart the song after a fix. A shader file that isn't found is reported too. More in Your own shaders.

shader[n].status tells a script what became of the file. The ones that need you:

Status Why What to do "refused" The shader check said no - the log names the line. Loop with for over a fixed number of rounds; no while, no out / inout. "broken" It doesn't compile. The driver's message is in the log, as above. "too heavy" It took over 25 ms a frame and was switched off for the song. Fewer picture reads, smaller loops. "disabled" The player switched song shaders off. Nothing - make the song work without. "fight only" Target "world" / "terrain" outside a fight. Use "screen" for practice.

docs.title: Find out what your script is doing
docs.text:
When in doubt, ask it. log takes any values and writes them in one line:

function onHit(note)
    log("hit", note.lane, note.judgment, note.offset, "combo", player.combo)
end

Each event writes at most 200 log lines per run, so even a log in onFrame won't flood the file. And when you want to know who set a property and why, inspect tells you.

docs.title: Songs
docs.text:
A MineFunkin song is simply a folder. Inside: the audio, one .mfknsong file that describes the song, one .mfkn chart per difficulty, and - if it has any - its own event scripts. That's the whole song. Zip the folder, send it to a friend, and they have everything they need.

my-song/
  my-song.mfknsong          the song: title, artist, audio, difficulties
  my-song-normal.mfkn       a chart: the notes and the chart events of one difficulty
  my-song-hard.mfkn
  Inst.ogg                  the instrumental
  Voices-Player.ogg         your vocals (a miss mutes them)
  Voices-Opponent.ogg       the opponent's vocals
  events/                   the song's own .event scripts (optional)

docs.title: Where songs go
docs.text: Where .minecraft/MineFunkin/client/songs/ Your own songs: practice at the Retro TV, the chart editor, fights against the dummy. <server>/MineFunkin/server/server_songs/ A server's songs. Players get them automatically when they join; fights between players, the leaderboard and the replays use them.

docs.title: Getting a song in
docs.text:
Three ways, from easiest to most hands-on:

  • Import: in the song list, open the ⋯ menu at the top, pick Import songs… and choose the song's folder - or just drag the folder onto the game window. This works at the Retro TV, and at a Speaker wherever your own songs play (in your own world). MineFunkin reads it and shows you what it found: the difficulties, the music, and a line for any difficulty that's missing its music. Title, artist and charter come from the song's own files. Change files… lets you pick other audio files; Enter imports. This works for MineFunkin songs and for Psych Engine and V-Slice songs (a .json chart and the .ogg files) - those get converted to .mfkn and .mfknsong on the way in. Psych chart events are kept; V-Slice's are left out (they'd look broken here).
  • By hand: a MineFunkin song (a folder with a .mfknsong) can simply go into the songs folder. A song from another engine that you put there by hand shows up with a ⚠ and a Convert… button.
  • Your own song, from scratch: the editor's song list → + New Chart, give it a name, drop the audio into the new folder, and the chart editor opens. Time to chart!

On Linux the folder picker needs zenity or kdialog (most desktops have one). Without either, just drag the folder in instead.

docs.title: On this tab
docs.text:
• Song files

    What's in a .mfknsong and a .mfkn - small JSON files you can fix by hand in any text editor.

    Song files

docs.title: Song files (format 1.1)
docs.text:
You'll rarely need to open these - the chart editor writes them for you. But when you do, they're friendly: both are plain JSON, kept small on purpose, with one note or event per line. Spotted a wrong note? Fix it in any text editor, no tools needed.

MineFunkin only plays format 1.1. Format 1 was used by MineFunkin's development builds before the first release - a song from back then needs one click to convert (see below).

docs.title: The song file (.mfknsong)
docs.text:
{
  "format": "1.1",
  "title": "Bopeebo",
  "artist": "Kawai Sprite",
  "charter": "NotFoxxz",
  "speed": 1.0,
  "character": "Boyfriend",
  "audio": {
    "inst": "Inst.ogg",
    "player": "Voices-Player.ogg",
    "opponent": "Voices-Opponent.ogg"
  },
  "difficulties": {
    "Normal": "my-song-normal.mfkn",
    "Hard": "my-song-hard.mfkn"
  }
}
Key format required "1.1" title The name in the song list. Default: the file's name. artist, charter optional Who made the music, who made the chart. speed optional The chart's scroll speed (1 = the player's own). Default 1. character The playable character of every difficulty, unless a difficulty names its own. Default "Boyfriend". audio The song's audio files, see below. difficulties required Label to chart file, in the order the song list shows them.

docs.title: Audio
docs.text:
Key inst The instrumental. player Your vocals: one file or a list of files. A miss mutes them. opponent The opponent's vocals: one file or a list. voices A vocal track with both singers in it. When it's the only one, a miss mutes it.

Every file is a name in the song's folder. A song without vocals just leaves player, opponent and voices out.

docs.title: A difficulty that's different
docs.text:
Most difficulties are just the name of their chart file. One that has its own character or its own audio becomes an object instead:

"difficulties": {
  "Normal": "my-song-normal.mfkn",
  "Erect": {
    "chart": "my-song-erect.mfkn",
    "audio": { "inst": "Inst-erect.ogg", "player": "Voices-Player-erect.ogg" }
  },
  "Normal (Pico)": {
    "label": "Normal",
    "chart": "my-song-pico.mfkn",
    "character": "Pico",
    "audio": { "inst": "Inst-pico.ogg", "player": "Voices-Pico.ogg" }
  }
}
Key chart The .mfkn file. label The name shown in the song list, when it isn't the key. Two characters can each have a "Normal": the keys have to differ, the labels don't. character This difficulty's playable character. audio Only the audio keys that differ from the song's audio - the rest is taken from there. start Practice starts the song here (ms, like the chart's times). Everything before it runs through silently first - chart events, scripts, shaders and texts stand where they would - then the music starts at that point. Notes before it aren't played or counted. Fights and replays always play the whole song.

Want a practice version of just the hard last part of a long song? Make a second difficulty with the same chart and a start:

"difficulties": {
  "Hard": "hard.mfkn",
  "Hard (last part)": { "chart": "hard.mfkn", "start": 367414.6 }
}

Scores and replays belong to song + character + difficulty label. So renaming a file is safe - but renaming a label starts its scores over.

docs.title: The chart file (.mfkn)
docs.text:
{
  "format": "1.1",
  "bpm": 140,
  "player": [
    [3428.6, 0, 797],
    [10285.7, 2],
    [10500, 2],
    [12857.1, 3, 0, "miss"]
  ],
  "opponent": [
    [1714.3, 0, 369]
  ],
  "events": [
    [0, "Power On", "EVENT SHOWCASE", "every effect is a .event file in this song's folder"],
    [3428.6, "Cam Sway", "on", "6"]
  ]
}

All times are milliseconds from the start of the song.

Key format "1.1" bpm The tempo: one number, or a list of changes [[0, 140], [32000, 170]] (time, BPM). player Your notes. opponent The opponent's notes. events The chart events.

A note is [time, lane, hold, type]:

time When it's hit. lane 0 = left, 1 = down, 2 = up, 3 = right. hold How long it's held, in ms. Leave it out (or 0) for a tap. type Optional. "miss" = a Forced-Miss Note: hitting it counts as a miss, letting it pass costs nothing. A type this version doesn't know skips the note.

An event is [time, name, value1, value2]. The name is the event's name (a built-in one or a .event file's); the two values are what its parameters read. Leave out values that are empty.

The order of the lines doesn't matter - notes and events are sorted when the chart loads, and an exact duplicate note (same lane, same time) is dropped. Times are written with up to three decimals.

docs.title: Format 1 (older songs)
docs.text:
Format 1 is the song format of MineFunkin's development builds before the first release. It wrote every note as an object ({"time": 3428.6, "lane": 0, "hold": 797.0, "forcedMiss": false}), the BPM as bpmChanges and the audio once per difficulty with voices + playerVocalIds / opponentVocalIds. MineFunkin doesn't play it anymore, but converting is one click: Song Select lists such a song with a yellow ⚠, and its Update all old songs button converts every old song at once - its charts, its song file and its event files (see old songs). Nothing is lost: the notes, events, BPM changes and audio stay as they were, and the originals are copied into the song's backup/ folder first. On a server, the admin runs /minefunkin convert for server_songs/.

A file with a newer format than this MineFunkin knows (1.2, 2.0, ...) isn't read at all - the song is left out of the list and the log says which version it needs.
